About Us
1GLOBAL is a technology-driven global mobile communications provider helping enterprises and consumer brands deliver seamless connectivity worldwide. Powered by a best-in-class telecom platform, proprietary eSIM technology, and its own mobile core network across 15 countries, 1GLOBAL operates as a fully regulated telecommunications provider in 43 countries.
Founded in 2022, 1GLOBAL has rapidly become one of Europe's fastest-growing telecom technology companies, connecting more than 80 million people and devices globally. Our customers include leading banks, multinational enterprises, global retailers, travel companies, payment service providers, and digital-first businesses.
Headquartered in the Netherlands, with R&D hubs in Lisbon, Berlin, and São Paulo, 1GLOBAL employs over 550 professionals across 16 countries. With annual revenues exceeding US$200 million and a strong track record of profitability, we continue to invest in innovation, infrastructure, and international expansion as we redefine the future of global mobile connectivity.
About the Ideal Candidate
We are looking for a talented Senior DevSecOps / Cloud Security Engineer to join our Technology Department, with a focus on strengthening and automating our security posture across cloud and hybrid infrastructure. As a DevSecOps / Cloud Security Engineer, you will be responsible for embedding security into every stage of our infrastructure lifecycle, from design to deployment. You will lead the implementation of cloud-native security controls in AWS, harden Kubernetes environments, and drive best practices across CI/CD pipelines. Your role includes continuous vulnerability management, network protection, monitoring for threats, and working with development, DevOps and IP teams to ensure secure-by-default practices. You’ll also proactively identify risks, secure network perimeters, and automate remediation wherever possible.
This role can be based remotely in Portugal, Germany, Spain, Poland, the Netherlands, Ireland, or the UK.
About the Role
• Design, implement, and evolve scalable cloud security controls across AWS multi-account environments using security-as-code principles • Own Kubernetes security architecture including workload isolation, RBAC, pod security standards, and network segmentation • Embed security automation into CI/CD pipelines, including image scanning, IaC validation, and policy enforcement • Continuously assess cloud and Kubernetes environments for vulnerabilities, misconfigurations, and emerging threats • Design and maintain strong IAM and secrets management practices, enforcing least-privilege access • Partner with DevOps, Platform, and IP/Network teams to deliver security controls as code and by design • Analyze network traffic and security telemetry using flow logs, metrics, and targeted packet inspection where required • Ensure alignment with internal security policies and external frameworks (CIS, NIST, ISO 27001, etc.) • Produce and maintain clear documentation, including security architectures, runbooks, and incident response playbooks • Act as a security champion, driving best practices, awareness, and secure engineering culture across teams
Requirements
About You
• A minimum of 3+ years of experience with Cloud Security / DevSecOps / Infrastructure Security • Strong AWS security fundamentals (IAM, KMS, GuardDuty, Config, Security Hub) • Solid Linux security and cloud networking fundamentals • Hands-on Kubernetes security (RBAC, NetworkPolicies, pod security, image scanning) • Infrastructure as Code (Terraform) and Git-based workflows • Scripting for automation (Python or Go or Bash) • Experience with vulnerability management and container security • Security-first mindset with strong troubleshooting skills • Experience with WAFs and cloud DDoS protection • Comfortable with packet inspection, flow analysis, and traffic monitoring (tcpdump, Wireshark, Suricata, etc.)
Benefits
Why 1GLOBAL?
• Growth Opportunities: Advance your career in one of the fastest growing telecommunications companies, expanding over 50% year-on-year under the leadership of successful tech entrepreneurs. • Major Transaction Exposure: Be in the driver’s seat for transactions that will have an impact on the future telco industry. • Work with a Talented Team: From the Board and the Founders to the Senior Management Team, you will collaborate daily with the most capable and renowned external advisors and constantly being exposed to talented and driven individuals. • Dynamic Work Environment: Thrive in a collaborative, fast-paced workplace where innovation is encouraged, and every contribution counts. • Professional Development: Work alongside industry experts to enhance your skills and knowledge in a cutting-edge field. • International Experience: Gain opportunities to work in different 1GLOBAL offices around the world as you grow within the company. • Open Communication Culture: Join a team where your ideas are heard, and open dialogue is encouraged, fostering a supportive and transparent work environment. • Get Things Done Attitude: Be part of a results-driven team that values efficiency, creativity, and the drive to make a tangible impact in the industry. 1GLOBAL is an equal opportunity employer, we value your character as much as your talent. Diversity drives our innovation, and we offer a collaborative, dynamic, and international work environment. We are excited for you to join our mission to revolutionise connectivity globally.

CAMO Airworthiness Engineer Doncaster
Full-Time, Permanent (Monday to Friday) At 2Excel Aviation, we thrive on solving some of aviation's most complex and demanding challenges. Our success is built on the expertise, dedication, and innovation of our people. As we continue to grow, we are looking for an experienced and motivated CAMO Airworthiness Engineer to join our Continuing Airworthiness Management Organisation (CAMO) team based in Doncaster. Reporting to the Deputy Continuing Airworthiness Manager, this role offers the opportunity to work across a diverse fleet and contribute to the ongoing airworthiness and operational effectiveness of our aircraft. We are particularly interested in candidates with experience within a CAMO environment and detailed knowledge of Turbofan/Turboprop engines or Avionic systems. This position would suit a detail-oriented professional who enjoys collaborating across departments, solving technical challenges, and driving continuous improvement within a dynamic aviation environment. As Airworthiness Engineer, you will: • Review, assess, and process incoming publications, Airworthiness Directives (ADs), Service Bulletins (SBs), and other mandatory and non-mandatory maintenance information. • Support the development, review, and maintenance of Aircraft Maintenance Programmes (AMPs), ensuring alignment between source data, the AMP, and Airworthiness Management software. • Assist with the loading and updating of maintenance programmes, task cards, and aircraft records within the airworthiness database. • Produce and analyse reliability reports, supporting Reliability Programmes and Engine Health Monitoring (EHM) activities. • Support fleet configuration control through modification and/or software status. • Contribute to the development and continual improvement of airworthiness procedures, processes, and documentation. • Support the review, amendment, and implementation of Minimum Equipment Lists (MELs). • Assist with root cause investigations, corrective actions, and the resolution of compliance deficiencies and occurrence findings. • Verify and process design changes following aircraft modifications and repairs. • Maintain audit readiness within your assigned areas of responsibility. • Ensure compliance with company policies, procedures, and regulatory requirements. • Obtain and maintain Security Clearance (SC) and/or Counter Terrorism Check (CTC) clearance as required. To be successful in this role, you will ideally have: • Previous experience working within a CAMO or continuing airworthiness environment. • A strong understanding of aircraft powerplant systems or Avionic systems and associated airworthiness requirements. • Knowledge of CFM56, RB211, and P&WC PT6 engine families (desirable), or; • Knowledge of Avionic systems installed on Boeing 737NG aircraft and/or Garmin G1000/Proline 21 cockpit (desirable). • Strong attention to detail and a commitment to regulatory compliance. • Effective communication skills with the ability to work collaboratively across multiple departments. • A proactive approach and a continuous improvement mindset. Benefits • Competitive salary. • 25 days annual leave from day one, plus bank holidays. • 5% matched pension scheme. • Group Life Insurance. • Private Healthcare. • Health and wellbeing support programmes.

• Good IT skills (including Microsoft Office), experience of working with systems to support day-to-day queries or design changes to optimise usage; able and keen to learn new systems quickly.

- Digital Commerce Platform and CRM

About the role

Product Manager, on a fixed term or contract basis, to lead the delivery of a new digital commerce platform for both B2B and consumer (B2C) customers, together with a new approach to customer relationship management (CRM).

We're a retailer who owns the end to end customer journey from discovery through to installation and post care, serving consumers (B2C) through websites, stores and home consultants and trade customers through a growing business to business (B2B) channel.

You will report to the Chief Technology Officer. You will own the product vision, roadmap and delivery plan for the programme, and you will be accountable for getting it live with no loss of functionality for customers or colleagues.
CRM is part of the role. The direction is not yet decided, so you will take the CRM approach (build, buy or a lighter model fed by an owned context layer) from options to a decision and into delivery, starting with one real use case such as recovering lapsed quotes. The detail is covered in a separate CRM strategy.

The programme

The programme replaces a legacy website and an overloaded back office system with a composable platform built around APIs, so that B2B and B2C trading can scale without headcount growing at the same rate (B2B revenue is targeted to grow several times over four years), and so that consumers get a faster, more personal journey from discovery to fitting.

Why we are changing

•
The current website runs on technology the business does not support and has no source code access, so every change depends on third party resource.

•
The back office system has absorbed pricing, promotions, quoting and order management and has become a bottleneck.

•
Internal applications are fragmented, with no single view of the customer or the order.

•
Personalisation is limited and the stack is not ready for AI assisted and agentic shopping.

•
Data arrives in overnight batches rather than as events.

B2B and B2C scope

•
B2B: a gated portal for trade customers with company accounts, price lists, order and fit date visibility, quoting and ordering, and service levels for the B2B operations team.

•
B2C: the consumer journey from discovery to order and installations, covering product search and merchandising, personalisation, pricing and promotions, basket and checkout, product samples, appointment booking, customer accounts and order tracking, store information and stock visibility, forms, reviews, and saved projects and property views.

•
Across both: a single source of truth for price and product, accessibility, performance and responsive design, search and answer engine visibility, and readiness for agentic shopping and support.

The target architecture

•
A commerce engine for B2B and B2C accounts, pricing, product and orders, with order status orchestration.

•
The existing enterprise resource planning system retained as the system of record for finance, stock, purchasing, shipping and invoicing.

•
A custom built customer experience layer for the consumer website, B2B portal and store and field applications, with personalisation and experimentation on the consumer side, connected through product, search, basket, quote, ordering, payments and refunds, identity and customer services.
•
Replacement content management, with a CRM approach still to be decided.

•
Product information management, search and merchandising, payment gateways and supporting services such as address lookup, samples fulfilment and reviews.

•
An event driven data platform from day one.



Key responsibilities

Programme leadership

•
Own the roadmap, plan, milestones, dependencies and risk register across the commerce, CRM, content, data and migration workstreams.

•
Run the governance rhythm and report progress, risks and decisions to the CTO and executive team.

Product scope and prioritisation

•
Question every requirement and remove what is not needed before simplifying or automating what remains.

•
Define what like for like means for each channel, and make scope trade offs on quoting, basket creation, payments, refunds and agentic shopping.

•
Maintain a prioritised backlog and clear acceptance criteria with engineering.

Delivery

•
Work day to day with engineering leads, architects and a specialist implementation partner to deliver in time boxed phases.

•
Make sure standards, automated tests and monitoring are in place from the first sprint.
Decisions and CRM

•
Drive the CRM and content management decisions through clear criteria, shortlists and proofs, and bring them to the CTO for sign off.

•
Take the CRM direction from options to a decision and the first CRM use case into delivery.

B2C experience

•
Own the consumer journey from discovery to order and installation, including search, personalisation, basket, checkout, samples and appointments.

•
Set conversion, search visibility and customer experience measures for the consumer site and track them from the beta onwards.

•
Run the consumer beta on the secondary brand site and use what it shows to de risk the main consumer migration.
Migration and risk

•
Own the customer data migration approach, the URL redirect plan and search visibility protection.

•
Plan parity testing and a staged launch, from B2B to a B2C beta on a lower-traffic site and then to the main B2C website.

Stakeholders and change

•
Engage stores, in-home teams, B2B and B2C operations, marketing, finance, installation and customer service, and agree what changes for each.

•
Plan adoption, training and process change, for example orders that cannot be edited after they close.

•
Help shape the team around you, including onboarding partner engineers.

Experience we are looking for

Essential

•
A track record as a product manager or programme lead delivering a major commerce, platform or CRM transformation from start to finish.

•
Experience across B2B and B2C commerce, including conversion, personalisation and search visibility, ideally in retail or a multichannel business.

•
Confident working with composable, API led and event driven architectures, and able to challenge engineers constructively.

•
Experience running build versus buy decisions and managing specialist implementation partners.

•
Strong stakeholder management up to executive level, with data driven prioritisation.

•
Experience of customer data migration and site migrations that protect search visibility.

•
Working knowledge of UK GDPR and PECR as they apply to customer data and marketing.

Desirable

•
CRM or customer data platform delivery, including AI assisted or agent based journeys.

•
Integration with enterprise resource planning systems.

•
Appointment based, field or installation service businesses.

•
Home improvement or store based retail.

job_description:
About AlphaSense: 
AlphaSense is the AI platform redefining market intelligence and workflow orchestration, trusted by thousands of leading organizations to drive faster, more confident decisions in business and finance. The platform combines domain-specific AI with a vast content universe of over 500 million premium business documents — including equity research, earnings calls, expert interviews, filings, news, and internal proprietary content. Purpose-built for speed, accuracy, and enterprise-grade security, AlphaSense helps teams extract critical insights, uncover market-moving trends, and automate complex workflows with high-quality outputs. With AI solutions like Generative Search, Generative Grid, and Deep Research, AlphaSense delivers the clarity and depth professionals need to navigate complexity and obtain accurate, real-time information quickly. For more information, visit www.alpha-sense.com. Come join us.
Location: London (In office presence required) About the Team:
The Customer Success organisation is composed of four teams: pre-sales, customer success managers, account management and support. The CS org is dedicated to ensuring every client realises the full value of their investment in our platform, working as an integrated partner to help clients achieve meaningful outcomes and embed AlphaSense into their everyday decision-making.
By blending industry knowledge, product expertise, and a deep understanding of client priorities, the team helps organisations uncover new use cases, accelerate adoption, and sustain long-term growth. Their close engagement with clients also creates a powerful feedback loop—informing product innovation, shaping content strategy, and ensuring that the evolving needs of the corporate community are consistently reflected in how AlphaSense delivers value.
About the Role: 
As a Senior Customer Success Manager (Sr. CSM) at AlphaSense, you will be the strategic lead for our most complex and high-value accounts within the Corporate sector. You are responsible for navigating multi-million dollar global organizations and driving long-term ROI through technical group/individual training while ensuring company-wide adoption across multiple business units. You will manage a concentrated portfolio of strategic accounts, remaining at the forefront of product and Corporate vertical expertise, while scaling your impact across the organization through account strategy, leadership and innovation.
What You’ll Do: 
• Strategic Account Influence: Navigate and influence multiple business units and key power users across the world largest and most complex global organizations. Create a groundswell of positive user sentiment to drive renewals and expansion with Senior Leadership.
• Architect Deep Adoption & Value Realization: Synthesize complex usage into actionable insights. Design multi-quarter adoption roadmaps in tandem with your Account Management peers that align AlphaSense capabilities with business objectives.
• Onboarding & Ongoing Training: As an expert on the product, you will guide new clients through onboarding, training, and best-practice adoption to ensure a strong foundation, both virtually and in person.
• Technical & Domain Mastery: Independently lead sophisticated technical conversations regarding Managed Content Providers (MCP), APIs, and Large Language Models (LLMs) with technical stakeholders and platform owners.
• Executive Presence & Communication: Command virtual and in-person rooms with executive presence, and leverage powerful, strategic follow-ups as a tool to drive adoption and link AlphaSense to specific Senior Leader business objectives.
• Solo On-Site Leadership: Fully own high-stakes, multi-day on-site engagements and lead customer "Lunch & Learns,’’ tailoring presentations to diverse user groups and core personas using our WWH (Why, What, How) framework.
• Company Innovation: engage in cross-functional initiatives outside the standard CSM scope, such as product feedback loops, hiring committees, mentorship programs and process innovation to improve team efficiency.
Who You Are:
• 4 -6+ years of professional experience in Customer Success or Account Management, with a proven track record of managing a strategic portfolio. 
• Ability to travel 20% of time. 
• Experience working with clients in the Life Sciences industry, including Pharma, Biotech, Medical devices and diagnostics - additional bonus for familiarity with competitive intelligence, business development and clinical and commercial strategy workflows. 
• Possess the technical acumen to navigate complex conversations around data integrations, APIs, and AI-driven market intelligence solutions.
• Ability to identify the 5% of users who drive the majority of sentiment and influence within an account, focusing on high-level business outcomes over basic feature adoption.
• Excellent communication skills with a demonstrable track record for collaborating internally in a cross-functional environment and onsite with customers. 
• A natural leader who thrives in fast-paced environments and is committed to contributing to the "AlphaSense Playbook" through mentorship and internal innovation.

job_title: Chief Engineer, Data Centre Engineering Operations, Data Centre Engineering Operations
job_description:
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation
of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the
cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage,
networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have
continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging
problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re
looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply
chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles.
You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest
standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at
the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive
culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

As Chief Engineer, you will be responsible for ensuring that all electrical,
mechanical, and fire/life safety equipment within the data center is operating
at peak efficiency. This involves planned preventative maintenance of equipment,
daily corrective work, and emergency response. You are expected to be a singular
focal point for all facility operations and to support Amazon within its owned
and operated data centers.

You should be able to manage large scale impacting projects and new region
support from conception to completion. These projects involve large amounts of
independent work as well as collaboration with external support groups including
engineering, automation, procurement, and finance in both local and global
settings. As Chief Engineer, you will be tasked with creating and delivering on
key milestones, obtaining and tracking quotes for all necessary costs, and
documenting project results for future implementation at other facilities. The
goals of such projects are for the Chief Engineers to drive innovation and
resiliency while reducing operational costs in the facilities.



Key job responsibilities
- Train and support the Engineering team in their role of providing electrical
and mechanical equipment troubleshooting and operations
- Implement and execute site or equipment-specific training exercises. Exercises
cover, but are not limited to: stand-by diesel generators, switchgear, UPSs,
PDUs, AHUs, chillers etc.
- Oversee day-to-day operation and maintenance of mechanical and electrical
equipment in data center sites
- Operate independently, with limited direct management
- Assist in the design and build-out of new facilities and perform root cause
analysis of equipment failures
- Act as an escalation point for all facilities-related issues within the data
center region. Work OT hours as needed to support site stability
- Troubleshoot and report facility and data sever-level events within internal
Service Level Agreements (SLA)
- Create and deploy standard practices for Engineering Operations Technicians,
Chief Engineers, and vendor support teams
- Ensure all safety procedures are adhered to by vendors, and AWS staff
- Respond to off hour emergency calls related to his data centers and help with
the investigation, mitigation, and recovery of the issue(s).
- Candidates should be able to lift up to 40 lbs and or work in elevated
locations.
- Ability to work in an environment that operates 24/7 with an ability to
provide after-hours support as needed. All physical requirements are expected
with reasonable accommodations

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS
- Work at height, and from ladders
- Perform physical tasks during the shift
- Work in a noisy environment, with ear protection

Antora Energy delivers affordable, reliable energy to industry, data centers, and the grid. Our thermal batteries turn low-cost electricity into always-on heat and power, without supply-constrained critical minerals or multi-year construction timelines.
We are growing our company with people who put team and mission first, value connection through laughter and joy, and work with humility and openness. We are committed to building a diverse, passionate, and creative team dedicated to a future powered by abundant, clean, low-cost energy.
About The Role
Antora Energy is seeking an engineer to own the real-time cloud infrastructure connecting our software systems to physical hardware.
Every five minutes, our software determines how our thermal batteries should charge and discharge. Those decisions must travel reliably through our messaging infrastructure and reach physical assets in the field. In the other direction, plant telemetry flows from the edge into our cloud data warehouse, where it must be complete, timely, and trustworthy enough to support operational decisions and financial trading.
You’ll also own the corporate cloud platform that the rest of the company builds on. While these systems have very different service-level requirements, they share a need for thoughtful architecture, strong operational practices, and reliable tooling.
We’re hiring one person for a scope that many companies divide across multiple teams. This is a high-impact opportunity to establish platform-wide standards, unify observability, and shape our infrastructure and operational strategy from end to end.
What You'll Do
Own the Real-Time Telemetry and Dispatch Path
Own the full data path from the edge, through streaming ingestion, into the warehouse, and back out to asset dispatch.
You’ll define service-level objectives, build freshness and gap detection, and ensure silent data loss becomes an actionable alert—not something discovered in a report a week later.
Manage Our AWS Infrastructure as Code
Own and evolve our AWS footprint across multiple accounts using Terraform.
You’ll operate containerized services on ECS and Lambda and manage orchestration, networking, secrets, access controls, and supporting infrastructure. You’ll design systems with failure modes, blast radius, observability, capacity, and recovery in mind from the beginning.
Advance an AI-First Software Development Lifecycle
Our engineers already work alongside AI coding agents. The constraint is no longer how quickly code can be written—it is how quickly that code can be verified and deployed safely.
You’ll build the systems that make agent-authored changes safe at scale, including fast and trustworthy CI, hermetic test infrastructure, preview environments, progressive delivery, and automated guardrails.
You’ll also establish the cost controls and verification workflows that allow autonomous development systems to operate without requiring a person to supervise every step.
Own Reliability for Systems Connected to Physical Assets
Participate in the on-call rotation for systems that dispatch instructions to a physical plant.
You’ll build the observability, alerting, and response processes needed to identify problems before they affect field operations. You’ll also define clear escalation paths across cloud infrastructure, site controls, and our market operations desk.
Build a Platform Engineers Want to Use
Treat infrastructure as an internal product. Create self-service tools, paved paths, and platform capabilities that help engineers ship safely without unnecessary friction.
You’ll set standards where consistency matters while avoiding process for process’s sake.
What We're Looking For
• Deep production infrastructure experience. You have several years of experience building and operating cloud infrastructure at scale, with strong expertise in AWS, Terraform, containers, and CI/CD.
• Hands-on site reliability experience. You have carried primary on-call responsibility for a production system that mattered. You have also planned and completed at least one zero-downtime migration involving a stateful, always-on service.

About The Role
Antora Energy is looking for a full-stack product engineer to build the software products that power our business - from external customer experiences to internal tools used by teams across Business Development, Operations, and R&D.
In this role, you’ll help shape product vision, design the underlying data models, and connect AI systems with the business logic that makes them useful. You’ll own products end to end, working directly with users to understand their workflows, translate ambiguous needs into practical solutions, and ship software that performs reliably in production.
You’ll also help build Antora’s long-term software capabilities. That means creating systems, standards, and guardrails that allow partner teams to safely modify existing tools and build new ones within our ecosystem - without engineering becoming a bottleneck.
This is a highly autonomous role with direct influence over how software is designed and built at Antora. We’re looking for deep expertise in one or more core areas - such as software engineering, data modeling, AI integration, or product development - along with the curiosity and practical judgment to work across the full stack.
What You'll Do
Build Full-Stack Products
Design, build, deploy, and maintain internal and external software products across the frontend, backend, data, and AI layers. Own the complete product lifecycle, including architecture, observability, reliability, and ongoing maintenance.
Enable Self-Service
Put workflow creation directly into users’ hands. Build systems that allow analysts, operators, and other domain experts to adapt their own tools without filing a ticket and waiting for engineering support.
Co-Create with Users
Work alongside the people doing the work. Learn their processes, build solutions with them, and give them the tools and confidence to continue improving those solutions independently.
When users contribute their own code or workflows, you’ll make those contributions safe to run, easy to review, and straightforward to maintain.

At Antora, an AI system that answers an unauthorized question is not a clever feature—it is a business risk.

Commercial Risk Consulting - Graduate Programme 2027
Start Date 1st September 2027
Application closing date 7th December 2026 Please note, we may close earlier if we receive the quantity, quality & diversity of applications required.
Better Decisions Begin with You
At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world. As an organisation, we are united through trust as one inclusive, diverse team, and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed.
Launch Your Career in Commercial Risk Consulting
Join Aon as a Commercial Risk Consulting graduate and, from day one, you’ll be an integral part of either our Strategic Engagement (Inpoint) or Aon M&A and Transaction Solutions (AMATS) team. You’ll help clients navigate complex business challenges, handle risk and make better-informed decisions.
Strategic Engagement (Inpoint):
Inpoint is Aon’s carrier engagement and management business, working primarily with insurers across Commercial Risk. Our teams use market insight, portfolio analytics and Aon’s broader capabilities to build stronger, more strategic relationships with carrier partners.
Strategic Engagement is focused on helping Aon and its carrier partners identify shared priorities, understand portfolio performance and turn insight into meaningful action. This is not a traditional strategy consulting role. It is a relationship-led, data-informed opportunity at the centre of Aon’s engagement with the insurance market.
As a Strategic Engagement Graduate, you will work with colleagues across Strategy & Technology Group (STG), the Global Broking Centre (GBC) and Commercial Risk UK. You will help prepare insight for senior conversations with insurers, support engagement on portfolio opportunities and contribute to initiatives that strengthen how Aon and its carrier partners work together.
The role offers exposure to senior leaders across Aon and the insurance market. It also provides the chance to build a strong understanding of commercial insurance, carrier priorities, broking, and portfolio dynamics.
What You Will Do
• Analyse market, carrier and portfolio information to identify trends and opportunities, turning data and analytics into practical insights for carrier and internal partners discussions
• Support strategic relationship planning and engagement for key insurers, helping teams establish clear priorities, actions and follow-through while deepening your knowledge of customer relationship management
• Collaborate across Inpoint, GBC and Commercial Risk UK to understand carrier objectives, capture insight and coordinate engagement with the market, building your project management and consulting skills over time
• Contribute to strategic carrier meetings and senior collaborator discussions and learn how strong commercial relationships are developed throughout Aon and the insurance sector
• Prepare clear, high-quality materials and presentations for strategic meetings and portfolio reviews, using focused research and document review to communicate complex information concisely
Aon M&A and Transaction Solutions (AMATS): Mergers and Acquisitions (M&A) and other event-driven situations can be complex, time-critical and highly specialised. The AMATS team typically assists clients in three core areas, prior to, during and/or after completion of an M&A deal or other investment opportunity, by:
• Providing due diligence on a ‘target’ business across a wide range of deal-critical areas, including risk & insurance, cyber & digital, human capital and climate matters. This diligence evaluates the target’s risk exposures - past, current, and future - which may impact transaction value for the buyer
• Arranging insurance solutions aimed at de-risking transaction liabilities and enhancing investor returns, often removing deal-breaking risks. This involves structuring and placing solutions like warranty & indemnity insurance and using insurance capital to mitigate contingent risks, such as tax and litigation
• Delivering portfolio value creation programmes for financial sponsors, including private equity, infrastructure funds, and real estate investors. Use their portfolio scale and insights from analysis, coordinate efforts to reduce the total cost of risk and improve governance
The clients include financial sponsors and Corporates, with transaction sizes ranging from small UK domestic deals (such as Voyage Care’s acquisition of Orchard Healthcare) to some of the largest cross-border transactions (such as KONE’s $34.4 billion combination with TK Elevators). Further deal examples can be found on Aon’s LinkedIn page.
You’ll gain exposure to several parts of our transaction advisory and broking business to help build your understanding of why clients implement M&A deals and how Aon supports their business and investment objectives.
What You Will Do
• Support transaction advisory work for private equity, infrastructure, real estate and corporate clients, helping the team research and analyse risks connected with M&A deals
• Support the arrangement of M&A insurance solutions by helping colleagues prepare information for the insurance market and learning how transaction risks can be transferred
• Coordinate Aon expertise across practices and geographies while developing your internal network and learning to handle actions and workstreams across a fast-moving transaction process
• Help identify relevant Aon products, services and solutions that may support client deals and investment objectives, applying commercial judgement and broader business context
• Build strong collaborative connections with clients, insurers, M&A advisers and internal collaborators, while developing your consulting and business communication skills over time
Your Development
As an Aon Graduate, you will be enrolled onto our Launch Programme when you join. Alongside your broader development, you will progressively build the technical and professional capabilities needed for the role. This development programme is built around the following core elements: 1. Business learning. On the job learning and experiences giving you the opportunity to develop your knowledge and understanding of the team and solution line you have joined.
2. Centralised learning. Our UK graduates complete in an Aon Induction, monthly webinars, business skills training and workshops; all designed to help you develop your knowledge of Aon, build your confidence and your network across our business.
3. Professional Qualifications. To enable you to be as successful as possible, as part of your role, you will be expected to complete our Go Further Apprenticeship programmes. We’ll fully support your study towards the level 4 Diploma in Insurance from the CII (Chartered Insurance Institute) and beyond. To support you as you study for your exams, you’ll receive paid study leave, plus an extensive range of study and tuition materials.
Your career beyond your Graduate programme
Once you’ve completed the formal graduate programme, you’ll continue to receive lots of support at Aon. As well as continued technical and business skills training, you’ll receive support for your CII qualifications. To aid your professional development you’ll receive regular performance feedback, and work with your line manager towards promotions.
Next Steps
If you are interested in this programme and would like to apply, here is some useful information: Please review the information on each team and select your first-choice preferred team should you be successful. Please note that, where possible, we will try to consider you for your first-choice preference, however we cannot guarantee your first choice due to availability of roles. If your top preference is unavailable at the time of your Assessment Centre, we will also consider you for the other teams.
Entry Requirements:
• You will need to have or be on track to achieve a 2:1 degree (or equivalent) in any degree subject.
• To ensure compliance with UK law, successful candidates must demonstrate their right to work in the UK throughout the duration of their time in role. What are we looking for?
• Motivation and ambition to pursue a career in Commercial Risk Consulting. You should be able to explain why Strategic Engagement (Inpoint) or AMATS at Aon interests you and how it aligns with your longer-term goals
• AI literacy, prompt engineering and AI judgement. Comfortable using AI-enabled technologies such as Copilot, analytics platforms and digital productivity tools, able to refine outputs and assess their accuracy, relevance and appropriateness
• Client centricity, strategic thinking and commercial awareness. Curious about the insurance market and able to connect your work to client and carrier outcomes while considering wider business priorities
• Critical thinking, problem solving and analytical skills. Able to analyse information, identify patterns, challenge assumptions and draw evidence-based conclusions using digital tools and data
• Strong communication and collaboration skills. Able to explain complex information clearly, ask thoughtful questions and build positive working relationships with a range of internal and external partners
• Results driven, dependable and adaptable. Takes ownership, applies feedback, continuously develops skills and can manage changing priorities while delivering accurate, high-quality work
• Inclusive. Values different perspectives, challenges assumptions and helps create an environment where everyone feels respected and able to contribute
Locations: Here are the locations where we have graduate opportunities this year: London
We recognise the value for our Early Career colleagues of being in the office environment from the beginning of their programme. As a new graduate, you will spend the first 6 months based in the office to support your learning, development, and progression. This will enable you access to support from managers, collaborate with colleagues as well as grow your network across Aon. After completing this initial training period, you will then have the opportunity to work more flexibly, spending at least 3 to 4 days face to face in the Aon office or with clients.
Aon UK Graduate Recruitment: What to Expect We know applying for your first graduate role can be exciting, and sometimes a little daunting. At Aon, we’re committed to making our recruitment process as transparent and supportive as possible. Here’s how our selection journey works, and what you can expect at each stage:
1. Application Review
• We process applications on a rolling basis, moving candidates forward as they complete each stage.
• Every application is carefully reviewed by our team (not by AI).
• Due to the high volume of interest, this stage can take up to two weeks.
• Please note: We do not review CVs or cover letters at this point.
2. Online Assessment
• We understand you want to put your best foot forward, so you’ll have 5 calendar days to complete the online assessment.
• If you need more time, just let us know as extensions are available.
3. Video Interview
• Preparation matters, so you’ll have up to 10 days (240 hours) from receiving your invitation to record and submit your video interview.
• Rest assured: Every video interview is reviewed by a real member of our recruitment team, not an AI system.
• You’ll typically hear back from us within 2-3 weeks after submitting your interview, though times may vary depending on the number of applications.
4. Assessment Centres
• Our assessment centres are held in person at the Aon office closest to the location you applied for.
• Please note: Due to the large number of applications, not every candidate who completes a video interview will be invited to an assessment centre.
• Assessment centres usually run after Christmas, from mid-January.
• If selected, you’ll have 7-14 days’ notice to help you arrange any travel.
• We run a limited number of Assessment Centre so please make every effort to attend if invited.
• We reimburse reasonable travel costs (such as standard class train tickets). Flights and hotels are only covered if agreed in advance.
• At the assessment centre stage, your CV and cover letter will be shared with hiring managers. This helps them get a fuller picture of you as a candidate—but these documents are not used for initial screening.
What is Aon's guidance of the use of AI during the selection process?
As an innovative global leader, we recognize and embrace the power of Artificial Intelligence (AI) to help job seekers be more efficient in their recruitment processes. In fact, Aon is in the business of developing and implementing innovative AI tools that support both colleagues and clients, which you’ll use as an Aon colleague if you join our team.
AI can be a helpful tool for researching Aon, preparing for interviews or refining your CV, it should support, not replace, your own thinking, judgement, skills and experiences. Any application materials you submit should accurately reflect your achievements, capabilities and potential.
We ask that you refrain from using AI when completing assessments or during live or pre-recorded interview processes, which will often include an in-person interview where the technology will not be available to you. Additionally, virtual or in-person interviews should not be recorded or transcribed.
At Aon, we foster a culture of inclusiveness, fairness and transparency. We expect all candidates to embrace these principles in every interaction with us.
Can I apply for more than one programme or role?
We ask candidates to submit one Early Carers application per recruitment cycle. We encourage you to explore our opportunities carefully and apply for the programme or role that best matches your skills, interests and career goals. This helps you focus on submitting your strongest application and ensures we can assess candidates fairly and efficiently.
If, during the selection process, we believe another opportunity at Aon may be a better fit for your experience and aspirations, our recruitment team may discuss alternative options with you.
If you're unsure which programme is right for you, we recommend reviewing the programme information on our careers site or attending one of our events before applying.
Top Tip: Choose the role you're most excited about, rather than treating a second application as a back-up option. We want to understand where your genuine interests lie and how you see your future career developing.
We’re here to support you every step of the way. If you have any questions or need accommodations, just contact our team - graduates@aon.co.uk. Good luck, and we look forward to seeing what you can bring to Aon! #AonGraduateUK #CommercialRiskConsultingUK

Location: Remote-first, UK. Occasional travel for team events or customer meetings.

Start: As soon as possible
Must hold (or be able to pass) an Enhanced DBS check
Programmes: Data Technician (level 3) and Data Analyst (level 4)

Curiosity over perfection
Progress over polish
People who take ownership without being asked

✘ You need a fully structured corporate environment to do your best work

Ongoing professional development and leadership support

About AQEMIA
AQEMIA is a drug invention company dedicated to creating entirely new medicines to address major unmet medical needs. At the core of our mission is QEMI, our proprietary molecule-invention platform, which uniquely combines cutting-edge science with advanced technology. Powered by physics-based modeling, statistical mechanics, and generative AI, QEMI allows our teams to design novel drug candidates from first principles.
What makes AQEMIA different is our commitment to true innovation: our research is dedicated to the invention of new molecular entities, not the refinement of existing ones. We focus on inventing never-before-seen molecules, without relying on experimental data, and advancing them into a growing pipeline of proprietary programs and strategic partnerships with leading pharmaceutical companies.
Our most advanced preclinical programs are currently in vivo optimization, targeting diseases still waiting for effective treatments, offering our teams the opportunity to work on science that can make a real difference in people’s lives.
For more information, visit AQEMIA.com, our WTTJ Page, and our LinkedIn.
About our Team
AQEMIA brings together a diverse, multidisciplinary team of 80+ professionals based in Paris and London. Our scientists and engineers, including chemists, physicists, machine learning experts, and software engineers, work side by side to push the boundaries of early-stage drug discovery.
This close collaboration across disciplines is central to our approach, enabling us to tackle complex scientific challenges from first principles and translate cutting-edge ideas into novel therapeutic candidates. At AQEMIA, team members are encouraged to contribute their expertise, learn from one another, and play an active role in shaping the future of drug invention.
About our Engineering Department
The Engineering team builds and scales the technical foundations that power Aqemia’s drug discovery engine.
Bringing together expertise across software engineering, cloud infrastructure, data engineering, site reliability engineering (SRE), and scientific computing, the team designs and operates robust, secure, and high-performance platforms that enable Aqemia’s scientific and AI teams to experiment, train, deploy, and run models at scale.
Their work spans data infrastructure, scientific compute systems, cloud operations, orchestration, observability, CI/CD, developer tooling, and platform scalability. By transforming cutting-edge research into reliable and scalable systems, the team accelerates the discovery of new medicines while ensuring operational excellence and an outstanding developer experience.
The role
At AQEMIA, our research teams develop cutting-edge methods, from physics-based statistical mechanics calculations to fine-tuned machine learning models for generative chemistry and property prediction.
As a Senior Scientific Software Engineer, you’ll turn these methods into robust, scalable software that powers our drug discovery platform. You’ll sit at the intersection of science and engineering, working closely with physicists and ML researchers to understand their methods, challenge prototypes and bring them into production. You’ll also help shape the architecture and engineering standards of our scientific computing stack, so it stays modular, scalable and maintainable as we grow. This is an opportunity to have a direct impact on how quickly and reliably our science reaches real drug discovery programs.
Responsibilities
Translate scientific strategies from our StatMech research teams into software components that run at scale.
Optimize compute-intensive code (profiling, parallelization, GPU acceleration) and run it reliably at scale on our cloud infrastructure.
Expose physics-based calculations through clean APIs that integrate into our technology platform.
Package ML models fine-tuned by our AI research teams (generative chemistry, property prediction, etc.) into versioned, reproducible, deployable components, and build scalable, GPU-efficient inference pipelines.
Implement MLOps practices, including model and data versioning, experiment tracking, model registry and monitoring.
Orchestrate ML models and physics-based calculations into end-to-end workflows.
Co-lead the architecture of our scientific computing stack and our Python engineering standards: packaging, typing, testing, code review and documentation.
Contribute to setting up and maintaining CI/CD pipelines and workflow orchestration (e.g. GitHub Actions, Docker, Airflow/Prefect, Kubernetes, Flyte), and stay up to date with advances in cheminformatics.
Qualifications
MSc or PhD in computer science, applied mathematics or a related quantitative field, with a background in computational chemistry, molecular simulation or statistical physics.
5+ years of software engineering experience, with strong expertise in a cheminformatics context.
Strong Python skills and experience with RDKit or similar libraries.
Solid software architecture skills: designing modular, maintainable systems used by several teams.
Hands-on experience with CI/CD, containerization (Docker) and workflow orchestration (e.g. Airflow, Prefect, Kubernetes).
Experience running compute-intensive workloads at scale on the cloud, including GPUs.
Ability to work closely with researchers (understanding their methods, challenging prototypes and explaining engineering trade-offs), with good communication skills and a collaborative mindset.
Nice‑to‑Have
MLOps experience: model versioning, experiment tracking, model serving.
Experience mentoring engineers or leading technical standards across an organization.

At AQEMIA, we work for a mission: joining us means having your own impact on changing the way drugs are discovered, and helping to shape the direction of our fast-growing company and team.
Expanding Drug Discovery Pipeline: Focused on critical therapeutic areas like Oncology, CNS, Immuno-inflammation... with in vivo proof of concept/patent stage programs. Collaborations with top Pharma, including a $140M Sanofi deal.

including effective use of AI tools where appropriate.

assessment and recommendation.
● Wider ownership: Take on additional Finance responsibilities and projects as the needs of the business and Finance function evolve.
This role is a great opportunity for someone with established accounting and finance experience, with the ambition to grow their skills and shape their own role. We are looking for someone who will not only deliver established processes, but will also identify areas for improvement and proactively progressively take ownership of a wider range of Finance activities.

You will maintain a structured view of AZ's highest-value AI science problems – mapping which questions most need answers, which frameworks are now mature enough to address them, and where AZ's unique data, biology, and portfolio create irreplaceable scientific advantage. You will also act as the scientific lead and orchestrator for delivering against those problems, assembling the right combination of expertise and resources and holding the scientific hypothesis through to a result that changes a decision.
This is a role for someone familiar with key questions across the drug discovery pipeline, who can attend a frontier AI seminar and immediately see which ideas are applicable to areas from target identification to trial design, and who has the scientific conviction to advocate for a particular problem in the face of competing priorities.
If you thrive at the intersection of machine learning and translational oncology and want to leave a direct mark on the scientific questions that shape AstraZeneca's pipeline, this role is for you.

AI Landscape & Opportunity Mapping:
• Maintain an interactive framework providing a structured, dynamic inventory of AZ's internal and external AI capabilities, including frontier models and platforms.
• Identify high-priority scientific questions—such as those in target discovery, combination therapy, tumor mapping, and trial design—where frontier AI can deliver significant value. Distinguish opportunities unique to AstraZeneca from those addressable with generic tools or public data.

• Apply scientific expertise and evaluation standards to AI-driven frameworks designed to maintain a live, structured record of R&D goals and decision-making.

About the Role
We’re looking for a Control Systems Engineer to join our Controls team at Grove, working on the systems that sit behind our gearbox and clutch.
Right now, the focus is the dyno: building and developing the control system that lets us recreate what the car sees on track. As the transmission programme moves forward, you’ll grow into owning the gearbox and clutch controls, covering calibration, development, control simulation and the tooling that goes with it. The aim is a gear shift and clutch response that’s reliable every time, in every situation.
You’ll work inside the standard ECU code, tracing through it to find where the gains and the pitfalls are, then tuning calibrations to get the best shift for each scenario. You’ll be part of a small team of around five, working closely with Vehicle Dynamics, Powertrain, Systems Simulation and Electronics.
It’s also a rare one. We’re developing our own gearbox from close to the ground up, which very few teams get to do, and the facility is being built with the long term in mind. Opportunities like this don’t come round often.
Key Responsibilities
• Calibrate and develop the gearbox and clutch control system, with a focus on reliable, repeatable gear shifts and clutch response
• Analyse data from dyno and car running to find the root cause of shift performance and reliability issues, then apply what you learn in calibrations and control tuning
• Learn, use and help develop the dyno control system, including integrating our vehicle models so the dyno reflects what happens on track
• Build control simulations and the supporting tooling, mainly in MATLAB, Simulink and Python
• Work within the standard ECU code and toolchain to get the best shift for each situation
• Support troubleshooting on the dyno and the car, diagnosing issues quickly and working with colleagues across the business to fix them
• Document designs, test protocols and results so that everything is accurate and traceable
About You
You’re a controls engineer who writes and understands the code, not someone who just edits other people’s. You know that code controlling physical hardware has to be right first time, and you take a proactive approach to safety-critical work. You pay attention to the detail, learn quickly, and are happy getting stuck into a programme that’s still taking shape.
• Degree in electrical, control systems, automotive, mechanical, software or a related engineering discipline
• At least 5 years in controls engineering, ideally in motorsport or high-performance automotive (Formula E, WEC and F1 backgrounds are all relevant)
• Strong MATLAB and Simulink experience, with confident programming and controls ability of your own
• Good understanding of embedded, real-time code that targets an ECU
• Able to read and trace through control code and state flows to spot where the advantages and risks sit
• Transmission controls experience is strongly preferred, and dyno knowledge is a close second
• Nice to have: dSpace or SpeedGoat, Python, the standard ECU toolchain (SECU, Atlas, SystemMonitor) and AVL Puma

What will you do on the programme?
As a Graduate Naval Architect at Babcock, you’ll play a part in some of the most complex and exciting engineering projects in the world today. You’ll be involved in a wide range of work that will help you build expertise across the many aspects of naval architecture.
Your projects could involve anything from helping us dock a 16,000-tonne nuclear submarine, to assessing the strength of an aircraft carrier’s flight deck for F35 Lightning landings. You might analyse mooring arrangements for a new frigate, design systems to withstand explosive events, or define stability requirements for a submarine surfacing through polar ice. Whatever you’re working on, you’ll learn directly from some of the most respected naval architects and structural engineers in the industry.
Along the way, you’ll gain expertise in analysing and designing all aspects of floating vessels and structures, from hull form and stability to propulsion and human factors. Whether supporting frontline capability or pioneering new technologies, you’ll be trusted to make a meaningful impact from the very beginning. How is the programme structured? The Naval Architecture Graduate Programme runs for two years and is designed to give you breadth and depth of experience across the discipline. You’ll move through a series of placements, each lasting a few months, giving you the chance to work in different teams and explore areas such as hydrodynamics, structures, design, stability and safety. These placements may take you to different areas of the business, from supporting submarine sustainment to working on surface ships or marine infrastructure projects. The team
The GPS EMEA Financial Institutions team helps banks and other regulated financial institutions with payments, liquidity, transactional FX and related treasury solutions. Within it, the UK Banks & PayTech team covers some of the most dynamic and fastest-changing parts of financial services.
PayTech is a fast-growing segment for the franchise. We are looking for a Vice President to own a defined portfolio of PayTech and digital banking relationships and help drive the segment's next phase of growth.
The role
The VP will report to the Head of UK Banks & PayTech. They will work under the segment direction of the EMEA PayTech Lead, who covers the largest strategic PayTech relationships and sets the segment agenda.
Within that framework, the VP will have primary GPS sales responsibility for a defined portfolio of names. The portfolio will mix established relationships, where the focus is protecting and deepening revenue, with growth names, where the focus is origination and building the relationship. The VP is accountable for portfolio revenue, product penetration, and opportunities from origination through onboarding, implementation and revenue realisation.
The portfolio mainly consists of:
• PayTechs: payment service providers, e-money institutions, merchant acquirers, money services businesses, card schemes and fintech platforms.
• Digital banks: a smaller number of neo/challenger banks and tier-2 UK banks.
Clients fall into two coverage models. Each needs a different way of working:
1. UK & Irish-headquartered clients: lead relationship coverage For clients headquartered in the UK or Ireland, the VP is the lead GPS relationship owner. They will:
• Own the overall relationship strategy, account plan and senior client dialogue from London.
• Coordinate with GPS colleagues in other regions as these clients expand internationally, including into the US and APAC.
• Act as the client's main point of contact for GPS across products and regions.
2. Inbound clients (mainly US and APAC-headquartered): EMEA coverage For global clients headquartered outside EMEA, the home-region Treasury Sales Officer owns the global relationship. The VP will:
• Own GPS coverage of the client's EMEA entities, licences and flows, including EU and UK-regulated entities wherever they are based in the region.
• Build joint account plans with home-region TSOs, Corporate Banking and CBK-S, and agree clear ownership of headquarters engagement, local coverage, product dialogue and implementation.
• Bring EMEA-specific insight to the global team, including regulatory, licensing, safeguarding and local payments requirements, and identify opportunities as the client's EMEA business grows.
PayTech clients build their businesses on payment infrastructure. They need scale, reach, resilience and speed to market across currencies and rails. The successful candidate will understand each client's business model, including how it collects, holds, converts and pays out funds. They will then bring the right capabilities together into one coherent strategy.
Responsibilities
Portfolio ownership and growth
• Own a defined portfolio of established and growth PayTech and digital banking relationships.
• Protect existing revenue through account, retention and recovery plans.
• Understand each client's licensing, legal-entity structure, flow of funds, settlement model and growth priorities.
• Originate new logos and entities where there is a credible business need, a model that fits the bank's risk appetite and an attractive risk-adjusted return.
• Work with the EMEA PayTech Lead on segment priorities, target lists and coverage plans.
Integrated solutions Build client strategies across:
• Collections and payouts, domestic and cross-border, across multiple currencies and rails, including real-time payments
• Currency clearing and account services
• Safeguarding, client money and settlement account structures
• Card and scheme settlement flows
• Liquidity and deposits
• Transactional FX, including AutoFX, embedded in the client's payment flows
• API connectivity, virtual account and data-led services
Position the bank as a scalable infrastructure partner, turning flows and balances into lasting, fee-based relationship revenue.
Execution and reporting
• Set clear deal plans, milestones, economics and accountable owners for priority opportunities.
• Own portfolio reporting across revenue, pipeline (identified, qualified, mandated, implementing, live) and forecasts, with clean CRM data.
• Spot onboarding, KYC, sanctions, credit and technology constraints early, and coordinate partners to resolve them.
• Stay accountable after go-live for adoption, volumes and revenue delivery.
Client advisory and governance
• Lead senior client meetings, RFPs and negotiations with founders, CFOs, treasurers and heads of payments.
• Engage clients on payments modernisation, real-time and always-on payments, APIs, digital money and operational resilience. Separate scalable opportunities from experiments, and never present pilots as generally available.
• Apply sound financial crime judgement: understand payments made on behalf of underlying customers, sanctions exposure and the risks of a client's merchant or customer base. Make sure every opportunity fits the bank's risk appetite and regulatory obligations.
• Feed client and market insight back to product partners.
• Support junior colleagues on the portfolio.
What we are looking for
• Client-facing experience in transaction banking, payments or FI coverage, with direct coverage of PayTechs, PSPs, EMIs, acquirers, card schemes or digital banks.
• A track record of personally originating and converting business with regulated financial institutions or payments firms.
• Experience both leading relationships directly and working within global coverage models alongside headquarters teams.
• Strong knowledge of cross-border payments, clearing, safeguarding, liquidity and transactional FX across major currencies.
• Understanding of PayTech business models, card and scheme settlement, real-time payments, APIs and multi-rail payment models.
• Good understanding of the UK/EU regulatory frameworks for payments and e-money, and of the related financial crime risks.
• Proven ability to coordinate across regions, products and control functions without formal authority.
• Sound commercial and risk judgement, plus excellent communication and negotiation skills.
• Experience covering US or APAC-headquartered clients in EMEA is preferred.
Measures of success
• Commercial: revenue growth and protection across established names; new logos and relationship growth across growth names; product penetration; fee-based revenue mix.
• Conversion: pipeline-to-mandate, mandate-to-live, time to revenue, realised revenue against the business case.
• Coordination: quality of account plans for UK/Irish-headquartered clients and joint plans with home-region teams for inbound clients; clear ownership and follow-through.
• Governance and team: sound risk management, clean onboarding outcomes, and contribution to junior talent development.
Why join This is a chance to own a defined portfolio in one of the franchise's fastest-growing segments, working alongside experienced senior coverage. The role combines leading relationships with UK and Irish PayTechs and covering in EMEA for leading global names. It offers significant exposure to senior clients, global coverage teams and GPS leadership, and suits an ambitious payments professional who wants to build a business, not inherit a static portfolio.

Acting as a technical authority, you’ll partner with backend engineers, product managers, SRE/DevOps, and architects to ensure our platform can evolve safely at scale, handling millions of requests while remaining reliable and future-proof. - Project management expertise to deliver complex procurement projects across multiple stakeholders.

- Professional procurement certification (e.g., CIPS, CPSM).
- Experience in media buying, creative services, or digital marketing procurement.
- Knowledge of emerging marketing technologies and trends.

[Apply Now](https://tally.so/r/pexEQq)
29th October 2026 (Strictly candidates only, recruitment agencies will be ignored) ## **The opportunity**.
Product design is changing faster than at any point in our careers, and we are looking for a designer who wants to be at the front of it. At Bettor Faster, the designers who get the best results from AI are the ones who started in UX. The judgement that tells you a user flow is wrong is the same judgement that tells you an AI's idea is wrong. This role is for a UX person who has made AI central to how they work, not a prompt writer who dabbles in design. Your core design skills and mastery of traditional tools like Figma and Miro remain essential, as AI is simply the accelerator that enables you to reach high-quality results faster. You will build the context that AI models work from, co-author briefs and specifications with them, decide when their output is right and when it only sounds right, and turn ideas into working prototypes through clear direction and instruction. Alongside that, you will run the discovery, research and audit work that Tier 1 sportsbooks, casinos, media companies and game studios come to us for. We are open on level. A strong mid-level designer who is ahead of the curve on AI is as interesting to us as a seasoned senior who has rebuilt their practice around it. We will shape the role and the package around the person we find. ## The role.
The majority of the role is to create background context, then work with AI models to produce briefs and specifications, knowing when those specifications are correct and when the model has produced a bad idea. From there you prompt prototypes rather than draw wireframes, and use your UX skill to refine them through instruction. In practice that breaks into four parts. **Building context.** You capture who the user is, how the product and the betting market work, what good looks like and how the brand sounds, in a form an AI can work from. The industry calls this context engineering. It is the foundation of everything the model produces afterwards, and the quality of your context is the biggest single lever on the quality of the output. **Co-authoring briefs and specifications.** You and the model write together. You set the problem, judge each draft and steer. **Job Title:** Digital Engineering Coordinator (BIM)
**Reporting to:** Digital Engineering Manager
**The Role**
We are seeking an experienced BIM Coordinator to join the Tunnels & Approaches contract on the LTC project, working within the Digital team and reporting to the Digital Engineering Manager.
This role is central to ensuring high-quality BIM data management throughout the design, construction and handover phases. You will be supporting the Digital Engineering Manager in the coordination of models from designers, subcontractors, and suppliers - with a particular focus on MEICA (Mechanical, Electrical, Information, Automation) scope.
You will work across the project to unlock the value of BIM data, supporting teams in leveraging models for quantity take-offs, 4D scheduling simulations, carbon analysis, and construction planning using our Digital Construction platform, DALUX. This is a technical, detail-focused role that requires strong BIM fundamentals, coordination discipline, and the ability to work collaboratively with designers, contractors, and digital teams.
**Key Responsibilities**
Model Data Quality and Coordination
- Liaise closely with Designers to review, and quality-assure models prior to construction issue, checking for completeness, accuracy, and compliance with project standards (including ISO 19650 and its related standards).
- Ensure design models are following the project Asset data requirements and monitor the asset tagging process prior to delivery for construction.
- Review models produced by supply chain partners and supplier. Ensure that they are all delivered in the project Common Data Environment and follows standards defined by the Exchange Information Requirements and Information Execution Plan.
- Work closely with both designers and suppliers to identify efficiency gains and apply good practices to avoid redundant work. Promote the use of parametric and data-driven modelling.
- Transfer Models from the Designers CDE to the project Digital Construction Platform, DALUX. Monitor that automated transfers are being performed effectively and flag any issues where required.
BIM Data utilisation and analytics
- Work with Digital Engineering Manager and relevant project teams to assist in data extraction and scheduling required for re-estimating or carbon calculations.
- Facilitate the use of 4D simulations on the project by supporting the planning team in their use of models.
Digital Awareness
- Promote the use of Models by all relevant project members. Ensure that the team can access models easily and are trained to use the agreed project toolset for Model visualisation.
- Perfom regular training sessions and produce training content to feed into the project Digital Learning Hub.
- Promote the wider use of digital solutions and ways of working on the project.
- Keep an open mind and manage conflict in a productive way to ensure that people feel empowered using technology rather than be overwhelmed by it.
**Essential Skills & Experience:**
- Proven experience working on construction projects (in the UK preferably)
- Proven experience in the production/management/coordination & validation of Graphical Information models on challenging construction projects
- Solid understanding of BIM principles and associated standards (ISO 19650 suite mainly)
- Familiarity with infrastructure, building services (MEP), or mixed-discipline project environments.
- Understanding of major projects workflows, processes, and team structures.
- Good technical and digital skills, with proven experience using tools such as Bentley iTwin, Autodesk Construction Cloud, Navisworks, DALUX or any other model coordination and validation tools.
- Previous experience using 4D simulations tool such as Synchro 4D will be a plus
- Awareness of key data management principles and appetite for automation
- Strong communication skills with the ability to engage and influence across multiple disciplines and seniority levels.
