Principal Scientist, Translational AI Foundations (Platform, Deployment and Knowledge Systems)
Position Summary
Translational IPS is forming Translational AI Foundations (TAIF), a small team of computational biologists and AI engineers that works side by side with our translational research groups. TAIF turns the biomarker analyses scientists already perform by hand into validated, reusable AI agents and workflows, then transfers each one to the research group that will use and maintain it. The science stays with those groups; TAIF builds the shared tools that make it faster and reproducible.
We are seeking a Principal Scientist to own the shared software platform the whole team builds on: the pieces no translational research group should have to build for itself. You will turn the team's engineering standards into tooling, own the ontology and knowledge graph as a shared service, and build versioned connections to our governed data. You will deploy validated tools as reliable services (REST APIs, tool servers, containers) with CI/CD, monitoring and a rollback plan. The initial scientific focus is circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA): its data connection and reference dataset, then, after the first spatial agents, a ctDNA agent built with the team's assay scientist. Deployment here means engineering deployment; broader adoption in the research groups is led by the team lead, with your hands-on support.
This role is for an architect who still builds: someone who has shipped governed data foundations and production services that scientists depend on, who understands the cost and value of regulated traceability (audit trails, versioning, validation evidence), and who has started building agentic automation on that foundation. You will build on the existing enterprise data platforms in partnership with the data, IT and knowledge-management teams that own them.
What you will have to work with
Established enterprise data platforms to connect to, not to rebuild. Governed data products on Databricks, the biomarker data stores behind our early-phase clinical studies (RNA-seq, ctDNA, WES, TCR-seq and CTC, with flow cytometry, cytokine profiling, IHC, proteomics, PK/PD and clinical data), an enterprise data catalog, an enterprise AI platform offering several large language models, and AWS cloud compute. Data operations, governance and the pipelines themselves sit with established partner teams; this role builds the data connections and a common data model on top of them.
An assay scientist on the same team who owns the scientific test cases and pass criteria that your validation pipeline applies, builds the assay agents on your platform, and co-builds the ctDNA agent with you.
Long-term owners for what you build. Established platform, research engineering and IT teams take over long-term operation of mature components.
Designated AI contacts in each translational research group who build tools using the team's templates, attend your hands-on sessions, and take ownership of what is deployed.
Your contributions will speed translational decisions across the BMS early clinical portfolio and help bring new medicines to patients sooner.
You will apply these resources across two areas:
• The shared platform and knowledge systems. The majority of the role: the shared software platform, engineering standards as tooling, the ontology and knowledge graph, and the connections to governed data.
• Deployment, hand-off and measurement. The remainder: deploying every validated tool, packaging it for the team that will own it, usage measurement, and direct work with translational research groups.
Key Responsibilities
The shared platform and knowledge systems
• Shared software platform. Build and maintain provenance tracking (data, code, model and prompt versions behind every number), evaluation tooling, access control, logging and usage telemetry, to enterprise security and release standards.
• Engineering standards as tooling. Implement the tool template, the automated test and validation pipeline, packaging of tools for use by AI agents (for example as Model Context Protocol tool servers), and a registry of tools with their owners, versions, lifecycle stages and users.
• Knowledge systems. Own the ontology and the knowledge graph service that hold the team's canonical biomarker definitions (their scientific content comes from the assay scientist). Start with a biomarker-trial ontology covering subjects, cohorts, visits, specimens, assays, endpoints and cutoffs, starting from the definitions scientists already use and connected to the enterprise data catalog.
• Data connections and governance. Build and maintain approved, versioned connections to the governed data products and biomarker data stores, recording the data version on every read; map clinical studies into a common data model; coordinate data logistics and governance with the data owners, starting with ctDNA.
Deployment, hand-off and measurement
• Deployment and operations. Containerize and deploy each validated tool and service (Docker; AWS ECS or Kubernetes on EKS, or the platform the owning team runs) with CI/CD, monitoring and a rollback plan, and own the release checklist (validation, access, monitoring, support owner, rollback) with the platform teams.
• Hand-off packaging and measurement. Package every component for the team that will own it (documentation, tests, versioning, a registry entry linked to its test cases) so it can be taken over unchanged. Instrument every tool for usage reporting (users, teams, elapsed and review time, test results, use after hand-off) and report usage and impact metrics.
• Research-group partnership. Work with the AI contacts in translational research groups: run hands-on tool-building sessions and review the tools they build against the team's engineering standards and for deployability.
• Engineering influence. Set the engineering practice the team and the AI contacts follow (code review, tests, versioning, release discipline), mentor junior team members on it, and document the shared platform so that its owning team can run it without you.
Basic Qualifications
• Ph.D. in computational biology, bioinformatics, computer science, data engineering or a related quantitative field with 4+ years of relevant academic and/or industry experience
• Or Master's degree with 6+ years
• Or Bachelor's degree with 8+ years.
Preferred Qualifications
We do not expect any one candidate to bring all of the following. Depth in several of these areas, combined with the habit of building for the owner who will run it after you, matters more than breadth across all of them.
• Ph.D. in computational biology, bioinformatics, computer science, data engineering or a related quantitative field with 4+ years of relevant academic and/or industry experience
• A record of shipping production data systems or services that other teams depend on: Python services, SDKs or pipelines with tests, version control and code review.
• Hands-on cloud engineering on AWS or an equivalent provider: storage and compute (for example S3, Batch, Lambda), containers (Docker), infrastructure as code, CI/CD, and monitoring and troubleshooting of running services.
• Experience designing governed FAIR (findable, accessible, interoperable, reusable) data foundations with their owners: schema and entity modeling, metadata harmonization, data-version and lineage discipline, access control and retention.
• Working familiarity with translational biomarker data (sequencing-based assays, liquid biopsy, clinical and sample metadata) sufficient to model it correctly, and with GxP-relevant traceability expectations (audit trails, versioning, validation evidence, human-review records).
• Experience building LLM-based or agentic automation, or building the data connectors, benchmark datasets and evaluation that such systems depend on, with the engineering judgment to run it as a maintained service.

Front-end experience (for example Streamlit, JavaScript or TypeScript) is useful, not required.

Senior Associate Scientist – In vitro Biology, Neuroscience Discovery
The Neuroscience TRC is committed to discovering and developing new therapies for patients with neurodegenerative and neuromuscular diseases. Our research combines human disease biology, molecular and cellular neuroscience, and target validation to identify and advance promising therapeutic opportunities. We are seeking a creative and rigorous scientist to investigate novel therapeutic targets and build confidence in their relevance to neurodegenerative disease. The successful candidate will develop and apply disease-relevant assays and advanced human iPSC-based models to understand how genetic or pharmacologic target modulation influences disease biology.
This role is ideal for a scientist with strong molecular and cellular biology expertise, a passion for understanding disease mechanisms, and experience translating biological questions into meaningful therapeutic hypothesis. The ideal candidate will have experience developing disease-relevant cellular assays and applying advanced human iPSC-based models to investigate target biology. Experience with microglia, neuroimmune biology, or multicellular CNS models is highly desirable.
Position Responsibilities
• Design and execute hypothesis-driven studies to investigate novel therapeutic targets in neurodegenerative disease.
• Develop and apply advanced human iPSC-based models and disease-relevant assays to evaluate target biology and therapeutic potential.
• Design, optimize, and implement mechanistic and translational assays that enable target interrogation, in vitro pharmacological characterization, compound profiling, and progression of drug-discovery programs.
• Establish causal relationships between target modulation and disease-relevant mechanisms using genetic, pharmacological, and molecular approaches.
• Support structure-activity relationship (SAR) efforts by generating high-quality in vitro pharmacology data that inform compound optimization, mechanism-of-action studies, and program progression.
• Represent Discovery Biology on cross-functional program teams, presenting experimental results and biological interpretation to support program progression.
Basic Qualifications
• Bachelor’s degree with 4+ years of academic and/or industry experience or
• Master’s degree with 2+ years of academic and/or industry experience
Preferred Qualifications
• Degree in neuroscience, biology, molecular biology, cell biology, or a related discipline.
• Strong foundation in molecular and cellular biology, with experience designing and executing experiments to address biological questions.
• Experience developing and applying cellular assays for target validation, pharmacological characterization, and/or compound profiling.
• Hands-on experience with human iPSC-derived neural and/or glial models and their application to neurodegenerative disease research.
• Demonstrated ability to independently drive experiments from conception through data interpretation and clearly present scientific findings within multidisciplinary teams
• Additional Preferred Qualifications and Experience
• Strong understanding of neurodegenerative disease biology, including pathways related to mitochondrial function, neuroinflammation, lipid and lysosomal biology, and protein homeostasis.
• Experience developing and applying robust cellular assays for target validation, pharmacological characterization, or compound profiling.
• Experience with disease-relevant cellular models and phenotypic endpoints applicable to neurodegenerative disease.
• Industry experience supporting target validation, in vitro pharmacology, or drug-discovery programs is beneficial.

Role Overview: We are looking for a commercially minded Director of Customer Success to transform and scale our Customer Success function. Cambridge Spark is entering an exciting new chapter of growth. We are winning some of the UK's largest enterprises, securing multi-million-pound commitments and helping organisations transform their businesses through AI and Data. You will be regularly partnering with both strategic and operational stakeholders from across the technology, people, and business teams on the customer side. Our GTM organisation has become a high-performing commercial engine. Customer Success is central to the next stage of that growth. You will lead an established CS team and shape it into a strategically led function that drives customer value and commercial growth at enterprise scale. You will build a function that establishes a world-class approach to demonstrating customer ROI, building strategic relationships with senior executives, and turning customer success into a measurable driver of revenue growth, customer engagement and client retention. With a rapidly expanding customer base amid strong commercial momentum this is a rare opportunity to build something of lasting importance and play a defining role in Cambridge Spark's next phase of growth.
Your mandate has the following core priorities:
• Commercial Transformation: Build a proactive motion that strengthens buying relationships, generates qualified expansion opportunities and contributes to revenue growth.
• Engagement and Renewals: Keep sponsors and learners engaged throughout their programmes, spot risk early, and secure renewals and repeat cohorts across our enterprise accounts.
• Customer Value Creation: Define, measure and communicate the business impact of our AI and Data programmes, turning customer outcomes into renewed and expanded investment.
• Team and Operating Model: Develop the current team, establish scalable processes and recruit enterprise-calibre talent to support our growth.
Key responsibilities:
Strategic Retention & Growth • Own the baseline, playing a key role in driving robust GRR/NRR across the client roster; helping to scale use cases carrying the highest customer value, and the greatest revenue opportunity for Cambridge Spark.
• Work with Delivery to track learner progress, completion and achievement across our apprenticeship and custom programmes, and act early where engagement drops.
• Build a Customer Success strategy that generates measurable CS-sourced pipeline and sales-accepted Customer Success Qualified Leads (CSQLs), working with Sales to turn opportunities into booked revenue.
• Develop multi-threaded relationships with L&D champions, business sponsors and C-suite leaders; turn successful customers into advocates and references.
Customer Value Creation & ROI
• Ensure your CSM team captures success criteria and business objectives during the sales process, and turn them into measurable success plans and structured handovers. • Drive strategic Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs) that evidence measurable impact, address challenges and identify where customers should double down or change direction.
• Build a data-led CS practice: capture data across the customer journey, use EDUKATE and delivery data to spot risks and improve the experience, and turn it into high-value client reporting and ROI evidence.
• Turn customer results into case studies, references and impact evidence that support renewals, new business and tenders.
Customer Success Leadership & Transformation
• Coach and elevate the existing CSM team in strategic discovery, executive communication, commercial judgement and performance; grow the team as the business scales.
• Set the standard for enterprise customer engagement, across all accounts and within our specialist sector teams.
• Build a disciplined operating rhythm, with clear KPIs, account plans, and accountability for performance.
Cross-Functional Leadership & Execution
• Establish a joined-up operating model between Customer Success, Sales and Delivery, with clear responsibilities and regular joint account planning prioritising early risk detection.
• Act as a senior strategic contact and escalation point for major enterprise accounts, balancing customer advocacy with commercial priorities.
• Contribute further by actively engaging in customer advisory initiatives, and public representation of Cambridge Spark, as and when required.
Candidate Specification: Essential
• Enterprise Customer Success leadership: A strong track record leading Customer Success or strategic account management in complex B2B organisations, ideally technology or technology-enabled services.
• Commercial credibility: Demonstrable success creating expansion opportunities, influencing revenue and navigating complex buying groups.
• Builder and change leader: Experience developing or materially transforming a CS function, rather than solely maintaining an established model.
• Value realisation: Able to turn customer objectives and operational data into credible ROI narratives and persuasive executive reviews.
• People leadership: Proven capability in coaching, hiring, setting high standards and managing performance.
• Operating discipline: Experience with QBRs, customer success plans, segmentation and cross-functional execution; comfortable in a fast-moving scale-up.
Desirable
• Background in enterprise SaaS, AI/data technology, consulting, professional services or workforce transformation.
• Experience designing CSQL or expansion motions; familiarity with MEDDIC or consultative sales qualification.
• Exposure to learning and development, professional education or UK apprenticeship funding.
What Makes You Different
You see Customer Success as a growth engine, not a reporting or support function. You are an excellent listener, commercially curious and able to connect learner outcomes to the priorities of senior business leaders.
You have raised the bar in a team before. You can coach a CSM, challenge an account strategy, present ROI to executives and navigate operational complexity and ambiguity at pace. .

• Leaders whose experience is limited to reactive customer servicing, satisfaction reporting or administrative account management.
• People who have only inherited mature CS operations and are uncomfortable building processes, coaching teams or driving change.

Background to our Organisation
We are an education technology company that enables corporate and government organisations to achieve their business goals by educating their workforce with critical digital transformation skills to succeed in the AI era.
We deliver unique and innovative professional education that is accelerating the digital transformation of our clients, advancing the careers of their employees, helping people get into work and closing the digital skills gap. We are in a sector that is crucial to the economy and workforce, with a lot of opportunity for change and innovation. We are at the cutting edge of teaching applied data and digital skills, with our unique patented learning platform EDUKATE.AI offering our clients and learners a unique learning experience. EDUKATE.AI was developed with support from Innovate UK and provides all of our learners with 24/7 immediate feedback on their work, helping accelerate the learning process and providing a sandbox environment to experiment on real world datasets.
Since 2016, we have supported more than 15,000 learners across four continents with nearly 550,000 pieces of code submitted for feedback on EDUKATE.AI. We are trusted by some of the most recognisable brands in the world to educate their workforce, including Microsoft, the NHS, GSK, easyJet, the BBC and John Lewis. Our focus on applied learning to create business impact sets us apart - individual learners have reported applying their skills at work to generate recorded value of up to £40m. Our Values

Entrepreneurial
We take initiative and show entrepreneurial spirit which fuels innovation at Cambridge Spark. This includes identifying opportunities for improvement, taking ownership for implementing solutions effectively and driving improvement by using proof of concepts to demonstrate the feasibility and value of their work.
Team Spirit
Everyone is part of building an open and transparent culture, communicating effectively to raise issues, discuss improvements and share the evidence used to make decisions.
Customer-focused
Our customers are at the centre of everything we do, inspiring us to create great work. We strive to build friendly, professional and lasting relationships with them to better understand and anticipate their needs.
Gold Standard
We are experts in our field and are constantly developing our technology and offering. We set the benchmark in our industry: both in what we offer customers and in how we deliver it.

At Camlin we believe in high quality engineering and design, allowing us to develop market leading products and services. In short, we love creating value for our customers by solving difficult problems. As of now, Camlin operates in over 20 countries worldwide.🌐
Role Description
The Mid-Level Firmware Engineer in the Real-Time Applications unit is a key contributor responsible for designing, developing, and optimizing cutting-edge solutions using DSP and Microcontroller technologies.
Role Responsibilities
· Design and implement real-time systems, including DSP algorithms and Microcontroller firmware, tailored to project requirements.
· Ensure firmware meets strict real-time performance constraints, focusing on latency, throughput, and efficient use of system resources (e.g. memory, processing power).
· Lead efforts in hardware/software integration to ensure seamless operation of real-time solutions.
· Optimize the performance and efficiency of signal processing algorithms and embedded systems.
· Conduct code reviews, design evaluations, and testing to uphold high-quality standards.
· Investigate and resolve complex technical issues in real-time systems, ensuring reliability and robustness.
· Debug hardware and software issues, getting to the root cause of the issue.
· Propose innovative solutions to technical challenges.
· Design high quality systems which comply with regulatory standards.
· Stay abreast of advancements in DSP and Microcontroller technologies to introduce innovative approaches to system design.
· Identify opportunities for process improvement and contribute to the optimization of workflows, tools, and methodologies. Contribute to the creation and maintenance of comprehensive technical documentation.
Essential Criteria
• 3+ years of professional experience in the design, simulation, implementation, verification and validation of real-time systems on DSPs and Microcontrollers.
• 3+ years of professional experience i in programming in C++ and C languages.
• 3+ years of professional experience with Real Time Operating Systems (FreeRTOS, Zephyr)
• Good knowledge of theory and design of complex digital electronic circuits and digital signal processing algorithms (FFT, digital filters, re-sampling, ecc.).
• Strong analytical and problem-solving attitude.
• Experience in the use of laboratory equipment (oscilloscope, logic analyzer, signal generators).
• Experience with peripheral standards and communication protocols (I2C, SPI, UART, RS485, RS232, RGMII, ecc.).
• Familiarity with scripting languages (e.g., Bash, Python).
• Proficiency in source code revision control, especially GIT.
• Good knowledge of agile methodologies.
• Fluent English communication skills, both written and verbal.
Desirable Criteria
• Good knowledge of SHARC or equivalent DSP architecture.
• Knowledge of FPGA architecture and design, as well as HDL languages.
• Good Knowledge of build systems (CMake).
• Proficiency with gitlab, docker, CI/CD, artifactory.
• Experience with application layer protocols, such as DNP, 1588, MQTT, and more.
• Knowledge of electronic components and PCB reworking.
• Experience with TCL scripting.
Our Values
• We work together
• We believe in people
• We won’t accept the ‘way it has always been done’
• We listen to learn
• We’re trying to do the right thing
Benefits:
• Competitive salary
• Company Pension & Life Assurance Schemes
• On-site parking
• Hybrid Working
• Subsidised Gym Membership
• Wellness programmes

Junior Project Engineer (Mechanical)
Full Time Permanent Lisburn Job Description:
Join our highly skilled and dedicated team committed to delivering high-quality, efficient high voltage monitoring solutions and ensuring exceptional customer satisfaction.
We are seeking a Junior Project Engineer who will be responsible for:
• Creating detailed customer engineering drawings.
• Developing comprehensive technical specification documents and checklists.
• Designing bespoke mechanically sound components, including hydraulic flange fittings.
• Collecting project requirements and understanding customer needs and preferences.
• Serving as a specialised point of contact for customer inquiries regarding our HV products.
• Produce accurate and detailed engineering drawings for customer projects.
• Develop and maintain technical specification documents and checklists.
• Ensure all designs, such as hydraulic flange fittings, meet mechanical integrity and safety standards.
• Collaborate with senior engineers and other departments to ensure project requirements are met.
• Support the implementation of HV monitoring solutions by providing technical expertise.
• Assist in troubleshooting and resolving customer issues related to project designs.
Qualifications: • A minimum 2:1 degree in Mechanical Engineering or a related discipline.
• Experience with CAD software packages (Solid-Edge preferably) including creating 2D technical drawings.
• Strong understanding of mechanical design principles.
• Excellent attention to detail and organizational skills.
• Good communication and teamwork abilities.
• Eagerness to learn and develop within a professional engineering environment.

Position: Manufacturing Engineer
Job Summary
As a Manufacturing Engineer, you will play a key role in supporting the operational performance, delivery, and continuous improvement of Camlin's innovative technology products. Working closely with Engineering, Operations, and Supply Chain teams, you will drive manufacturing excellence through process improvements, lean initiatives, and the successful introduction of new products into production.
This is an exciting opportunity for an engineer who enjoys solving complex manufacturing challenges, improving efficiency, and working in a fast-paced environment supporting electro-mechanical products used by critical infrastructure customers worldwide.
Responsibilities
• Collaborate with Engineering, Production, and Supply Chain teams to improve product manufacturing and production efficiency.
• Drive best-in-class manufacturing practices across Health & Safety, Quality, and Operational performance.
• Support the introduction of new products into manufacturing, ensuring Design for Manufacture (DFM) principles are embedded from the outset.
• Lead Lean Manufacturing, flow optimization, and 3S/5S improvement initiatives across production.
• Develop and implement production layouts based on lean manufacturing principles.
• Drive productivity, quality, and cost-reduction projects within the manufacturing environment.
• Identify, design, and maintain production jigs, fixtures, tooling, and assembly aids.
• Investigate manufacturing issues and lead root cause analysis and corrective actions.
• Support inventory reduction and waste minimization initiatives.
• Support TWI implementation (KATA, JI, SWARMS)
• Maintain manufacturing documentation, including work instructions, process documentation, and standards.
• Support operational excellence programmes and continuous improvement activities.
• Ensure production tooling, equipment, and calibration systems are maintained and fit for purpose.
Qualifications & Skills – Essential Criteria
• Degree qualified or HND/ HNC in Manufacturing, Mechanical, Electrical, Electronic Engineering, or a related discipline
• Experience working within a technical manufacturing, production, or engineering environment.
• Experience supporting electromechanical assembly and test processes.
• Knowledge of Lean Manufacturing principles and continuous improvement methodologies.
• Experience supporting New Product Introduction (NPI) activities.
• Strong problem-solving skills with experience of root cause analysis and corrective action implementation.
• Experience of working within Health & Safety requirements in a manufacturing environment.
• Strong communication, organisational, and stakeholder management skills.
• Good IT skills, including Microsoft Office applications.
Desirable Criteria
• Experience within electronics, electrical, industrial technology, or electromechanical manufacturing environments.
• Experience leading Lean, Kaizen, 5S, or process improvement projects.
• Knowledge of Design for Manufacture (DFM) principles.
• Experience with NCR, CAPA, RCA, 8D, or similar problem-solving methodologies.
• Experience supporting inventory reduction, process optimisation, or production efficiency initiatives.
• Exposure to TWI, KATA, SWARMs, or operational excellence programmes.
• Experience developing manufacturing tooling, fixtures, and assembly aids.
• Understanding of production test equipment and calibration requirements.
Our Values
• We work together
• We believe in people
• We won’t accept the ‘way it has always been done’
• We listen to learn
• We’re trying to do the right thing

Senior DevSecOps Engineer
Location: London | Practice Area: Technology & Engineering | Type: Permanent
Build the platforms that power secure, intelligent and scalable enterprise engineering.
The Role
At Capco, we're looking for a Senior DevSecOps Engineer to help design, build and modernise enterprise software delivery capabilities for leading financial services organisations.
You'll play a key role in developing a modern enterprise Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC) platform, with a focus on CI/CD automation, policy-as-code, security controls and cloud-native engineering.
This is a hands-on engineering opportunity where you'll translate architecture into production-ready capabilities, integrate complex enterprise technologies and support engineering teams in adopting scalable, secure delivery practices.
You'll also explore approved AI-enabled engineering tools and workflows to improve development productivity, automation and delivery quality, while maintaining appropriate human oversight, security controls and responsible AI practices.
What You’ll Do
• Build modern CI/CD platforms: Design, develop and implement enterprise GitLab SaaS CI/CD pipelines, reusable engineering patterns and automated workflows, leveraging approved AI-assisted engineering capabilities where appropriate to improve efficiency and quality.
• Embed security and governance: Implement policy-as-code, automated security and quality gates, change controls, SAST, DAST, secrets management and vulnerability management throughout the SDLC.
• Engineer cloud-native solutions: Build and integrate services across Azure, Kubernetes and Azure API Management, supporting application, cloud and data workloads, including Snowflake and Salesforce.
• Modernise enterprise engineering environments: Support migrations from legacy Jenkins, GitLab, SonarQube, Artifactory/Nexus and AWS environments, integrating observability capabilities using Grafana and Prometheus.
• Enable engineering teams: Translate target architecture into working production capabilities, develop reusable platform services and onboard engineering teams, promoting responsible AI-enabled workflows with appropriate review, auditability and human decision-making.
What We’re Looking For
• GitLab and Azure expertise: Extensive hands-on experience designing, building and operating enterprise GitLab CI/CD pipelines and Azure-based engineering solutions.
• Cloud-native engineering: Strong practical experience with Kubernetes, DevSecOps principles, infrastructure automation and policy-as-code.
• Security and governance integration: Experience embedding identity, security controls, automated testing, quality gates and compliance requirements into enterprise delivery pipelines.
• Enterprise modernisation: Demonstrated experience modernising complex engineering environments, integrating multiple technologies and delivering scalable, production-ready platform capabilities.
• Technical leadership and delivery: Ability to take architectural designs through implementation, collaborate with engineering teams and support knowledge transfer, with an interest in applying approved AI tools and automation responsibly to improve engineering outcomes.
Bonus Points For
• Experience integrating Azure API Management with cloud-native platforms and enterprise applications.
• Familiarity with Snowflake, Salesforce and engineering patterns supporting data-intensive workloads.
• Experience migrating from Jenkins, SonarQube, Artifactory/Nexus or AWS-based engineering environments.
• Knowledge of Grafana, Prometheus and enterprise observability practices.
• Experience using AI-assisted development tools or AI-enabled DevSecOps workflows, with an understanding of responsible AI, human review and appropriate security guardrails.
Why Join Capco
• Deliver high-impact technology solutions for Tier 1 financial institutions.
• Work in a collaborative, flat, and entrepreneurial consulting culture.
• Access continuous learning, training, and industry certifications.
• Be part of a team shaping the future of digital financial services.
• Help shape the future of digital transformation across FS & Energy.
Benefits
We offer a competitive, people-first benefits package designed to support every aspect of your life:
• Core Benefits: Discretionary bonus, competitive pension, health insurance, life insurance and critical illness cover.
• Mental Health: Easy access to CareFirst, Unmind, Aviva consultations, and in-house first aiders.
• Family-Friendly: Maternity, adoption, shared parental leave, plus paid leave for sickness, pregnancy loss, fertility treatment, menopause, and bereavement.
• Family Care: 8 complimentary backup care sessions for emergency childcare or elder care.
• Holiday Flexibility: 5 weeks of annual leave with the option to buy or sell holiday days based on your needs.
• Continuous Learning: Your growth, your way – minimum 40 hours of training annually. Take your pick: workshops, certifications, e-learning. Plus, a Business Coach assigned from Day One to provide one-on-one guidance to support your goals and development.
• Healthcare Access: Convenient online GP services.
• Extra Perks: Gympass (Wellhub), travel insurance, Tastecard, season ticket loans, Cycle to Work, and dental insurance.
Inclusion at Capco
We're committed to making our recruitment process accessible and straightforward for everyone. If you need any adjustments at any stage, just let us know – we'll be happy to help.
We value each person's unique perspective and contribution. At Capco, we believe that being yourself is your greatest strength. Our #BeYourselfAtWork culture encourages individuality and collaboration – a mindset that shapes how we work with clients and each other every day.

💳 Capital on Tap started because small businesses were underserved. Big banks were slow, their products weren't fit for purpose, and small business owners often couldn't access what they needed. We set out to fix that.
Today we're a financial platform - not just a credit card company. We offer a best-in-class business credit card, SME-focused spend management platform, a savings product that hit £1 billion in funds within its first year, and a growing suite of tools and financial products that make running a small business easier. 
1,000+ employees, £20bn in annual card spend, 200,000+ customers, 17,000+ Trustpilot reviews averaging 4.7 stars, and we're profitable. We’ve done a pretty good job so far, but we’re just getting started! 
📍 London / Porto | 🏢 2 days a week
The Team 🚀
You’ll join one of our platform teams (XP Platform, within Engineering). We build the foundations that every web and mobile app at Capital on Tap sits on: the design system and shared UI packages, the app shell, and core flows such as sign-in, settings and protected actions. Product teams build their features on top of this, so we set the patterns, prove they work, and help other teams adopt them.
Right now the focus is the Customer Portal, the signed-in experience our customers use every day. We work very closely with Design, talk to Product early about what’s coming, and partner with the Engineering Architecture Team on where the frontend is heading. We also run a monthly demo for the whole department to share what we’ve built.
The Role
This role is for an engineer who wants to make web development the focus of their career. You might be a backend or mobile engineer who has picked up some React along the way, or someone who has built a few things in their own time and wants to do it properly. You don’t need to be an expert yet. What matters is real interest in the web and the drive to get good at it.
You’ll join a team of experienced web and mobile engineers and learn the craft on real work, not side projects. You’ll pair with seniors, have your code reviewed by people who care about it, and over time take full ownership of features in packages that the rest of the department builds on. Because those packages are used by other engineers, you’ll learn to think about developer experience as well as what the customer sees.
You already know how Capital on Tap works, which products we have and how our teams fit together. That context is useful here from day one.
What You’ll Be Doing

Checkout.com http://Checkout.com built its name serving the world's largest enterprises. As our product range grows, that takes us from thousands of customers to millions.
At that scale, the decision about who we work with, and on what terms, can't be a manual review at the end of a sales process. It has to be a product. It decides how quickly a good business goes live, how much it costs us to serve them, and how confident our regulators and scheme partners are in us. We're looking for a senior Engineering leader to own that decision.
This team decides which businesses we can work with and on what terms. It covers business verification, screening, underwriting, ongoing monitoring and financial crime. It's a shared platform that serves every one of our businesses. Its users are our customers (directly, or through the platforms they sign up with) and, internally, our Risk, Compliance and Financial Crime teams and the analysts who run reviews and investigations.
Much of what we have today was built segment by segment and market by market, for a smaller number of large customers. The next chapter is one opinionated, configurable decisioning platform. Enterprise, platform and SMB customers should all run on the same foundations, with the right depth of checks and the right terms for each. That way a new product, segment or market doesn't mean rebuilding our controls, and this team isn't on the critical path for every launch.
ROLE OVERVIEW | RISK, VERIFICATION & COMPLIANCE
The remit covers:
- Risk decisioning: underwriting, risk tiering, exposure limits, reserves and settlement terms, and when to restrict or offboard, re-assessed across the customer lifecycle.
- Business verification: company, ownership, document, bank account and website checks, run once for every segment.
- Financial crime: sanctions and PEP screening, AML and transaction monitoring, and the controls, audit trails and reporting behind our regulatory obligations.
- Decisioning platform: the shared infrastructure that runs these checks automatically for every market and customer type.
You'll partner closely with the teams that own onboarding and identity verification.
ROLE OVERVIEW | REMIT AND RESPONSIBILITIES
You'll be comfortable building and scaling critical platforms in a regulated environment, where correctness, auditability and availability matter as much as speed. You'll balance two goals that are often in tension: making it fast and easy for good businesses to work with us, and keeping bad actors out and the business compliant.
This is a change role. You'll assess what we have, set a clear direction, and move us from segment-specific, analyst-led processes to an automated decisioning platform, without pausing the business while you do it. You'll do this in close partnership with Product, Risk, Compliance, Financial Crime and Legal, and with the leaders of the businesses that depend on the platform.
You'll directly lead an established team of engineers and managers of varying seniorities. Amongst other duties, you'll have impact across:
- Setting the technical vision and strategy for Risk, Verification & Compliance. That includes deciding what we build once and share, and what each segment, product or market configures.
- Building a decisioning platform that automates the decisions that don't need a human, safely, and sends the rest to the right analyst with the context they need. Our automation rate sets our cost to onboard and to serve.
- Making risk dynamic across the customer lifecycle. New businesses start on terms that match the signals we see: limits, reserves and settlement speed. - Making decisions explainable, so that customers, partners and our own analysts understand why a decision was made and what happens next.
- Giving Risk and Compliance the dials. Acceptance criteria, early-life controls and policy should be configuration that can be changed, tested and measured by cohort, not a code change.
- Keeping our financial crime controls ahead of growth. Screening and monitoring have to scale from large enterprises to a very large base of smaller businesses, through new channels, payment methods and products.
- Leading the design and delivery of verification, screening, underwriting and monitoring systems that are accurate, auditable and highly available.
- Representing Engineering in regulatory, audit, scheme and partner conversations where needed.

An Introduction to Codal
Codal is an award-winning web design and development consultancy that helps enterprise organizations solve complex problems and accelerate growth through elegant, data-driven digital solutions. Our areas of expertise include application modernization, eCommerce, UX/UI design, product strategy, data analytics, and artificial intelligence.
At Codal, you will collaborate with some of the most innovative organizations in the world and work on cutting-edge technologies that push the boundaries of design and software development. We promote long-term success, not just for our clients but for our team, helping you develop a professional roadmap that takes your career to new heights.
Codal is looking for a Solutions Architect who can look at a client's technology landscape, understand what's working, what isn't, and chart a credible path forward. You'll design and defend end-to-end solutions across software, systems, data, AI, and DevOps, translating ambiguous business goals into architectures that are practical to build and easy to evolve.
This is a hands-on and client-facing role. You'll move between whiteboard sessions with client executives, deep technical design work, and hands-on prototyping to prove out an approach before committing a team to it. You're comfortable weighing cost, timeline, risk, and maintainability against each other, then making a recommendation and standing behind it.
We expect this role to embody Codal’s principles of mindful excellence, insatiable expertise, diverse intuition, data-led curiosity, and candid leadership in how you lead technically, mentor your team, and engage with clients.
*Please note this role is 3 days onsite in our office in Lincoln.
Who You'll Be Working With
You'll work alongside client stakeholders, from engineering leads to executive sponsors, as well as Codal's project managers, designers, and delivery teams. You'll be involved from early discovery and pre-sales conversations through hands-on implementation and post-launch support.
Responsibilities
- Assess a client's existing technology landscape (software, systems, data, and infrastructure) and rationalize the pros, cons, and risks of what's in place versus what's proposed.
- Design end-to-end solution architectures spanning application, data, AI/ML, and DevOps concerns, and document them clearly enough for both engineers and executives to act on.
- Present and defend architecture recommendations to client stakeholders, including technical leads and executive sponsors, with support from Codal's delivery and account teams.
- Support discovery, technical planning, and pre-sales conversations, translating client goals and constraints into a scoped, deliverable technical approach.
- Create and maintain architecture decision records that capture the trade-offs considered and the reasoning behind each major decision.
- Guide engineering teams through implementation, staying hands-on where needed (prototyping, code review, unblocking hard technical problems) without holding up delivery.
- Evaluate emerging tools, platforms, and AI capabilities, and bring forward recommendations that would meaningfully improve a client's solution or delivery speed.
- Partner with DevOps, data, and engineering leads to align architecture with CI/CD, cloud infrastructure, and data platform realities on the ground.
- Mentor engineers and technical leads on architectural thinking, not just implementation, helping the broader team reason about systems, not just code.
- Support planning, estimation, and risk management across the project lifecycle, flagging architectural risk early.
What You'll Need to Be Successful
- 9+ years of hands-on software or systems engineering experience, including experience designing and owning architecture for complex, client-facing solutions.
- Understanding and ability to solve complex client problems that will impact client business.
- Proven ability to evaluate an existing technology landscape and make a clear, defensible recommendation, including build-vs-buy and platform trade-offs.
- Strong grounding across at least two of the following: application architecture, systems/infrastructure design, data architecture, AI/ML solutioning, and DevOps.
- Comfort learning a new domain or stack quickly (just-in-time), with enough hands-on ability to validate an approach yourself rather than only directing others.
- Experience presenting technical recommendations directly to clients, including non-technical and executive stakeholders.
- Hands-on experience with cloud platforms (AWS, GCP, or Azure), containerization (Docker, Kubernetes), and modern CI/CD practices.
- Solid understanding of databases and data platforms (SQL, NoSQL, and analytics platforms such as BigQuery).
- Clear, confident communication skills, and the judgment to know when to hold a position and when to adapt it.
- The drive to learn, adapt, and apply to the ever changing technology landscape.
Preferred Qualifications
- Experience in a consulting or professional services environment, including supporting pre-sales, proposals, or client discovery.
- Experience architecting solutions that incorporate AI/ML capabilities into existing products or platforms.
- Experience leading architecture review boards or similar governance processes.
- A track record of guiding teams through complex technical challenges and ambiguous requirements to a shipped outcome.
- Certifications in a cloud platform or AI such as AWS Solution Architect or Claude Certified Architect

Job Description
The Role
A Project Manager in the Information Technology (IT) sector is responsible for planning, executing, communicating and closing projects within the given time frame and budget. This role requires a blend of technical know-how, managerial acumen and interpersonal skills to lead cross-functional global teams and ensure successful project delivery.
Key Responsibilities
• Define project scope, objectives and deliverables in collaboration with senior management and stakeholders.
• Develop comprehensive project plans that include timelines, milestones, risk assessments and resource allocation.
• Identify project requirements and ensure all necessary resources are available for project execution.
• Conduct feasibility studies and cost-benefit analysis to support project approvals.
• Follow workload planning processes to register a project.
• Lead project teams comprising EUC, Cloud and Infrastructure, and SecOps Engineers, as well as Network and Voice Engineers and other IT professionals.
• Coordinate tasks, assign responsibilities, set expectations and ensure tasks are being completed.
• Monitor project progress and performance using appropriate tools and techniques (e.g. project dashboards, project cards, SharePoint site).
• Ensure that projects are delivered on time, within scope and within budget.
• Manage changes to the project scope, schedule and costs using appropriate verification techniques.
• Track project performance, specifically to analyse the successful completion of short and long-term goals.
• Meet budgetary objectives and make adjustments to project constraints based on financial analysis.
• Regularly communicate project status, updates and progress to stakeholders, including senior management.
• Facilitate meetings, workshops and presentations to keep all parties informed and engaged.
• Develop strong relationships with customers, vendors and other stakeholders to ensure their needs are met.
• Manage stakeholder expectations and ensure their involvement throughout the project lifecycle.
• Identify potential project risks and develop mitigation strategies to address them.
• Implement risk management processes to monitor and control risk factors continuously.
• Prepare contingency plans to handle unexpected challenges that may arise during the project.
• Escalate to the project owner/sponsor when needed.
• Ensure that project deliverables meet quality standards and customer expectations.
• Implement quality control processes to monitor the quality of work throughout the project.
• Conduct regular reviews and audits to ensure compliance with project requirements and standards.
• Conduct project evaluations and assessments at the end of each project phase.
• Compile comprehensive project reports that include lessons learned, success factors and areas for improvement.
• Ensure that all project documentation is completed and properly archived.
• Facilitate post-project reviews and feedback sessions with team members and stakeholders.
Knowledge, Skills and Behaviours

Job Description
Purpose of the job
The Scrum Master will support the SmartDelay team to establish a consistent, transparent and effective delivery rhythm, helping the team manage competing priorities, dependencies and live client demands while maintaining focus on agreed sprint outcomes.
This is a hands-on delivery role rather than a purely facilitative Scrum Master position. The role will work closely with Commercial and the SmartDelay delivery squad, including Business Analysis, Engineering and QA, to make work visible, improve planning and flow, remove blockers and ensure issues are surfaced and addressed early.
The successful candidate will be calm, credible and resilient, able to challenge constructively and bring clarity and delivery discipline in a complex environment without introducing unnecessary process.
Key Responsibilities
Sprint and delivery management
• Run effective sprint planning, daily stand-ups, sprint reviews and retrospectives.
• Ensure sprint goals, priorities and commitments are understood and visible.
• Track progress through the sprint and address slippage, blockers and dependencies early.
• Help the squad balance planned delivery with defects, production issues and urgent client demand.
• Reduce avoidable carry-over by ensuring incomplete work is understood, challenged and addressed rather than routinely rolling into the next sprint.
• Make changes to priorities or sprint commitments explicit, including the impact on existing work and delivery dates.
Backlog readiness and planning
• Work with Commercial, Business Analysis and the wider SmartDelay squad to ensure work entering a sprint is sufficiently understood, prioritised and ready.
• Improve backlog and sprint readiness by identifying unclear requirements, missing decisions and unresolved dependencies before work is committed.
• Support practical prioritisation where demand exceeds available capacity.
• Make trade-offs and capacity constraints visible so that changes in priority are conscious decisions.
• Ensure upcoming work is refined early enough to support effective sprint planning.
• Help Commercial and the squad understand the impact of new or urgent requests on existing commitments.
Team effectiveness
• Build a stronger and more predictable delivery rhythm across Commercial, Business Analysis, Engineering and QA.
• Facilitate difficult delivery conversations constructively where priorities, ownership or expectations are unclear.
• Challenge unhelpful delivery behaviours and ways of working without creating unnecessary conflict.
• Help establish clear ownership and follow-through on actions and decisions.
• Encourage accountability while maintaining a collaborative team environment.
• Create a working environment in which delivery issues can be raised early and dealt with openly.
• Reduce reliance on senior leadership to resolve routine delivery issues by helping the squad establish clear responsibility and effective routes to resolution.
Blockers and dependencies
• Identify blockers quickly and ensure there is a clear owner and route to resolution.
• Ensure blockers and dependencies are actively managed through to resolution rather than simply recorded.
• Escalate issues when the squad cannot resolve them within an appropriate timeframe.
• Coordinate dependencies across other Collinson teams and third parties.
• Ensure decisions and dependencies do not remain unresolved because ownership is unclear.
• Distinguish genuine blockers requiring intervention from issues that the squad can and should resolve itself.
Delivery visibility and reporting
• Maintain a clear and current view of sprint health, capacity, delivery risk and upcoming demand.
• Use Jira to provide accurate delivery visibility without creating administration for its own sake.
• Provide concise, evidence-based updates to Product & Delivery leadership.
• Identify recurring causes of delay, rework, interruption or carry-over and work with the squad to address them.
• Use appropriate delivery measures to support improvement and informed planning rather than target-driven reporting.
• Ensure committed work, emerging demand and capacity constraints are visible to Commercial and the wider squad.
• Help ensure delivery problems and risks are surfaced early, reducing late surprises for the squad and stakeholders.
Continuous improvement
• Use retrospectives and delivery evidence to identify practical improvements to flow and squad effectiveness.
• Help the squad establish sustainable and repeatable ways of working.
• Apply Scrum and Agile practices pragmatically, adapting them where necessary to improve delivery outcomes.
• Focus improvement activity on practical delivery problems rather than process for its own sake.
• Leave the squad with stronger delivery disciplines and less reliance on day-to-day intervention.
Knowledge, skills and experience required
Essential skills
• Strong practical knowledge of Scrum and Agile delivery, applied pragmatically rather than rigidly.
• Excellent facilitation skills, including the confidence to handle disagreement, ambiguity and competing priorities.
• Calm and resilient under pressure, with the ability to challenge constructively and maintain delivery focus.
• Strong planning and problem-solving skills, with the ability to identify and drive resolution of blockers and dependencies.
• Strong stakeholder management and communication skills across Commercial, Business Analysis, Engineering and QA.
• Able to make capacity constraints, delivery trade-offs and the impact of changing priorities.
• Confident use of Jira and practical delivery measures to support planning and visibility.
Essential experience

• Experience joining established teams where delivery flow, discipline or predictability needs strengthening.
• Experience working across Commercial or business stakeholders, Business Analysis, Engineering and QA within a cross-functional delivery squad.

Desirable experience

• Professional Scrum Master, Certified ScrumMaster, SAFe Scrum Master or equivalent practical experience.

Job Summary
Comcast is seeking an enterprise leader to build and lead an integrated organization spanning Data and AI Governance, Data and AI Architecture, and Data and AI Products.
The Executive Director will translate enterprise strategy into a coherent portfolio of trusted, scalable, and high-value data and AI capabilities. This leader will establish the standards and controls that protect the organization, define the architectures and platforms that enable scale, and develop data and AI products that deliver measurable value for customers, employees, and the business.
The successful candidate will be equally comfortable setting enterprise direction, operating across organizational boundaries, and building a high-performing multidisciplinary team. They will bring together governance, architecture, and product management as complementary capabilities—not separate functions—and create an operating model that enables innovation while maintaining appropriate security, privacy, quality, and responsible-AI safeguards.
Job Description
Key Responsibilities:
Enterprise Leadership and Strategy
• Define and execute the enterprise strategy for data and AI governance, architecture, and products in alignment with business priorities and the broader data and AI strategy.

Data and AI Governance
• Establish and continuously improve an enterprise-wide governance framework covering data, analytics, AI, and generative AI.
• Define decision rights, accountabilities, policies, standards, controls, and escalation paths across the data and AI lifecycle.
• Build a federated governance model that provides enterprise consistency while enabling business domains to move with appropriate autonomy.
• Partner with Legal, Privacy, Information Security, Compliance, Risk, Internal Audit, and business teams to embed regulatory and ethical requirements into everyday delivery.
• Oversee capabilities such as data ownership and stewardship, data quality, metadata and lineage, classification, access, retention, model governance, responsible AI, and third-party data and AI risk.
• Establish practical review and approval processes proportionate to the value, materiality, and risk of each use case.
• Develop metrics that demonstrate governance effectiveness, including improvements in data quality, policy adherence, control performance, model oversight, and speed to approved use.
Data and AI Architecture
• Define and maintain the target-state architecture for enterprise data, analytics, machine learning, generative AI, and related platforms.
• Establish architecture principles, reference patterns, technical standards, reusable components, and lifecycle-management practices.
• Ensure that architectures are scalable, interoperable, secure, resilient, cost-effective, and aligned with enterprise technology strategy.
• Guide decisions involving cloud and hybrid platforms, data integration, APIs, lakehouse and warehouse technologies, semantic layers, master and reference data, model platforms, AI agents, and MLOps/LLMOps.
• Reduce unnecessary technology fragmentation and technical debt while improving reuse, portability, and time to delivery.
• Partner with engineering, cybersecurity, infrastructure, application, and business architecture leaders to ensure end-to-end alignment.
• Chair or lead relevant architecture councils and provide timely, pragmatic guidance to delivery teams.
Data and AI Product Leadership
• Establish and mature product management practices for enterprise data, analytics, AI, and shared-platform capabilities.
• Develop a portfolio of reusable data and AI products tied to clearly defined users, business outcomes, service expectations, and product economics.
• Create transparent product roadmaps informed by enterprise strategy, user research, value potential, risk, feasibility, and organizational readiness.
• Ensure product teams own the full lifecycle—from discovery and prioritization through delivery, adoption, measurement, maintenance, and retirement.
• Define product health and value metrics, including adoption, customer satisfaction, business impact, reliability, quality, cost, and speed to insight or action.
• Partner with business leaders to identify high-value opportunities and establish shared accountability for adoption and realized benefits.
• Promote reusable products and platform capabilities over one-off solutions where doing so improves scale, speed, and economics.
Organization and Talent Leadership
• Recruit, develop, and lead a multidisciplinary organization that may include governance leaders, data stewards, architects, product executives, product managers, responsible-AI specialists, and portfolio professionals.
• Design the organization, roles, forums, and ways of working needed to connect governance, architecture, engineering, product, and business teams.
• Create a culture of clarity, accountability, collaboration, inclusion, constructive challenge, and continuous learning.
• Develop succession plans and career paths while strengthening the organization’s enterprise data, AI, architecture, and product-management capabilities.
• Set clear objectives and empower teams to make decisions within well-defined guardrails.
• Manage the organization’s budget, workforce plan, vendor relationships, and strategic partnerships.
Measures of Success
Success in this role will be demonstrated through outcomes such as:
• A clear and adopted enterprise strategy and operating model for data and AI governance, architecture, and products.
• Stronger alignment between business priorities and the data and AI investment portfolio.
• Increased adoption and measurable value realization from data and AI products.
• Improved data quality, trust, discoverability, lineage, and ownership.
• Responsible and timely delivery of AI capabilities with effective risk management and regulatory compliance.
• Greater reuse of shared data, models, platforms, architectural patterns, and product capabilities.
• Reduced duplication, technical debt, delivery friction, and unnecessary technology cost.
• Faster progression from business opportunity to governed, production-ready capability.
• A high-performing team with strong engagement, clear accountability, and a sustainable leadership pipeline.
Required Qualifications
• [12–15]+ years of progressive leadership experience across data, analytics, AI, technology, digital product management, or related disciplines.
• Significant experience leading multiple functions at enterprise scale, ideally including governance, architecture, product management, data platforms, or AI.
• Demonstrated success translating enterprise strategy into operating models, investment portfolios, roadmaps, and measurable business outcomes.
• Strong understanding of modern data and AI architectures, platforms, integration patterns, cloud ecosystems, analytics, machine learning, generative AI, and operationalization practices.
• Experience establishing data governance, responsible-AI, model-governance, privacy, security, and risk-management capabilities in a complex environment.
• Proven ability to develop and manage data, platform, analytics, or AI capabilities as products with defined users, roadmaps, service levels, adoption goals, and value measures.
• Experience influencing senior executives and aligning stakeholders across business, technology, legal, security, risk, and compliance functions.
• Demonstrated success building, developing, and retaining diverse, high-performing teams.

• Talent leadership: Sets high standards while fostering trust, inclusion, learning, and psychological safety.
• Change leadership: Navigates ambiguity, competing priorities, and organizational resistance with resilience and discipline.

The Workplace Product Owner is accountable for maximising the value delivered through Workplace products and services by translating business outcomes, colleague needs and technology priorities into a clear product vision, prioritised roadmap and actionable backlog.
Working closely with Workplace leadership, Delivery Managers, Design Lead, CTO, Cyber, Data, Service Operations and strategic vendors, the role ensures that Workplace initiatives are aligned to organisational strategy, governed appropriately and delivered to time, cost and quality.
 
The role owns product performance measures, adoption outcomes and benefits realisation, using insight and feedback to continuously improve the end-user experience, simplify ways of working and ensure Workplace products are secure, reliable, cost-effective and fit for purpose.
 
What you’ll do
 
Product Vision & Roadmap (20%): 
Define and maintain the product vision, outcomes and roadmap for Workplace products and services, including end-user devices, collaboration platforms, M365 services, identity and access, workplace facilities technology, endpoint lifecycle and workplace tooling. Translate organisational priorities, business needs and technology direction into an outcome-based roadmap with clear milestones, dependencies, benefits and measurable value.
 
Backlog Management & Prioritisation (25%): 
Own, shape and prioritise the Workplace product backlog, ensuring work is clearly defined through user stories, requirements, acceptance criteria, non-functional requirements and business value statements. Balance demand across strategic change, operational improvement, risk reduction, technical debt, regulatory requirements, adoption needs and end-user experience improvements. Ensure delivery teams have a transparent, well sequenced and delivery-ready backlog.
 
 Stakeholder Engagement and Business Alignment (15%): 
Build strong relationships across Workplace, CTO, Cyber, Data, Service Operations, Finance, Change, regional teams and internal customer groups. Understand business needs, user pain points and operational priorities, then translate these into clear product outcomes. Communicate roadmap progress, trade-offs, risks, dependencies and decisions so expectations are managed and business value is understood.
 
 
Delivery Support & Acceptance (15%): 
Work with delivery teams through discovery, design, build, test, release and adoption. Provide timely decisions, clarify requirements, support Agile ceremonies and formally accept outcomes against agreed acceptance criteria. Ensure operational readiness is embedded, including support models, knowledge articles, communications, training, monitoring, service transition, disaster recovery and business continuity considerations.
 
Governance, Risk & Financials (15%):

Ensure product decisions align to architecture, security, change, assurance and service management processes. Performance & Continuous Improvement (10%): 
Define and monitor product KPIs such as adoption, usage, colleague satisfaction, incident trends, service performance, time-to-deliver, cost-to-serve and realised benefits. Measurable improvements in Workplace KPIs (e.g., adoption, CSAT, incident reduction, time-to-deliver) and demonstrable benefits realisation.

Stakeholder management: ability to influence, negotiate trade-offs and align diverse groups (business, engineering, operations, security and suppliers)

Who are Eque2?
Eque2 provides specialist software for the construction and housebuilding sectors, helping businesses manage everything from estimating and financial management to commercial operations and project delivery.
We work with leading platforms including Microsoft, Sage and Xero, helping construction businesses improve visibility, stay in control and manage their operations more effectively. Today, we support over 3,000 construction businesses across the UK and Ireland, from growing contractors to large, complex organisations.
Role Purpose
To own and prioritise the delivery backlog for Eque2’s cloud estimating and cost-control product, translating product direction and validated customer needs into delivery-ready work. You will use AI-enabled development, design and product management tools to accelerate delivery and help build market-leading customer-facing Artificial Intelligence (AI) capabilities.
About the Role
We are seeking a Technical Product Owner to help shape the next generation of Eque2’s cloud estimating and cost-control software. Reporting to the Chalkstring Product Director, you will own backlog quality, prioritisation and day-to-day delivery decisions within the direction set by Product Management, defining clear requirements and testable acceptance criteria for Engineering and QA.
You will partner with Product Management, Product Design, Engineering and QA from discovery and rapid prototyping through to customer delivery and validation. You will use AI-enabled product, design and development tools to accelerate this process and play a central role in expanding Chalkstring with capabilities from our established EValuate product.
You will engage directly with customers to understand their processes, validate use cases, explore emerging AI opportunities and support acceptance testing, using customer and delivery evidence to inform product decisions.
Location: This is a UK-based hybrid role, with office access in Maidenhead and Newcastle-upon-Tyne. Travel is required for team, customer and stakeholder meetings, with office attendance expected 1–2 days per week.
Is this role right for you?
This is a hands-on product delivery role rather than a Product Management position.
You will have authority over the delivery backlog, priorities and day-to-day delivery decisions within the direction set by Product Management. Product Management retains ownership of overall product strategy, roadmap direction, pricing and market positioning.
This role will suit someone who enjoys being close to customers, Engineering and delivery, and who can turn broad product direction and complex customer needs into well-defined work that teams can confidently build and test.
Key Responsibilities
• Own and prioritise the delivery backlog within Product Management’s agreed direction, making trade-offs, dependencies and delivery decisions visible.
• Turn validated customer needs into delivery-ready epics, stories, workflows and acceptance criteria that Engineering and QA can implement and test without repeated clarification.
• Lead refinement and contribute actively to sprint planning and reviews, resolving ambiguity quickly and accepting completed work against agreed criteria.
• Engage directly with construction customers to understand estimating and cost-control workflows, validate use cases and edge cases, and support user acceptance and adoption.
• Use AI-enabled development, design and product management tools to accelerate research, requirements, prototyping and delivery while maintaining appropriate review, security and data controls.
• Identify and validate valuable customer-facing AI opportunities, defining quality thresholds, safeguards, human oversight and evaluation requirements for probabilistic features.
• Work closely with Product Design, Engineering and QA on workflows, data models, integrations, APIs, technical constraints and testability.
• Measure adoption, quality and customer outcomes; use evidence to guide iteration, priorities and recommendations to Product Management.
• Communicate progress, decisions, risks and dependencies clearly, and keep product documentation, release notes, Support and Customer Success briefings current.
Knowledge, Skills & Experience
• Demonstrable experience as a Product Owner, Business Analyst or in a closely related B2B SaaS delivery role.
• Practical experience owning and prioritising backlogs within an Agile delivery environment.
• A strong track record of translating customer and operational needs into clear user stories, requirements and testable acceptance criteria.
• Strong process, workflow and data analysis skills.
• Enough technical understanding to discuss APIs, integrations, data and dependencies confidently with Engineering teams.
• Hands-on experience using AI tools in areas such as product discovery, analysis, design, requirements or prototyping.
• An understanding of the quality, risk and human-oversight considerations associated with customer-facing AI.
• Confidence engaging directly with customers and communicating technical and product decisions to different audiences.
• An evidence-led, proactive and collaborative approach, with strong attention to detail.
• Experience using Jira or a comparable product delivery tool.
Desirable
• Construction estimating, quantity surveying or cost control.
• EValuate or other construction estimating software.
• AI, machine-learning or data-driven product capabilities within complex B2B workflows.
• AI prototyping, evaluation or observability tools.
• Low-code or no-code platforms or AI coding assistants.
• SQL.
• API tools such as Postman or Swagger.
• Process modelling, including BPMN.
Personal attributes
You are a practical, customer-focused Product Owner who enjoys turning complex operational problems into clear, deliverable outcomes.
You are comfortable getting into the detail with engineers while keeping sight of the customer problem and intended outcome. You ask precise questions, challenge assumptions and identify dependencies early rather than allowing ambiguity to reach Engineering.
You will be:
• Curious and evidence-led, using customer and delivery insight to inform decisions.
• Proactive and solutions-focused, comfortable resolving ambiguity and moving work forward.
• Commercially and technically credible, able to communicate confidently with customers, engineers and senior stakeholders.
• Collaborative and adaptable, working effectively across Product Management, Product Design, Engineering and QA.
• Quality-conscious, balancing pace and innovation with security, responsible AI use and customer trust.
The successful candidate will be:
• Highly organised, detail-oriented and effective at managing time and priorities.
• Professional, credible and confident when engaging with senior stakeholders.
• Proactive, solutions-focused and able to anticipate needs.
• Calm under pressure and adaptable to changing priorities.
• Trustworthy, discreet and demonstrates sound judgement.
• Collaborative, approachable and service oriented.
• A positive ambassador for the organisation’s culture, values and standards.
Measures of Success
Success in this role will be demonstrated through:
• Backlog readiness: priority work has a clear outcome, scope, acceptance criteria and dependencies before it reaches sprint planning.
• Requirement quality: Engineering and QA can implement and test work without recurring clarification, with requirement-related rework reduced over time.
• Delivery predictability: risks, dependencies and material scope changes are identified and communicated early.
• Customer validation: priority features are tested with representative customers and validated against defined needs and use cases.
• AI quality and safety: customer-facing AI capabilities meet agreed standards for quality, reliability, privacy, security and appropriate human oversight before release.
• Adoption and value: released capabilities have clear outcome measures, such as adoption, usage, satisfaction or operational improvement, which are reviewed after launch.
• AI-enabled productivity: AI tools demonstrably improve discovery, prototyping or delivery without weakening quality, controls or traceability.
• Operational readiness: relevant documentation, release notes and Support and Customer Success briefings are complete before launch.

We are proud to be an equal opportunities employer, committed to creating an inclusive environment where everyone feels valued, respected and has the opportunity to thrive.

## FAQ
What is blockchain? - Blockchain is a distributed, immutable digital ledger that records transactions across a network of computers, making it secure and resistant to tampering.
How does blockchain work? - Blockchain works by organizing transaction data into blocks, linking them cryptographically, and distributing copies across a network of nodes for verification and storage
What is a block in blockchain? - A block is a unit of data in a blockchain that contains transaction information, a timestamp, and a cryptographic hash of the previous block, forming a chain of information.
What is decentralization in blockchain? - Decentralization in blockchain means that no single entity controls the network; instead, it's maintained by a distributed network of computers, enhancing security and reducing single points of failure.
What is a consensus mechanism in blockchain? - A consensus mechanism is a protocol that ensures all nodes in a blockchain network agree on the validity of transactions, maintaining the integrity of the ledger.
What is the difference between public and private blockchains? - Public blockchains are open to anyone, while private blockchains restrict access to authorized participants. Public blockchains are typically more decentralized, while private ones offer more control and privacy.
What are smart contracts? - Smart contracts are self-executing contracts with the terms directly written into code. They automatically execute when predefined conditions are met, facilitating trusted transactions without intermediaries.
How is blockchain different from traditional databases? - Blockchain differs from traditional databases in its decentralized nature, immutability of records, and the use of consensus mechanisms for validation, providing enhanced security and transparency.
What is mining in blockchain? - Mining is the process by which new transactions are verified and added to the blockchain. Miners use computational power to solve complex mathematical problems, securing the network and potentially earning rewards.
What are the potential applications of blockchain beyond cryptocurrency? - Blockchain has potential applications in supply chain management, voting systems, healthcare records, digital identity verification, and intellectual property rights management, among others.
What is a hash in blockchain? - A hash is a fixed-size string of characters generated from input data. In blockchain, hashing is used to create unique identifiers for blocks and to link them securely in the chain.
How does blockchain ensure security? - Blockchain ensures security through cryptographic hashing, decentralization, consensus mechanisms, and the immutability of records, making it extremely difficult to alter or hack.
What is a node in a blockchain network? - A node is a computer that participates in the blockchain network by maintaining a copy of the blockchain, validating transactions, and relaying information to other nodes.
What is the block time in blockchain? - Block time is the average time it takes for a new block to be added to the blockchain. It varies between different blockchain networks and affects transaction speed and confirmation times.
How does blockchain impact data privacy? - Blockchain can enhance data privacy by giving users more control over their personal data, enabling secure and transparent data sharing, and reducing reliance on centralized data storage systems.
