About Us 
Hawk is the leading provider of AI-supported anti-money laundering and fraud detection technology. Banks and payment providers globally are using Hawk’s powerful combination of traditional rules and explainable AI to improve the effectiveness of their AML compliance and fraud prevention by identifying more crime while maximizing efficiency by reducing false positives. With our solution, we are playing a vital role in the global fight against Money Laundering, Fraud, or the financing of terrorism. We offer a culture of mutual trust, support and passion – while providing individuals with opportunities to grow professionally and make a difference in the world. 
Your Mission
As a Customer Data Scientist at Hawk, you're the person our customers trust to make their AML and fraud detection models actually work for them: tuned to their transaction patterns, defensible to their regulators, and provably effective in their own numbers. You sit inside the regional customer team, working directly alongside Customer Value Partners on live accounts, not behind a wall of tickets from a central data science function. Your work spans model and threshold tuning, deep analytical investigation into detection performance, and building the customer-facing narrative that shows exactly what's improved and why. You've done this in front of customers before, and you know the difference between a model that scores well in a notebook and one that survives contact with a real investigator's workload.
Key Responsibilities
Tune and optimize detection models and thresholds against each customer's live transaction data, balancing detection effectiveness against false positive load, not just against a benchmark dataset.
Investigate detection performance deeply: dig into missed cases, alert quality, and pattern drift, and turn what you find into concrete tuning or configuration changes.
Translate technical findings into customer-facing insight: build the analysis that shows investigator productivity gains, false positive cost reduction, and detection effectiveness improvements in language a customer's compliance and risk leadership actually uses.
Sit in the room with customers directly. Present findings, defend your methodology to a customer's own data science or compliance team, and answer the hard “why did the model do this” questions live.
Partner closely with your regional Customer Value Partners on account strategy, informing where the model needs to change to unlock the next stage of value realization or a renewal conversation.
Feed patterns and findings back into Hawk's broader model and product functions, distinguishing between “this customer needs local tuning” and “this is a systemic gap worth fixing centrally.”
Own the regulatory defensibility of the tuning decisions you make. Document your reasoning so a customer's audit or regulator review holds up.
Bring rigor to how you validate model changes before they go live: backtesting, sample review, and sign-off discipline that protects the customer's compliance posture.
Your Profile
5-7 years as a data scientist in a customer-facing role, presenting analysis and defending model decisions directly to clients. This is not an internal-facing engineering or product data science background; you've sat across the table from a customer before.
Real experience in AML, fraud detection, or financial crime analytics is required. You understand transaction monitoring, typologies, and what a false positive actually costs an investigator, not just what one costs on a confusion matrix.
Strong hands-on skills in the standard data science stack (Python, SQL, and whatever ML tooling you've used in production), but your edge is judgment under ambiguity: knowing when a model change is safe to make and when it needs a human in the loop.
Comfortable being the technical voice in a room with a customer's risk, compliance, or data science stakeholders, and holding your own when questioned.
A track record of translating model performance into business value a non-technical stakeholder can act on: not just accuracy metrics, but investigator hours saved, false positive cost avoided, and cases caught.
Genuine comfort with ambiguity and live production systems. You're not looking for a clean offline research problem, you're looking for the “why did this alert fire on a real customer's data at 2pm today” problem.
An ownership mentality. You don't wait for a ticket; you notice when an account's detection performance is drifting and you go find out why.
Bonus
Experience specifically in transaction monitoring or payments fraud detection at a bank, payment provider, or a vendor serving them.
Familiarity with explainable AI and rules-based hybrid detection approaches, since that's core to how Hawk's models work.

Senior Technical Support Engineer – CX Team

What We Do
At Heat Geek, we are tackling one of the UK’s biggest carbon contributors: home heating. Nearly 20% of all UK carbon emissions stems from home heating  – and that contribution is even bigger on a global scale. At Heat Geek, we are changing that. By simplifying a traditionally complex industry and revolutionising the technology used by installers, we’re making low-carbon heating mainstream. We have already prevented over 2,500 metric tonnes of carbon from entering our atmosphere as of May 2026, and we aren’t stopping there!
 
Join Us!
People are at the core of who we are and what we do. From decreasing homeowners’ energy bills to help with the cost of living, to empowering talented heating engineers to perform outstanding installations, to ensuring a greener world for all of us, we believe in the power of what we can all do together. – And we need passionate, talented, hard working people to be a part of this journey. 
The role
As our Senior Technical Support Engineer, you’ll be the technical lead in the Customer Experience team, resolving issues with underperforming heating systems. You’ll take on our most complex cases, set the standard for how we diagnose and resolve technical issues, and be the final escalation point when installers or homeowners face problems that need a deep understanding of heating systems.
You’ll oversee support for systems both before and after commissioning, bringing strong knowledge of thermodynamics and hydronics alongside hands-on troubleshooting experience. You’ll build and own the team’s knowledge base, coach and develop team members, and work with product, engineering and installation teams to turn recurring issues into lasting fixes. 
Key Responsibilities
Technical Escalation
• Own complex escalations from installers and homeowners end to end, leading root cause analysis and defining corrective actions through to resolution. Reassure homeowners and give expert guidance throughout, maintaining our 5-star service and outcomes.
• Agree remedial work with installers, ensuring solutions meet Heat Geek’s quality, regulatory and compliance standards.
• Use sound engineering, commercial and customer-focused judgement to decide when a site visit is needed, and hand cases over cleanly to field, commercial and engineering teams so they’re resolved quickly and efficiently.
Fleet Quality & Performance
• Build and own the in-life care service, including alert rules, severity tiers and triage SOPs for each issue type.
• Oversee monitoring run by the CX team, handle complex alerts
• Analyse fleet data to spot recurring failures
• Uphold Heat Geek’s technical standards and use front-line insight to improve design guidance, commissioning standards and processes.
Scalable Processes & Tooling
• Replace manual effort and reliance on individual expertise with processes that scale as the business grows.
• Own the technical accuracy of AI-assisted support tools, correcting outputs that diverge from Heat Geek’s approach.
Team Development
• Lead the technical development of the Upgrades CX team, identifying knowledge gaps and delivering training that sticks.
• Build and maintain a library of technical SOPs and a technical database that standardise how we handle issues, capture lessons from every case, and help both non-technical colleagues and installers resolve known problems without escalating
• Act as the team’s technical sounding board on unfamiliar or borderline cases.
Product & Business Influence
• Represent the installer voice across the business, gathering feedback through Featurebase, conversations and escalations, and presenting key themes at team meetings and sprint demos.
• Contribute meaningfully to the Heat Geek technical forum, gathering issues raised by the CX team and making sure they lead to positive changes across the business.
• Separate one-off problems from systemic gaps, and turn frontline insight into clear input for product and engineering.
Candidate requirements 
• Extensive technical knowledge of heating systems and associated regulations, with proven experience in fault finding
• Clear, structured communication, able to explain complex issues simply and give direct, technically credible feedback to installers and advice to homeowners
• Real world installation experience 
• Excellent customer-facing skills, with a level-headed approach under pressure
• Experience building and improving processes that scale
• Highly organised, with excellent attention to detail
• Ability to write clear, structured technical documents that can be followed and understood by both technical and non-technical readers
It’s a bonus if you have:
• Heat Geek Mastery Qualification
• Technical knowledge of Heat Pumps 
• Experience with a CRM system 
• Experience of working with AI integrated systems and automations
 
We believe great teams are built from different ways of thinking, learning, and living, and as such, we strive to build an organisation where people can show up as themselves. Even if you don’t tick every box listed above, but are passionate about the work that we are doing and believe that you can make a positive impact here, we’d love to hear from you. So please drop us a message or share more detail in your application!
Ways of Working + Benefits
This is a 3-day-in-the-office hybrid role where you will work with the team at our office in Sustainable Ventures in Waterloo, Europe's biggest climate tech hub. It's a 5-minute walk from Waterloo Station and an energising space for anyone working on climate change. And don’t get us started on the epic view!
 
Some of our measurable benefits include:
• £5,000 contribution towards your own heat pump installation
• Shares in the company, allocated under a tax-incentivised scheme
• Salary that’s evaluated regularly, and based on skills, impact, and role scope - not negotiation tactics
• Private medical & dental insurance
• Learning and development budget 
• Annual summer retreat
• Gym membership contribution 
• Season train ticket loan
• Cycle to work scheme
• Yoga, run club and social events with other sustainability startups in our co-working space
…alongside regular socials and regular collaboration opportunities with a team that’s passionate, hardworking, and kind.

About The Role
The Senior People Business Partner runs the People function day to day. You will keep the full employee lifecycle running smoothly, managing People Business Partners and the People Co-ordinator, and make sure managers get consistent, high-quality support.
Hippo is a fast growing UK digital consultancy of around 750 permanent staff and 300 contractors. Our People function is going through its own transformation, with AI and automation at the centre of it whilst also growing the size of the team. We want technology to handle the repetitive, transactional work, so that the team can spend its time on culture, coaching and the moments that need a human touch. This role is for someone who is excited by that shift and will lead the team in making it happen. Our values are pragmatic, human and ambitious and we as a team keep these at the heart of everything we do.
This is a hands-on leadership role. You will take on the most complex and sensitive casework yourself, while building the confidence and capability of the people around you.
Where the role sits
The role reports to the Head of People and directly manages the People Business Partners and the People Co-ordinator, indirectly managing 3 advisors and an administrator. Between them, the Senior Business Partner and the Business Partners cover the full breadth of partnering work, while the Co-ordinator supports the day-to-day running of People operations. How the partnering splits by business area or type of work will be agreed with the team and is likely to change as the business grows.
You will work closely with the Head of People, Talent Acquisition, and senior leaders and line managers across the business.
Key responsibilities
You will be accountable for the day-to-day running of the People function. In practice, that means:
• Running People operations. Oversee the employee lifecycle from onboarding to offboarding, including absence, pay and promotion cycles, HR processes and employee records. Make sure the work is accurate, on time and consistent.
• Complex employee relations. Oversee the ER processes, supporting the rest of the team and occasionally step in to lead the more sensitive and complex cases. Keep the team's casework to a consistent standard, and inform the Head of People about risks early.
• Leading the team. Line manage, coach and develop the Business Partners and the People Co-ordinator. Give them clear direction and priorities, share the workload sensibly, and hold them to account in a way that is firm and fair.
• Compliance and risk. Make sure People processes meet UK employment law, data protection requirements, our ISO requirements and Hippo's own policies. Ensure the team keeps policies and manager guidance up to date as legislation changes.
• Data and insight. Own the quality of people data in our core systems. Use AI-powered analytics and reporting to turn that data into clear recommendations for stakeholders at every level.
• Automation and improvement. Find repetitive or cumbersome work and replace it with automated or AI-assisted workflows. Document processes so they scale and do not depend on any one person.
• Culture, engagement and wellbeing. Use engagement data to shape a positive, progressive culture. Shape the development strategy and how such processes such as 360 feedback, psychometric assessments, mentoring and manager coaching feed into this.
• Business partnering. Build genuine relationships with senior stakeholders. Understand their people priorities and make sure the People function's plans and insights line up with what the business is trying to achieve.
• Planning and strategy. Help the Head of People shape and deliver the People strategy. Give reliable inputs on capacity, cost and priorities
Skills and experience that you need
How we expect you to work
At this level, the job is to enable others rather than do everything yourself. Here is what that looks like at Hippo:
Critical thinking. You define the real problem before the team starts solving it. You make timely decisions with incomplete information and say what you are assuming.
Taking responsibility. You are accountable for everything the team delivers, including work you did not do yourself. You commit the team only to what it can realistically deliver, then treat those commitments as promises. You pick up problems that sit between teams and own them until they are solved, and you make sure every piece of work has a clear owner.
Planning and organisation. You plan around people's real capacity, map what the work depends on, and manage those dependencies before they become critical. You protect your team from interruptions and unnecessary work.
Leadership and influencing. You give the team a clear sense of what matters and what comes first. You develop each person deliberately through stretch, honest feedback and coaching.
Change, growth and resilience. You watch the team's workload and wellbeing, stay calm when things go wrong, and make sure lessons lead to improvements that actually stick.
Skills and experience
You will be an experienced, CIPD-qualified HR generalist who has led a team and run day-to-day people operations in a fast-paced environment, ideally in consultancy or professional services. You will have:
• A strong record of handling complex and sensitive employee relations cases, and of coaching managers to handle their own.
• Experience of managing and developing people, including setting direction, giving honest feedback and having difficult conversations.
• Real confidence with data: collecting, analysing and presenting recommendations to audiences at different levels, using (or keen to quickly learn) AI-powered analytics and reporting tools.
• A working knowledge of UK employment law and data protection requirements, and the judgement to know when to seek specialist advice.
• Strong relationship-building and influencing skills, including with senior stakeholders.
• A willingness to challenge "the way we've always done it" and propose smarter, technology-enabled ways of working.
• A collaborative approach to working alongside peers on a shared remit.
What makes us great
Alongside working with some of the most talented people out there and on-top of a competitive salary, which we’re transparent about from the outset, you can also expect a range of benefits:
• Contributory Pension Scheme (Hippo 6% & Employee 2%)
• 25 Days Holiday plus UK Public Holidays
• Perkbox access for a wide range of discounts

• Financial and general wellbeing sessions
• Flexible benefits scheme with options of:
• Private health cover

• Wellbeing contribution
• Charity contributions
• Tree planting
Diversity, Inclusion and Belonging at Hippo
At Hippo, we’re dedicated to creating a diverse, equitable and inclusive workplace that works for everyone. We understand that having a diverse team unlocks our capacity for innovation, creativity and problem solving. Only by building a community of diverse perspectives, cultures and socio-economic backgrounds can we create an environment where all can contribute and thrive.

We are committed to providing an inclusive and accessible recruitment process that reflects our workplace culture. We are a registered Disability Confident Employer, Mindful Employer, Endometriosis Friendly Employer and a member of the Armed Forces Covenant. Hippo continually strives to remove barriers, provide accommodations and offer reasonable adjustments to ensure equity throughout our practices.
Hi, we’re Hippo At Hippo, we design with empathy and build for impact. We do this by combining data-informed evidence, human-centred design and software engineering. We're a digital services partner who is genuinely invested in helping our clients thrive as modern organisations. Our delivery methodology is truly agile, from concept to reality, supporting innovation and continuous improvement to achieve your desired outcomes.
We firmly believe that technology should serve humanity, not the other way around. We take a human-centred approach to everything we do because we understand that complex problems require a service design approach. This means understanding how users behave and ensuring our solutions work for them in the real world. Our combination of data, design, and engineering delivers bespoke digital services that make a positive and meaningful impact on organisations and society. Have a look through our Website at Our Story & Purpose, Our Culture & Values, Case Studies and Our Solutions & Services to find out some more!
Hippo Locations
We are headquartered in Leeds and have offices across the UK in Liverpool, Glasgow, Manchester, Birmingham, London and Bristol. ## About the Role
Senior Scrum Master – Agile Delivery Manager  Remote Permanent About HF  People. Not just lawyers  We’re not your typical law firm – we’re people with a passion for helping our clients and each other achieve the best possible outcomes. We are leading legal advisers to the insurance and commercial sectors across the UK & Ireland, known for our innovation, client focus, and long-lasting relationships. We do things differently, with a forward-thinking approach built around our clients’ needs, supported by cutting-edge technology and a culture built around people from a wide range of backgrounds who are taking an equally wide range of routes to building their careers in law. We are looking for an experienced and delivery-focused Senior Scrum Master / Agile Delivery Manager to lead a multidisciplinary Agile team delivering change across the Clio Operate platform. This is not a traditional Scrum Master role focused solely on facilitating Agile ceremonies. We need someone who will take real accountability for delivery, creating an environment where the team can perform effectively while ensuring commitments, risks, dependencies and blockers are actively managed. You will be expected to understand what the team has committed to, whether delivery is on track and, critically, why it is not progressing when expected. You will challenge constructively, remove obstacles, drive issues through to resolution and escalate where intervention is required. The successful candidate will combine strong Scrum Master capabilities with many of the responsibilities of an Agile Delivery Manager, providing the leadership, structure, transparency and momentum needed to help the team consistently get things done. What you’ll be doing • Take accountability for the team's delivery against agreed Sprint, PI and wider programme commitments. • Maintain a clear understanding of delivery progress, priorities, dependencies, risks and blockers. • Identify when delivery is falling behind and proactively establish the underlying cause. • Constructively challenge the team where progress, ownership or pace is below expectations. • Drive blockers and impediments through to resolution rather than simply recording or reporting them. • Escalate issues quickly and appropriately where resolution sits outside the team's control. • Work closely with Product Owners, engineering, testing, business SMEs and other delivery teams to resolve cross-team dependencies. • Maintain a strong focus on outcomes and completed work, not simply activity or ceremony. Agile & Scrum Leadership • Lead and continuously improve the team's Agile delivery practices. • Facilitate effective Sprint Planning, Daily Scrums, Refinement, Sprint Reviews and Retrospectives. • Ensure Sprint Goals are meaningful, understood and actively managed throughout the Sprint. • Lead effective PI Planning and delivery against committed PI Objectives. • Drive high standards around Definition of Ready, Definition of Done, estimation, capacity planning and backlog readiness. • Use retrospectives and delivery data to identify improvements and ensure agreed actions translate into measurable change. • Promote accountability and ownership within the team rather becoming the team's task manager. Delivery Management • Maintain a clear delivery plan and understand whether upcoming milestones and commitments  • remain achievable. • Proactively manage risks, issues, assumptions, dependencies and delivery constraints. • Coordinate dependencies across teams and workstreams. • Ensure emerging delivery risks are identified early rather than becoming last-minute surprises. • Work with the Product Owner to ensure the team has sufficient prioritised, refined and delivery-ready work. • Balance Agile principles with the practical realities of delivery within a complex enterprise programme. Metrics, Reporting & Governance • Own accurate and transparent reporting of team delivery performance. • Use delivery metrics to understand performance and support evidence-based conclusions. • Translate detailed delivery information into clear executive messages covering progress, confidence, risks, impact and required decisions. • Ensure reporting provides an honest view of delivery health rather than simply reporting that activity is taking place. What do I need? • Significant experience as a Scrum Master and/or Delivery Manager within technology environments. • Strong practical knowledge of Scrum, Agile and preferably SAFe. • Experience leading multidisciplinary teams including developers, testers, analysts, platform specialists and Product Owners. • An understanding of software delivery and the SDLC. • Experience managing delivery risks, dependencies, blockers and competing priorities. • Strong delivery reporting and analytical capability. • Experience using Jira or comparable Agile delivery tooling. • The ability to interpret delivery metrics and turn data into meaningful management insight. • Experience producing reporting for senior leadership and governance boards. • Strong stakeholder management and communication skills. Experience working with Clio Operate or comparable enterprise case-management/workflow platforms would be highly advantageous. What Success Looks Like • The team understands what it has committed to and delivers with increasing predictability. • Problems and blockers are identified early and resolved quickly. • Delivery slippage is understood, challenged and addressed rather than simply reported. • Risks and dependencies are visible and actively managed. • Product, engineering, testing and business stakeholders understand their responsibilities. • Senior leadership receives clear, accurate and concise information about delivery health. • Agile ceremonies have a clear purpose and contribute to delivery rather than becoming administrative exercises. • The team continuously improves how it plans, collaborates and delivers.
What’s in it for you? Apart from the competitive salary you’d expect, our package of benefits reflects our values of partnership, innovation, and being real people. We’re committed to creating a dynamic workplace where everyone feels supported, empowered, and part of our success. You’ll enjoy: • 25 days’ annual leave (rising to 30 with service) + Holiday Buy Scheme • Life Insurance & Income Protection • Private Medical Insurance & Healthcare Cash Plan • Employee Assistance Programme & Digital GP services • Pension Scheme • Electric Car Scheme  • Enhanced Maternity, Paternity & Adoption Leave • Hybrid & Flexible Working Options • Discounted Gym Membership & Employee Discount Hub • Flu & Eyecare Vouchers – and more! What next? If HF sounds like a place where you could belong, we'd love to learn more about you! Submit your CV here and we’ll be in touch if we have any opportunities that match your experience and interests. If we don’t have something right now, we’ll keep your details on file and may reach out in the future as part of our talent pipeline. As an equal opportunities’ employer, we're passionate about inclusive hiring approaches. When you apply, you'll be asked about any adjustments you might need to support the recruitment process. Let us know, and we'll do our best to support you.

Every engineer here is product-minded. You will talk to the people who use what you build, decide with product people what is worth building, and find out afterwards whether it worked.

The Senior level
Senior Software Engineer. You own a product area: its architecture, how it is staged, its quality bar, and working out with customers what is needed. Own the delivery of what you are given, from the first ticket to production, with tests, and be the person who fixes it if it breaks.
Talk to the people who use what you build, and use what you learn to shape and cut scope.

You’ve kept quality high without a peer reviewer, and other engineers have come to you for design review.

You own that team’s backlog, the discovery work behind it, the acceptance of what the team builds, and the conversations with the customers it is built for. You report to the CTO, and our product manager, who owns product strategy and the roadmap across the teams, supervises your work day to day.
This is a product role first and a coding role second. You also generate code with AI tools, mostly on the front end, at roughly the level of a junior to mid-level engineer. We expect you to build working prototypes and small features that an engineer then takes over. We do not expect back-end work, architecture or being on call.
Our teams are formed from the people we have at the time, so you are not being hired into a named team. You will work with the engineers in your team, the product manager, the CTO and our customer-facing colleagues.
In your first year, you will get a team running on your backlog without the CTO or the product manager stepping in, and you will have personally shipped front-end changes and prototypes that engineers took forward.

Key Responsibilities
Own your team’s backlog: decide what goes in, what stays out and what comes next, and keep it in order.
Run discovery with customers, so that what the team builds is something customers need and will use.
Turn messy requests, rules and processes into small slices of work with precise acceptance criteria that an engineer can build and a customer can recognise.
Accept the team’s work against the acceptance criteria.
Say no, or reshape the request, when a customer asks for something that does not fit, and agree a next step with them.
Build prototypes and small front-end features with AI tools, check what the tools produce, and hand the work to an engineer to take forward.
Work with the product manager so that your backlog fits the roadmap, and tell them early when it does not.

Who we’re looking for
You have owned a team’s backlog. You decided what was built next and what was not, you accepted the work, and you can say what you decided and why.
You have told a customer no, or changed what they asked for. You can say what they wanted, what you said and what happened next.
You find out what customers need before building. You can show us a time you did discovery and what it changed.
You turn messy requests, rules and processes into small slices with precise acceptance criteria. You can show us a time you did it, how you knew you had it right, and what you got wrong.
You build working front-end prototypes or small features with AI tools, in the last 12 months, and an engineer took them forward. You can say what you built and what the engineer changed.
You check what AI tools produce. You can describe a time the output was wrong and how you caught it.
You work well with engineers: you hand work over clearly and accept the finished work against what you agreed.
Knowledge of parking or of any one industry is welcome, but none of it is required.

What We Offer
Hybrid working, 3 days in the office and 2 days from home.
Real ownership of a team’s backlog and its customer conversations, with a product manager alongside you.
A small team and real influence over what we build.
A strong, high performing culture, with genuine influence over how that culture develops as Hozah grows.
A fully refurbished, modern office, right next to East Croydon Station (with a fully stocked kitchen, offering free breakfast, lunch and drinks!).

Hozah is a tech-led, award-winning company driving change in the parking industry and reimagining urban mobility. Our mission is simple but powerful: to transform parking into a seamless, automated experience, paving the way for smarter, more sustainable cities.

Role Overview
You will build the products drivers and car park operators use every day: ANPR camera enforcement, pay-by-web, Autopay, permits, a client console and a motorist account app, across about 160 sites, and the new products we build next. We are a small engineering team, and we form teams around the work from the people we have.

You will report to the CTO and work with a team that reviews each other’s work.

The Mid-level
Mid-level Software Engineer. You own features end to end: you shape them with a product person, build them, test them, release them and look after them once they are live. Own the delivery of what you are given, from the first ticket to production, with tests, and be the person who fixes it if it breaks.
Talk to the people who use what you build, and use what you learn to shape and cut scope.
Write acceptance criteria, and check a feature after release to see whether it was used and whether it worked.
Work in our existing codebase and its layering, and keep it consistent for the next engineer.
Use AI coding agents as part of how you work, and be accountable for everything you ship, however it was written.
Take part in the on-call rota and look after what you ship.
Review other engineers’ pull requests, and welcome review of your own.

You’re product-minded. In the last 12 months you’ve talked to real users or customers, and what you learned changed or cut the scope of what you built. You write acceptance criteria, you check a feature after release, and you can say whether something you shipped got used.

You review others’ pull requests, finding real problems and saying so well, and you change your own design when review shows you a better way.
You do not need a degree, a particular programming language, or Kotlin. Experience of Axon, Temporal, GCP, Kubernetes, Terraform, parking or payments is welcome, but none of it is required.

A team that works with AI coding agents every day and measures what they do for us.

ABOUT HYPEREXPONENTIAL (HX)
At hyperexponential, we're building the AI-powered platform that enables the world's most critical decisions in a $7 trillion industry - which risks to take, and how to price them. These are the decisions that shape real-world outcomes: whether rockets successfully launch into space, autonomous vehicles make it to market, or communities recover after major storms.
Until now, insurance has been making billion-dollar decisions using outdated tools. We're changing that. Our platform brings together data, AI, and human expertise to give insurers the fastest path from submission to decision - helping them move faster, act smarter, and take on more risk with confidence.
Backed by a16z, Highland Europe, and Battery Ventures, we're scaling globally - already trusted by nearly 50 of the world's largest insurers, with zero churn and billions in premiums flowing through hx.
What began as a single product in one market has rapidly evolved into a multi-product, multi-territory platform powering every stage of pricing and underwriting. AI is at the core of what we do - from building the world's first domain-specific AI peer programmer for insurance (think GitHub Copilot with a PhD in actuarial science) to shaping agentic workflows that reinvent how this industry operates.
What makes hx different is the people who build it. Here, impact isn't tied to title or tenure; it's defined by the challenges you take on and the discipline you bring. Surrounded by peers who stretch you, you'll do the best, hardest work of your life in a company engineered to endure.
If that sounds like you, join us in building what comes next.

The Customer and Consulting team sits at the heart of how hx delivers lasting value to its clients. As hx continues to expand across global carriers, reinsurers, and specialist MGAs, this team ensures that customers don't just adopt the platform, they transform the way they price and underwrite risk. Hyperlayer is the intelligent banking platform built for the agentic economy: the financial control layer that sits above banks' existing cores, enabling next-generation Smart Accounts, without ripping anything out. From a single integration, we give financial institutions a secure rules and orchestration engine that lets them design, launch and scale hyper-personalised products in weeks while preserving stability, compliance and control. And there's nothing like us anywhere in the world.
Hyperlayer works with Tier 1 and Tier 2 FIs across the UK, US, EMEA and Hong Kong, with an award-winning UK consumer app (HyperJar) sitting in the group. We're creating the fintech category that every bank in the world needs: programmable, governed, agent-ready accounts. Your job is to make sure our audiences know that.
About the Role
As Head of DevSecOps, you'll own the security, reliability and delivery of the platform that Tier 1 and Tier 2 banks build their products on. Sitting in our Engineering team and reporting to the CTO, you'll lead our DevOps engineers (a team of 4) and set the direction for how we build, ship and secure our infrastructure, with security built into every stage of the software lifecycle rather than added at the end. You'll also be a trusted voice for our banking clients, helping them feel confident in how we protect their data and keep the platform running. As we expand into new markets, the role will grow to cover a larger team and a broader security and resilience remit.
This is an office-based role, with regular in-person collaboration in the office.
What You'll Do
• Lead, support and develop the DevOps team, creating an environment where engineers can do their best work and grow their skills.
• Own the DevOps strategy and roadmap, embedding security controls such as code and dependency scanning, container scanning and secrets management into our CI/CD pipelines.
• Set the direction for our cloud infrastructure and infrastructure as code, keeping the platform secure, scalable and cost-effective.
• Oversee platform reliability, including observability, incident response, on-call, disaster recovery and business continuity testing.
• Lead our security certification and compliance work (e.g. ISO 27001, SOC 2, PCI DSS) and help us meet the operational resilience expectations of our regulated clients.
• Act as the technical security point of contact for clients and partners, handling due-diligence questionnaires, audits and penetration test findings.
• Work with Engineering, Product and IT to manage vulnerabilities, access and risk, and build a security-aware culture across the business.
• Keep the CTO and leadership team informed on security posture, risk and platform health.
Qualifications
• 7-15 years of experience in DevOps, platform or security engineering, including time leading or managing an engineering team.
• Hands-on experience with at least one major cloud platform (AWS, Azure or GCP), infrastructure as code (e.g. Terraform) and containers/Kubernetes.
• A track record of building security into CI/CD pipelines and the wider software delivery lifecycle.
• Experience working to security or compliance frameworks such as ISO 27001, SOC 2 or PCI DSS.
• The ability to explain technical risk clearly to non-technical colleagues, clients and auditors.
• Confident, everyday use of AI tools in your work, such as Claude, Claude Code or GitHub Copilot.
• Experience in FS, fintech or another regulated environment, particularly working with banks. • Familiarity with financial-sector resilience regulation such as DORA or the FCA operational resilience rules. • Security certifications such as CISSP, CISM or a cloud security certification.
• Experience with policy-as-code, zero-trust architecture or cloud security posture management tools.
• Experience scaling a team and its infrastructure through a period of fast company growth.
Using AI at Hyperlayer
Hyperlayer is hyper-focused on making the most of AI across every workstream, and DevSecOps is no exception. In this role, you'll use AI coding assistants such as Claude Code to speed up infrastructure-as-code and pipeline work, and AI tools to help triage vulnerability findings, summarise incident timelines and draft responses to client security questionnaires. You'll also help shape how we use AI safely across Engineering, setting sensible guardrails for tooling, data and access.
Working at Hyperlayer
We value our team and are proud to offer some great benefits:
• A performance-based employee bonus scheme.
• 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays, a day off on your birthday, and an additional day per year of tenure to a maximum of 30.
• Critical illness and life insurance cover.
• AXA PPP Health Insurance, including gym offers.
• Cycle-to-work scheme.
• Referral bonus scheme.
• Workplace nursery scheme.

Applicants must have the right to work in the UK. We are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this role unless stated otherwise.
Equity, diversity, and inclusion
Hyperlayer's mission is to make a positive impact on people's lives, making it easier for everyone to manage their money.
Hyperlayer's commitment to equity, diversity, and inclusion is a key part of this; it helps us better serve our customers, employees, and business partners from every background.
We are constantly learning and striving to do better, and we expect all staff to actively take part in this process.

## About the role
## ****What You’ll Do****
- ****Coordinate a Single-Track Roadmap****: Serve as the primary point of contact between the UX team, engineering, product management, and other stakeholders, aligning everyone to one overarching roadmap.
- ****Plan & Track with Jira****: Use Atlassian Jira as the central project management tool, setting milestones, tracking progress, and ensuring on-time delivery.
- ****Define Project Scope & Goals****: Collaborate with leadership and stakeholders to clarify requirements, set objectives, and outline deliverables for each phase.
- ****Risk Management & Problem-Solving****: Identify potential bottlenecks, issues, or conflicts early, proposing solutions to maintain momentum.
- ****Cross-Functional Collaboration****Cross-functional collaboration
- ****Stakeholder Communication****: Provide regular updates on project status, challenges, and successes to technical and non-technical stakeholders.
- ****Mentor & Lead****: Encourage best practices in project organization and teamwork, fostering an environment of ownership, accountability, and proactive problem-solving.
### ****Projects You’ll Work On****
As part of our User Experience team, you will focus on the most important family of products Hypervolt creates for its customers:
- ****UltraGrid****: Our core backend engine for serving hundreds of thousands of connected homes with real-time data. UltraGrid is a connectivity layer that facilitates grid balancing and integration with some of the world's largest VPPs and energy retailers.
- Built to allow rebalancing the grid and sustain EV adoption at mass scale, UltraGrid aims to be a masterpiece of performance engineering, deeply focused on performance and cost, while streaming 100,000 telemtries daily from each connected household.
## ****What We’re Looking For****
- ****Experience at the Highest Level of Professional Software Development****: While this is not a coding role, you should be able to collaborate closely with “super hardcore” engineering teams and navigate complex development projects.
- ****Startup Background****: Previous experience in a startup environment is highly valued; you should be comfortable operating with less structure than in a large corporate setting.
- ****Tier-1 Software company background****: Our engineers come from Tier 1 software companies, such as Google, Twitter, and Netflix, organisations where software quality and performance matter. You will need deep experience interacting with experienced engineers and complex requirements.
- ****Consumer-Facing Products****: A proven track record of successfully managing projects for products at scale (experience with large-scale consumer tech is a plus).
- ****Technical & Customer Insight****: You understand technology deeply and recognize what our customers want, translating user needs into actionable product goals.
- ****Fast-Growing Environment****: Ability to thrive in a rapidly scaling, fast-paced company, juggling multiple priorities and projects simultaneously.
- ****Green Energy Enthusiasm****: Bonus points if you’re passionate about electric cars, energy transition, or sustainability initiatives.
## ****Benefits****
- ****Competitive Salary & Generous Stock Options****: Be rewarded for helping us grow and succeed.
- ****Hybrid Working Policy****: 3 days a week in our prime offices in Canary Wharf London, and flexibility to work from home the rest of the time.
- ****Diverse International Environment****: English is the company's ****primary language****, and our team is spread across different countries and cultures.
- ****Professional Growth****: Career advancement and professional development opportunities ****in**** a fast-growing company.
- ****Inclusive Environment****: Join a diverse, inclusive team that values collaboration and innovation.
## ****Our Values****
### Be persistent
What we aim to do is not always going to be easy, and problem-solving, no matter how big or small, is essential if we are going to achieve our mission. Whether it be a technical challenge you are struggling to unblock, a new client you are trying to win or a logistical puzzle you need to solve, the only way we will grow as a company and as individuals is by being persistent in working things through to a solution. Success seldom comes from the first attempt, but it almost always comes from the 1000th, and the difference between success and failure often isn’t persistently or the aha moment or the brilliant idea: it’s having the perseverance to continue pushing and never giving in to failure.
### Be accountable
We operate in a fast-paced, highly collaborative and increasingly autonomous environment at Hypervolt. We are on the journey from a scrappy startup to a true market contender, but no matter how big the company gets, treat it as your own. Be accountable for its progress, and look after it as you would your creation. If you know things can be improved, articulate them, say them, and don’t go along in the silence of knowing we could have done better. If we make a mistake, find a way to say it. There’s no value in keeping it to yourself; we will succeed or fail together.
### The ‘Ello Sir Ethos
We should always aim to treat people the way they want to be treated and always remember the “voting” power of customers. They are the actual boss and real “employer”—the market.
### Dare to dream
Every technological advancement we use today was once a crazy dream that a few persistent pioneers truly believed. “Most things have to be seen to be believed, but some things have to be believed to be seen!” – Steve Jobs, on building the Apple Mac, the best-selling computer of all time.
### Stay hungry, stay foolish.
The hunger and ambition for continuous success are the orbital solar beam-powered reactor at the core of our success, and our ability to stay foolish and humble and continue to let ourselves be educated by our market will help us reach the full potential of our ambition. Only through the most selfless dedication to our dreams will we achieve the most selfish of successes.
### True Greatness is Blind
Great ideas and execution can come from anyone and anywhere at any time.

We believe games and interactive media are on the verge of a fundamental shift.
Today’s experiences are largely scripted, characters follow predefined paths, and player choice is limited. We’re building systems that change that: digital actors that can think, communicate, and take action in real time.
Our goal is to create worlds that are truly alive—where stories emerge from interaction, and every player experience is unique.

• Take ownership of features throughout their development, and act as an ambassador for the features you own
• Ensure the final delivery of features are fun, engaging, and meeting the expectations of our fanbase
• Develop feature prototypes to test and iterate on ideas early
• Ensure productive playtesting, fix reported bugs, and secure Director validation
• Iterate upon live experiences using direct player data and community sentiment

• Proven game design experience on a high-profile console or PC title

• Experience prototyping game features

• A highly collaborative developer

# ABOUT THE JOB
We are looking for an Senior Substation Engineers – Primary Plant Engineer to join the team of Energy in our offices Manchester. IDOM is a global engineering consultancy with a strong reputation in the energy sector. In the UK, we are growing to support utilities with substation projects, bringing our experience from major projects around the world from power grid and renewable energy to hydro pumped storage plants, synchronous condenser plants, interconnectors, and other critical infrastructure.
Primary Plant Engineer. Core responsibilities:
- Lead HV/EHV substation physical design (layouts, busbars, equipment arrangement)
- Perform sag & tension calculations, busbar sizing, and earthing system design
- Review and approve GA drawings, single-line diagrams, and cable routing plans
- Ensure compliance with UK utility standards and project specifications
- Provide technical leadership and client interface for utilities.
- Act as main technical contact for clients and coordinate with multi-disciplinary teams.
At IDOM, we offer you the opportunity to participate in national and international projects as part of a team where you will have the support to push your professional boundaries and improve your skills every day. - Work-life balance
- Long-term career path
- Opportunity to become a partner

- Opportunity to take on more responsibility

- Strong interpersonal relationships

As a Business Development Manager at IES, you will play a critical role in driving our mission forward by engaging with key stakeholders across the Architecture, Engineering and Construction (AEC) industries.
Reporting to the Head of UK & Ireland, you will lead sales efforts and customer success across UK accounts, promoting solutions that enable significant reductions in energy consumption and carbon emissions across the built environment. IES Live represents the next chapter of our growth story, bringing real-time operational intelligence and digital twin technology to buildings in operation and connecting design-stage performance modelling with how buildings actually run. IES has traditionally led the building design market through the VE platform, trusted by engineers and consultants worldwide. IES Live extends that leadership into building operations, creating a powerful bridge between predicted and actual performance.
As a strategic pillar of our product portfolio, IES Live enables us to support customers across the entire building lifecycle, from initial design and simulation through to real-world operation and continuous performance improvement. This creates a significant market opportunity for both IES and the individuals who join the team.
We are now transitioning IES Live from an emerging business into a global growth engine. This is a unique opportunity to join at a formative stage, help shape our commercial success, influence the future direction of the business and play a visible role in building a market-leading proposition. For ambitious individuals, the role offers significant scope for personal growth, increased responsibility and the opportunity to develop alongside a business with substantial long-term potential.
We are seeking an outstanding sales leader to own and accelerate the commercial growth of IES Live globally. This is a senior leadership appointment with a clear and deliberate progression pathway. For the right individual, the role will evolve into full Business Unit Leader accountability for IES Live, encompassing P&L ownership, product strategy input and cross-functional leadership.
You will define and execute the go-to-market strategy, build and lead the commercial team, and personally engage with the market's most strategic accounts. Working closely with Product, Marketing and Executive leadership, you will establish IES Live as the category leader in operational building performance.

**Commercial Leadership**
- Own the global revenue target for IES Live, with full accountability for pipeline, forecasting and commercial discipline.
- Refine and execute the go-to-market strategy, including segmentation, pricing input, routes to market and partner and channel models.
- Personally lead engagement with major strategic accounts, building long-term C-suite relationships and positioning IES as a trusted, long-term partner.
- Identify, structure and pursue strategic partnerships that expand IES Live's customer base and market presence.
**Team and Organisational Build**
- Recruit, lead, coach and develop a high-performing sales team, operating a player-coach model during the build-out phase.
- Establish scalable sales processes, qualification rigour, such as MEDDIC or MEDDPICC, and performance frameworks.
- Collaborate with Customer Success to support retention, expansion and net revenue retention growth across the installed base.
**Business Unit Development**
- Develop divisional growth plans and budgets in partnership with the CRO and CFO, building towards full P&L accountability.
- Work with the Product Team to feed back customer and market requirements, understand the roadmap and represent IES Live on the Product Strategy Committee.
- Partner with the Chief Customer Officer to ensure a co-ordinated sales and marketing strategy, including sector collateral, case studies and thought leadership.
- Monitor market dynamics, competitor activity and emerging opportunities, adjusting strategy to maintain a competitive edge.
- Represent IES at industry events, conferences and networking forums globally, building brand presence and strategic alliances.
### Essential Skills and Experience
- Experienced senior commercial leader with proven success in outcome-based energy services and technology sales.
- Comfortable navigating complex, multi-stakeholder deals and sales cycles typical of building owner and operator procurement for energy services and associated technology.
- Demonstrable success owning and exceeding significant revenue targets, ideally in energy software and services, PropTech, smart buildings or related technology markets.
- Proven ability to build and manage a sales team, including recruiting, coaching and developing people through a growth phase.
- A zero-to-scale track record, having built a new product or offering and its pipeline from scratch, for example from zero to £500k-£1m in annual revenue, in a start-up or new product launch environment rather than taking over an established offering.
- An outcome-based selling mindset, with experience selling measurable energy savings and performance outcomes to building owners, operators, facilities managers and real estate portfolios, rather than focusing solely on software licences.
- Experience creating and operating partnership and channel sales models alongside direct sales.
- Ability to engage credibly at C-suite level and translate technical propositions into compelling commercial narratives.
- Strong command of sales performance metrics, forecasting and pipeline analytics, with the discipline to act on them.
- A high degree of commercial acumen, with the ability to identify market gaps, shape strategy and capitalise on opportunities.
- Strong emotional intelligence and communication skills, both internally and with customers.
- A proactive approach to continuous professional development, staying ahead of industry trends and emerging technologies, including the practical application of AI in sales.
- Genuine ambition and capability to progress into general management or business unit leadership.

About IonQ: 
IonQ, Inc. [NYSE: IONQ] is the world’s leading quantum platform and merchant supplier - delivering integrated quantum solutions across computing, networking, sensing, and security. IonQ’s newest generation of quantum computers, the IonQ Tempo, is the latest in a line of cutting-edge systems that have been helping customers and partners including Amazon Web Services, and AstraZeneca achieve 20x performance results and accelerate innovation in drug discovery, materials science, financial modeling, logistics, cybersecurity, and defense. In 2025, the company achieved 99.99% two-qubit gate fidelity, setting a world record in quantum computing performance.
Headquartered in College Park, Maryland, IonQ has operations in California, Colorado, Massachusetts, Tennessee, Washington, Italy, South Korea, Sweden, Switzerland, Canada, and the United Kingdom. Our quantum computing services are available through all major cloud providers, while we also meet the needs of networking and sensing customers across land, sea, air, and space. IonQ is making quantum platforms more accessible and impactful than ever before.  
Role Overview
Role:
We are looking for a Principal Software Architect to join our Compute Software organisation at IonQ. In this role, you will be responsible for developing and maintaining the architecture of the software that enables a quantum computer, from low level hardware control up to developer programming interfaces, contributing to the team’s mission of delivering a complete software product for a quantum computer.
You’ll play an important part in shaping the software and tools that support our work in building the world’s most advanced quantum systems. Our architecture now needs to evolve to support the next generation of our systems, and you will lead that work.
Responsibilities:
In this position, you will develop the software architecture covering real-time and non-real-time hardware management, low level orchestration and user interfaces for the current product and the future roadmap of products. You will also work with the technical leads from the development teams to support the effective development and delivery of a scalable solution that supports internal experimental scientists and external customers.
You’ll have the opportunity to develop an evolving software architecture to support a family of products, contributing directly to the success of the system software team in delivering a world leading quantum computer. You will coach and train technical leads in good architectural principles, and work closely with the infrastructure, firmware and compiler teams across the UK and the US.
Key responsibilities include:
• Development and documentation of the system software architecture
• Managing the evolving architecture across a family of products
• Coordination with other architects across the whole of software and the wider system
• Research and analysis to support future requirements elucidation
• Coordination with technical leads to ensure that the design and implementation meets the intention of the architecture
Requirements:
To be successful, you will need prior experience of developing a large and scalable software architecture covering real-time requirements and distributed processing. We’re looking for someone who can think strategically at the architecture level, solve challenging technical issues, track the latest industry good practice and tools, and communicate those ideas and technologies to the wider software team.
You will work at the level of the whole system, describing each component, what it does and its constraints, and then handing the detailed design and implementation to the development teams rather than designing through code. A grounding in formal architecture methods and principles such as cohesion, coupling and encapsulation will help you succeed, as will experience of evolving an architecture that has to grow with the product. Our immediate focus is system software and lower level control; experience further up the software stack is an advantage.
You’d be a great fit with:
• More than 10 years of software development experience, with more than 5 as a software architect
• A clear understanding of software architecture principles
• A background in real-time software development
• Experience working on software projects written in Rust

job_title: Senior Site Reliability Engineer, AI-DNA, $100k/year USD
job_description:
When the alarm fires, you are the first responder — but by the time you reach it, the AI agents you built and maintain have already validated hypotheses against years of prior incidents, parsed the logs and code paths, found the failure pattern, and proposed — or applied — a remediation inside policy guardrails. Your job is the shift and the agents that run it: take the page, resolve what the agents could not, and make sure the next page of that kind handles itself. You operate an AI-native community and social engagement platform that the world's largest brands run their customer relationships on — where one outage is a brand-damaging event for a Fortune 100 company, so the standard is set there. You are a senior SRE who could run the whole operation by hand; the way this team works, you bake that expertise into the agents and runbooks instead of spending your life in a ticket queue.
## What you will be doing
- Own the shift as first responder — take the page, triage and resolve customer-impacting incidents on the platform you cover, and escalate to the tech lead when the blast radius warrants.
- Execute production changes safely — deploys, cost-optimization runbooks, and config changes from other teams run through the quality gates with a rollback ready before you start, and you pull it the moment a change goes off-plan.
- Build, operate, and maintain the AI agents that do the operations work — pre-triage, change-validation gates, permanent-fix chase, RCA drafting, auto-healing — and write the AI and human runbooks they run on. The harness is the product.
- Execute the ticket work — but measured on how well your agents make it scale, not how many tickets you personally close. Every one-off you solve by hand, you generalize so an agent handles the next one.
## What you will NOT be doing
- Closing tickets as the goal. Throughput is not your scoreboard; the leverage your agents create is. Hours into a queue instead of into the agents that drain it means you are off-strategy.
- Waiting to be told what to do. You pick up the page, find the next gap, and ship the fix. Nobody assigns you your day.
- Solving the same problem twice by hand. A one-off you do not generalize is unfinished work.
- Treating this as a credential or a résumé line. The bar is ownership, depth, and obsession — not titles. If you have never been deeply, sustainedly obsessed with a hard problem, this is a bad fit.
## Responsibilities
- Own the shift and the outcome on it — like a founder. You are first on the page. When something is down on your watch, that is your problem; you do not sleep peacefully through a customer outage.
- Build, operate, and maintain the agents that run the operation. New agents that catch a class of incident before it recurs, existing ones tuned higher, guardrails added when production teaches you something the spec missed. You build within the architecture the tech lead sets — and push back with a better idea when you have one.
- Protect production every time you touch it. When you run a deploy, a cost-optimization runbook, or a config change, you go through the quality gates, keep a tested rollback ready, and pull it the moment the change goes off-plan. You are a guardian of uptime, not only a responder to its loss.
- Find the root cause — not the symptom — and close the loop. A disciplined, structured investigation that separates symptom from cause; then the part most teams skip — identify the prevention, build it, and track it to done. The tech lead reviews your RCAs; you write them to a bar that needs little correction. An RCA whose fixes never ship is theater.
- Generalize relentlessly. You may solve a one-off to restore service, but you do not stop there — you turn it into an agent, a runbook, or a guardrail so the next occurrence handles itself. The scoreboard is what the agent surface can carry, not how fast you close tickets.
- Multiply the team, and write so the work survives you. Fix the underlying agent when it fails and share the fix as reusable rules, context, and skills; encode every procedure so an agent can retrieve it and the next responder is never starting cold. In an async team, an undocumented fix is a fix that doesn't exist.
## Requirements
- 5+ years operating SaaS at scale as a senior, on-call SRE — real first-responder time on production incidents, not just project or build work.
- Extreme ownership, fully self-directed. You run your shift like your own business, and you can answer "the hardest you have ever worked on something" with a story we can probe for an hour. Nobody assigns your day or checks your work; you challenge a standard with a better idea but never quietly ignore it. This team does not babysit — if you need to be managed, it is the wrong fit.
- Deep production scars — outages, incident management, hands-on troubleshooting. First on the bridge, diagnosis under pressure, the failure modes known from having lived them. Deep AWS at scale (multi-AZ, multi-account; not Azure-only, not greenfield); you run production change with gates and tested rollbacks and investigate to the actual root cause, symptom separated from cause. You could run it by hand — the point is you bake it into the agents.
- AI-native operator who multiplies. You delegate whole units of work to agents that verify their own output, fix the underlying capability when they fail, and share it so the team levels up — measured on leverage, not AI-usage %. Advanced across agentic tools (Claude Code, Codex, Warp, custom agents); when a new model ships, you are testing it that day, not next quarter.
- AWS Solutions Architect – Associate (or higher) — or a production track record that makes the certification redundant. Scars over badge, but a useful floor at this level.
- Fluent / advanced English — precise under pressure, on the bridge and in writing.
- Shift coverage is core, not occasional — on-call rotations and the shift window you are hired into, with the time-zone overlap that window requires. Reliability is a 24/7 outcome for the whole team, and you carry the share in your geographical area.
- OFAC-clear country of residence.
## Nice to Have
- Pioneer or builder voice in agentic SRE / AIOps — original posts, talks, open-source, or agents and tools you have built and shipped. - - Followers and reposters are not what we are looking for.
- A documented obsession with one hard thing outside of mainstream work — depth matters more than the title on the latest role.
- Modern observability / incident-response stacks (Grafana, Prometheus, OpsGenie, PagerDuty, Datadog) and Azure exposure alongside your AWS depth.
- Background in multi-tenant B2B SaaS at scale — community, social, customer-experience, observability, or AIOps platforms.
## What you will learn
- You will become one of the engineers who actually built agentic SRE — not read about it — on a platform the world's largest brands depend on, where AI agents are full members of your team and the runbooks you write run themselves. You will leave with hands-on agent-ops and incident experience the rest of the industry is still trying to hire.
## Working conditions
- Enterprise scale, startup cadence. Large-enterprise customers, footprint, and contractual stakes; a startup operating model — outcomes measured week over week, decisions in days, the playbook rewritten as the field moves. If you need a year to land the framework from your last role, this is not it.
- No token or tooling limits. The harness is the product, and we resource it that way — if the right answer is more compute, a better model, or a tool we have not bought, we buy it.

Kids Planet is an independent, family run group of nurseries providing the highest standard of nursery care across the UK.
What if your next job meant more than just work, what if it meant shaping futures, every day?
Kids Planet is a proud family-run business, we do things with heart and we’re passionate about giving every child the best possible start. No two settings are the same, but all of them are built around our shared values: care, curiosity, and a genuine love for early years.
Join Kids Planet as a People Advisor Coordinator!
Reporting to: People Relations Manager
Role Purpose
The People Advisor Coordinator plays a key role within the People Advisory Team, providing first-line coordination and administration of employee relations activities. The role is responsible for managing tickets, ensuring requests are prioritised appropriately, assigned to the correct advisor, accurately updated throughout their lifecycle. In addition, the role supports the People Team by producing regular ER reports, analysing trends, and identifying themes that support proactive people interventions and continuous improvement.
Key Responsibilities
Case & Ticket Management
• Act as the first point of contact for incoming ER Tickets.
• Review, triage and categorise all people tickets relating to the Advisor team within agreed service levels.
• Assess urgency, risk and priority levels and allocate cases to the appropriate People Advisor or People Business Partner.
• Ensure all tickets contain accurate and complete information before assignment.
• Maintain the People case management system and ensure records are updated throughout the case lifecycle.
• Record case outcomes, lessons learned and key data points to support reporting and trend analysis.
• Escalate high-risk or sensitive employee relations matters where appropriate.
Data Management & Reporting
• Maintain accurate ER Case records and case management data.
• Produce monthly ER reports and dashboards.
• Collate data relating to absence, employee relations cases, turnover, recruitment, disciplinary, grievance and performance management activity.
• Analyse trends and patterns within ER data and highlight emerging risks or opportunities.
• Provide insights and recommendations to the People Relations Manager based on data trends.
Continuous Improvement
• Identify recurring themes within people cases.
• Assist with audits and quality reviews of people records and case documentation.
• Support system improvements and enhancements to people processes.
• Ensure confidentiality and compliance when handling sensitive employee information.
Person Specification
• Excellent organisational and prioritisation skills.
• Ability to assess and prioritise competing requests based on risk, urgency and business impact.
• Strong attention to detail and data accuracy.
• Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities.
• Ability to identify trends, themes and opportunities from people data.
• Ability to manage confidential and sensitive information appropriately.
• Proficient in Microsoft Office, particularly Excel, Word, Outlook and Teams.
• Experience working in an HR, People Administration, Shared Services, Employee Relations, Coordination or Customer Service environment.
• Experience using HR, ticketing, case management or workflow systems.
• Experience producing reports and analysing data.
Why Kids Planet?
• Great Place to Work Certified 2025/26
• Ranked #1 UK Best Workplaces for Women, for the second year running
• Crowned NMT’s Large Nursery Group of the Year, for the second year running
• Awarded one of the UK's Best Workplaces in Education & Training by Great Place to Work 2026
• 80% Childcare Discount – T&Cs apply
What’s in it for you?
• Life Insurance cover and access to a health plan.
• Free breakfast, lunch, and healthy snacks to fuel your day!
• Accredited training through our awesome KP Academy and bespoke training platform.
• Enhanced leave for maternity, paternity, fertility, and adoption because family matters.
• Wellbeing goodies, staff rewards, and fun events all year round.
• Long service awards to celebrate your commitment.
• Take the day off on your birthday, it’s all about you!
• Competitive salary, pension plan and enhanced holiday allowance.
Like the sound of joining our family?
Apply today to be a People Advisor Coordinator with Kids Planet!
We are unable to offer any kind of visa sponsorship for this role.
We embrace everyone. Our goal is to create a truly inclusive culture and diverse workforce. We break down barriers so you can be your authentic self and flourish!
Kids Planet is dedicated to safeguarding and promoting the well-being of children and young people. An enhanced DBS check will be required for this role. We expect all staff and volunteers to uphold this commitment, and safeguarding training is a fundamental part of every role. All colleagues are required to complete regular training to ensure they understand and fulfil their responsibilities. A Disclosure and Barring Service Certificate is mandatory for all positions, and this role will be subject to enhanced checks as part of our safeguarding duties.
Kids Planet is committed to equal opportunities for all. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all our staff and children. Applications are encouraged regardless of age, disability, sex, gender reassignment, sexual orientation, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief and marriage and civil partnerships.

Exciting Career Opportunity as a Workshop Engineer at STILL Materials Handling in Exeter.
Join STILL Materials Handling, a global leader in forklift trucks and warehouse equipment, and become part of a team that values innovation, collaboration, and excellence.
Working with everything from small pallet trucks, through to IC trucks, Reach Trucks and VNA trucks and automated trucks, you will be required to find, diagnose, and rectify faults, and undertake preventative maintenance on STILL forklifts and other material handling equipment within our Workshop
We offer:
At STILL Materials Handling, we believe in rewarding our people. Your package will include:
• Competitive salary based on experience
• 39.5 hour working week, generally 0800-1630, Mon-Thursday & 0800-1600 on Fridays
• 25 days annual leave plus statutory bank holidays
• Company pension scheme (5% employer contribution, minimum 5% employee contribution)
• Overtime opportunities
• Access to discounts from major UK brands

• Able to work both independently and collaboratively as part of a wider engineering team.
• Highly organised, proactive, and self-motivated, with a positive, can-do attitude and strong problem-solving skills.
