Demonstrate resourcefulness across a variety of research techniques, including library, online, archive and market research.
Identify inspiring references for silhouette, proportion, fabric, colour, print, texture, garment construction and finishing.
Maintain a strong understanding of the luxury fashion landscape, identifying opportunities to introduce fresh perspectives whilst remaining true to the Mulberry brand.
Share research, knowledge and inspiration with the wider design team, supporting a collaborative and informed approach to design development.
Design
Design and develop the Women’s RTW collections, working under the direction of the Design Director to interpret the seasonal creative direction and translate it into a cohesive, distinctive and commercially relevant product offering.
Take ownership of design projects from initial concept through to final product, ensuring consistency of vision and quality throughout the development process.
Demonstrate strong creative judgement and the ability to develop original design ideas that balance innovation, wearability and commercial relevance.
Experiment with silhouette, proportion, fabrication, garment construction and detailing to create distinctive and varied collections.
Demonstrate confidence in developing ideas three-dimensionally through draping, toile development, garment manipulation and collaboration with pattern cutters and technical teams.
Apply an in-depth understanding of garment construction, fit, fabric behaviour and finishing to inform and strengthen design decisions.
Ensure individual designs proposals work cohesively within the wider collection, contributing to a balanced and considered product offering.
Present design concepts and proposals clearly and confidently, articulating the rationale behind creative decisions.
Responsibilities
Ensure all designs are communicated effectively through accurate technical drawings, CADs, specifications and construction details, for the atelier and suppliers.
Manage workload and prioritise projects effectively, ensuring the critical path is adhered to, and all key deadlines are met.
Work collaboratively with the wider design, technical and production teams to ensure design intent is maintained throughout the product development process.
Maintain accurate records of design development, sample comments and amendments throughout the season.
Support the Junior RTW Designer in prioritising workload, improving technical accuracy and developing confidence and independence in their role.
Prototypes and Fittings
Take responsibility for ensuring prototypes and samples are developed and delivered in line with the critical path, working closely with product development
Lead or contribute to fit meetings and sample reviews, assessing garment fit, proportion, construction, fabric performance and overall appearance.
Provide clear, considered and technically accurate feedback to product development / suppliers, ensuring amendments are communicated efficiently and effectively.
Work collaboratively with pattern cutters, garment technicians and suppliers to resolve complex fit and construction issues. Demonstrate strong technical judgement when assessing samples, balancing creative intent with garment functionality and wearability.
Refine and improve designs throughout the sampling process, ensuring the final product reflects the original creative vision and meets the required quality standards.
Specifications and Production Handover
Work closely with the production development and technical teams to ensure product specifications are accurate, commercially viable and suitable for production handover.
Produce and oversee accurate technical sketches and CADs, ensuring all amendments following fittings and sample reviews are incorporated.
Ensure garment measurements, construction details, fabrications, trims and finishing specifications are clearly and accurately documented.
Culture:
Embrace and demonstrate the Mulberry values and behaviours: honesty, dynamism, and a community-oriented spirit.
Support Mulberry to deliver an inclusive culture, through behaving in a way that is open-minded and respectful towards others, and understanding that your views, opinions, and experiences may not always be shared by your colleagues.
Act as an ambassador for Mulberry and communicate positively about the brand.

As a certified B Corp, we are committed to using business as a force for good. You’ll be encouraged to incorporate environmentally and socially responsible practices into your work, supporting our Made to Last strategy across Climate, Circularity, and Community.
Help foster a culture where diversity is celebrated and every individual feels valued, respected, and included. Champion equity, empathy, and understanding in all interactions - internally and externally.
Skills & Knowledge:
Appropriate degree in Fashion Design or a related discipline, supported by a strong portfolio.
Proven experience designing and developing a RTW collection from initial concept through to production at a similar level.
Strong understanding of garment construction, pattern cutting principles, fit and technical specifications.
In-depth knowledge of fabrics, trims and garment finishes, with a strong appreciation of quality, craftsmanship and luxury product development.
Demonstrable ability to take creative ownership of projects, exercise independent design judgement and translate seasonal direction into commercially relevant product.
Experience supporting, mentoring or guiding junior members of a design team.
Confident communicator, able to present and articulate ideas clearly, both verbally and visually.
Collaborative and approachable, with the ability to build positive working relationships across the business and within the RTW team.
Adaptable and comfortable working within a fast-paced, evolving design environment.
Self-motivated, proactive and resourceful, with a strong sense of accountability.
Highly creative, with a strong individual approach to design and a clear understanding of the Mulberry aesthetic.
Computer Skills
Proficient in Adobe Creative Cloud and other appropriate CAD programmes.
Computer literate in Excel and Outlook.
Strong online research skills, including the ability to identify relevant design references, emerging trends and market opportunities.

Collections agents only work in production when someone owns the build in detail. Each one handles regulated conversations, sensitive customer situations and payment outcomes, and has to behave correctly every time.
Forward Deployed Engineers own that build. They turn a customer's collections strategy, policies and systems into a working agent, prove it in a POC, and take it to full production. About the role
As a Forward Deployed Engineer, you own the technical execution of AI agent builds for our enterprise customers, mainly banks and large lenders. You scope with the customer's technical and operations leads, design the agent, build and test it, and launch it on their systems. After launch, you own the agent's performance: you analyze production data, explain results to the customer, and decide what to change in the agent and the contact strategy. Each deployment should leave behind patterns, tools and tests that make the next one faster.
You'll be based in London and lead enterprise deployments for banks and large lenders in the UK and Ireland.
In this role, you will
• Own end-to-end delivery of enterprise agent builds, from POC scoping through implementation, evaluation and production launch.
• Define the agent operating procedures (actions, guardrails, escalations) with the customer, and turn them into agent behavior.
• Design and engineer the prompt and agent logic that drives identification, negotiation and payment conversations, across languages and channels.
• Configure Murphy to fit each client’s needs on how and when to reach debtors: call windows, retry and frequency rules within each country's regulations, channel mix (voice, SMS, RCS, WhatsApp), payment links and hand-offs to human agents.
• Build evaluation and simulation harnesses, plus regression tests against real call outcomes, to catch errors and drift before customers do.
• Build, validate and maintain integrations with customer systems: core banking, collections platforms, data pipelines, telephony.
• Diagnose failures from transcripts, traces and logs, find the root cause, and fix it in the agent or flag it to Engineering.
• Analyze production performance (contact rates, promises, payments, funnel) with SQL and dashboards, explain changes to the customer, and turn findings into agent or strategy improvements.
• Work with senior technical and operations stakeholders at the customer to define success metrics and deliver against timelines.
• Support Account Executives with technical discovery and demos for strategic deals.
• Turn recurring lessons into reusable templates and playbooks, and help train newer FDEs.
Your background looks something like this
• 5+ years in a technical customer-facing role: forward deployed engineering, solutions engineering, implementation engineering, technical consulting or technical product management.
• You write code and SQL, work with APIs and build integrations end to end.
• Hands-on experience building with LLMs: prompting, evals, guardrails, harnesses, tool use.
• You've delivered production systems for enterprise customers that needed structured testing and iteration.
• You explain technical decisions clearly to senior stakeholders and turn requirements into a delivery plan.
• You're comfortable in fast-moving, ambiguous situations where you shape the solution as much as you build it.

Patterns, standards and non-functional requirements

As a Product Manager within the Data Privacy Products team, you will play a crucial role in ensuring that our products and services comply with global data privacy regulations and best practices across the Global Streaming Platform (GSP). Global Dormancy Manager (GDM) is a core privacy product that identifies dormant accounts and initiates the deletion across operational systems.
In this role you will combine strong analytical and technical expertise with product manager responsibilities. Your primary focus will be owning and maturing GDM, defining its roadmap and evolving the capability as deletion needs grow. Alongside this, you’ll contribute to the wider deletion strategy, helping shape how GDM fits into our end-to-end approach to data deletion across the business.
You will work closely with Product, Legal, Compliance and business stakeholders to define priorities, manage delivery, improve reporting processes, and ensure that the team continue to meet developing business requirements in relation to data deletion.
Responsibilities
• Define and maintain the GDM product vision, strategy and roadmap.
• Identify future product improvement opportunities including automation, reporting and deletion orchestration across the wider data ecosystem, with the aim of achieving product parity and maturity across business propositions.
• Partner with Legal, Compliance and Data Governance teams to establish and maintain deletion policies, dormancy rules and retention requirements.
• Define requirements, user stories and acceptance criteria for new capabilities and enhancements.
• Work closely with engineering, architecture and programme teams to deliver roadmap commitments.
• Own the end-to-end product backlog and prioritization.
• Prioritize product enhancements based on regulatory requirements, risk reduction, operational efficiency and business value.
• Drive the evolution of GDM from a deletion engine to a scalable enterprise data lifecycle management capability, ensuring effective integration between related privacy capabilities.
• Act as the product subject matter expert for dormancy deletion requirements and controls.
• Support audits, regulatory enquiries and compliance reviews relating to deletion processes.
• Communicate progress, risks, blockers, and key decisions to stakeholders while building trusted cross-functional relationships.
QUALIFICATIONS
Basic Requirements:
• Previous experience in data protection, product management, or a related field.
• Knowledge of global privacy regulations, including GDPR, CCPA, and industry-specific standards.
• Hands-on technical experience with software management (e.g., PowerBI, Tableau)
• Previous experience working with compliance-related matters (e.g., privacy and security standards, consumer protection risks)
• Tangible experience designing and implementing data governance frameworks and controls in cloud-based environments – preferably with a focus on consumer data in a large media organization
• Bachelor’s degree in Information Security, Data Science, Law, Computer Science, or a related field. A Master’s degree or privacy certification (e.g., CIPP, CIPM) is a plus.
Desired Characteristics:
• Strong analytical skills with the ability to interpret complex privacy regulations and apply them to product development.
• Excellent communication skills, with the ability to convey privacy concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences.
• Detail-oriented with strong organizational and project management skills.
• Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced environment.
• Understanding of data privacy principles, privacy-by-design, and privacy engineering.
• Familiarity with product development lifecycles and agile methodologies.
• Experience working successfully with stakeholders and partner teams to translate business needs into product requirements.
• Strong written and verbal communication skills
• Ability to thrive in ambiguity and manage multiple tracks of work.
• Adaptable and ability to learn quickly.

THE ROLE As a Carbon Analysis Engineer at Neutreeno, you’ll take ownership of automating how our emissions and decarbonisation insight reaches customers. You’ll sit at the intersection of emissions science, agentic workflows and data engineering, turning the outputs of our novel methodologies for measuring greenhouse gas emissions across complex industrial processes into carbon and performance insights, accurately and at scale. Working across diverse sectors from jet engine production to energy infrastructure and pharmaceutical manufacturing, you’ll collaborate with our data science, modelling and customer-facing teams to replace manual data validation and processing effort with production-grade pipelines, and to make sure every figure that reaches a customer is one we can stand behind. This is a role for someone who thrives in a dynamic, fast-paced startup and enjoys automating complex workflows by building AI agents; analysing datasets to uncover and resolve irregularities; managing multiple workstreams and priorities; and continuously learning at the intersection of engineering, climate science and AI. This position operates on a hybrid work model with 3 days per week in our Cambridge office. Fully remote arrangements will be considered for outstanding candidates, provided there is sufficient overlap with UK working hours. THE WORK YOU’LL DO • Own the current measurement pipeline: interpretation, extraction and validation of customer-provided supply chain and manufacturing data, as well as verification of emission modelling assumptions and outputs. • Deliver end-to-end automation of the customer data pipeline (ingestion -> extraction -> validation) turning a semi-manual process into a scalable, fully automated, auditable pipeline. • Design, build, deploy and maintain AI agents that automate data extraction, validation and analysis that use the process engineering-based tools that you will develop (mass and energy balance, energy benchmarking, etc.). • Team up with cross-functional partners to shape new reporting features, translating technical breakthroughs into functionality that helps customers identify, track and amplify decarbonisation wins across their entire value chains. Requirements
THE MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS YOU NEED • Bachelor’s or master’s degree in chemical engineering or mechanical engineering or a related field. • 0-2 years professional experience in building agentic workflows. Professional experience is preferred, but a strong, relevant fourth-year degree project is more than acceptable. • A solid understanding of industrial processes, energy systems and mass flow analysis. • 1+ year of experience in Python-based tools: placements, internships and substantial projects on building pipelines and reusable tooling rather than one-off analysis scripts. • Familiarity with CI/CD practices: GitHub, linting, automated tests and integration tests as part of the PR workflow. • Hands on experience using LLMs in your work, beyond chat interfaces e.g. calling model APIs, prompt engineering or AI coding assistants. • Strong communication skills and the ability to explain complex technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders. PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS • Experience in building, deploying and evaluating AI agents (e.g. tool use, multi-step workflows, agent frameworks). • Familiarity with carbon accounting frameworks (e.g., GHG Protocol, ISO 14064, CBAM, PACT). • Experience in industrial decarbonisation specification and modelling, preferably with a focus on mass and energy efficiency. • Familiarity with systems thinking in the context of value chain modelling. • Experience in early-stage startups, with a demonstrated ability to thrive in fast-moving environments. Benefits
WHAT NEUTREENO CAN OFFER YOU Compensation & Benefits: • £42,000 - £60,000 dependent on your skills, qualifications and experience. • 25 days annual leave. • Year-end performance bonus. • Meaningful equity stake. We want you to think and benefit like an owner as the company grows. • Company pension with NEST. • Leading private health insurance with WPA (the only Which? Recommended Provider for Private Medical Insurance). • Cycle to work scheme. Work Environment: • A hybrid work model that fosters both teamwork and individual flexibility. • Remote working allowance of 2 weeks per year for personal travel, in addition to regular holiday policy. • Work from Neutreeno HQ at the Cambridge Institute for Sustainability Leadership, recognised by the FT as one of Europe's leading startup hubs. • Great on-site amenities (unlimited free coffee, regular events with global sustainability leaders, and more). Culture & Growth: • A diverse, fast-growing team that has grown 200%+ YoY, recently closed a $5M seed round and been named one of Gartner's Coolest Vendor Innovations in Supply Chain Sustainability for 2026. • An open-minded, non-hierarchical culture where everyone vectors in the same direction and ideas and ownership matter. • The chance to work alongside world-class climate scientists and engineers on one of the most important problems of our time. • HOW WE HIRE
Here’s what to expect if you apply. The whole process has four steps.
• Intro call with our Operations and Finance Lead, Jobey (30 mins). A chance for us to learn about your background and what you’re looking for, and for you to ask about Neutreeno and the role.

About us
We see proteins as programmable nanomachines, some of the most capable technology nature has ever built. And we think the proteins that will matter most over the next decade are not the ones evolution handed us. Planes, after all, do not fly like birds.
Over the last five years, protein design has exploded. Tools like AlphaFold and ProteinMPNN let designers generate new proteins far faster than anyone can reliably make them. Manufacturing has not kept up. That gap, between what can be designed and what can actually be produced at useful quantity and sensible cost, is now the bottleneck on almost everything a designed protein could become.
Closing that gap is the whole point of nfin. We are building the manufacturing platform for protein designers. Our platform uses engineered Komagataella phaffii (K. phaffii) yeast to express recombinant proteins through precision fermentation, turning a design into real, usable protein reliably and rapidly. We are an early-stage company, already working with customers and partners across the designed-protein space. If that mission excites you as much as it does us, read on.
About the CADMUS project
This job is part of an Advanced Research + Invention Agency-funded project, subject to contract negotiations.
You would join CADMUS (Computer Aided Design of Materials for Universal Synthesis), a UK research consortium made up of Imperial College London, the University of Sheffield, and nfin, funded through ARIA. CADMUS has a bold goal: to develop a new way of manufacturing advanced magnetic materials by using designed proteins as programmable scaffolds to organise inorganic particles with nanoscale precision. It brings together machine learning for protein design, engineering biology, materials science, magnetic characterisation, and scalable biomanufacturing, to test whether proteins can control the structure of rare-earth-free magnetic materials in ways conventional manufacturing cannot.
nfin is responsible for the protein production and biomanufacturing side of CADMUS, and this role sits right at the heart of it. You will produce the designed proteins that the consortium tests as scaffolds for materials assembly, turning designs from the computational team into expressed, characterised protein. The programme runs on rapid design-build-test-learn cycles, so our bioreactor output feeds directly into the materials work, and the results feed back to shape the next round of designs. You will be part of a highly interdisciplinary team working at the interface of AI, biology, and materials science, helping to build a new platform for sustainable functional-materials manufacturing.
Our values
• We empower bright people to find and solve problems.
• We take our work seriously, but not so much ourselves.
• We celebrate the process, not the outcome.
The role
We are looking for a full-stack Bioprocess Engineer to lead the rapid production of de novo protein prototypes end to end. Your job is to turn novel protein designs into real, purified protein, from building the expression strains, through fermentation, to downstream processing and recovery.
This is a hands-on, in-person lab role. You will build strains, run bioreactors, and carry out downstream processing day to day, driving fast iteration between the designs we receive and the proteins we ship. We give bright people room to find the real problems and solve them, so you will own this work rather than wait to be told what to do next. If you like to see the immediate impact of your ideas and learn fast, you will feel at home here.
What matters most to us
More than any single skill, we are looking for a way of thinking. We can teach you a technique or a piece of kit. What we cannot teach is caring about the problem, and that is what we are really after.
The people who do well here take the initiative and own their work. They are curious, they ask why, and they think creatively when the obvious approach isn't working. Progress in startups and science is non-linear, with ups and downs, and you're joining us on that journey. What we offer in return is a supportive environment to solve what we think are some really cool problems.
What you will do
• Build and engineer K. phaffii expression strains for new protein targets.
• Plan and run bioreactor cultivations to express recombinant proteins in K. phaffii.
• Run downstream processing and recovery, and optimise both upstream and downstream conditions to improve yield, speed, and reproducibility.
• Keep clear, honest records and feed results back into the platform to shorten the design-to-protein cycle.
• Work closely with the CTO to develop and implement novel process automations and ML-guided bioprocess controls.
We care about how the work is done, not just the headline number. Careful method and good record-keeping matter to us as much as a strong yield.
What we are looking for
• Around 2 to 4 years of relevant experience, from industry or research.
• People who grok ("to understand intuitively or by empathy") biology, and who know their way around a wet lab. If you don't have experience of the entire stack, from strain engineering to freeze-drying, we can teach that.

ABOUT NIVODA
Nivoda is the B2B marketplace rebuilding how the jewellery industry works. We connect independent jewellery retailers with a global network of diamond and gemstone suppliers, so a jeweller in Denver or Devon can source from anywhere in the world without the cost, risk, and hassle of doing it the old way. We handle the logistics, the payments, and the quality checks, the messy middle that used to put global sourcing out of reach for small businesses.
Today we process over $300M in transactions a year in a $350B industry that still runs largely on personal relationships and paperwork. We are growing quickly, we are backed by leading investors, and we are only getting started.
We built Nivoda so every jeweller, whatever their size and wherever they are, has access to the same global supply, pricing and tools as the biggest players.
WHY THIS ROLE & WHY NOW
You will sit on the Extended Leadership Team, report to the CFO, and own how Nivoda plans, reports and is funded. You will present to the board, investors and our receivables lender yourself, work directly with the CFO on equity and debt financing, and build a finance function that runs on routine rather than heroics. This is for someone who wants to lead a team and shape the company’s financial story, not only model it.
WHAT YOU WILL OWN
Planning and forecasting. You own the annual budget, quarterly reforecast and long-range plan, plus scenario and funding cases for the C-suite and board. You are accountable for forecast accuracy against agreed tolerances, and for an honest post-mortem whether we miss or overachieve.
Board, investor and lender reporting. You own the monthly board pack and the numbers behind it, plus materials for existing and prospective investors and our receivables lender, including covenant reporting and onsite diligence. You present to these audiences yourself and you are their first call for analytical questions. The aim is that they trust the numbers without the CFO needing to vouch for them.
Corporate finance. You build the models and documentation for equity and debt financing, analyse term sheets, work with the People team on cap table and option pool, and support the CFO on transactions.
Commercial and unit economics. You own cohort economics, customer lifetime value, geographic and segment profitability, and the return on marketing and sales spend. With the CRO’s organisation, you build quota and commission models so targets, incentives and the forecast point at the same numbers.
Business partnering. You partner with Product and Engineering, Fulfilment, Fintech and the commercial teams on build versus buy, hiring cases, pricing and fee experiments, and capital allocation. The function says yes, no or not yet, with a model behind it.
Leading the function. You lead the team: hiring, onboarding, objectives, development and performance, including written objectives and regular structured feedback for each person. You set the review standard and deliverables calendar, agree data contracts with the Data team, and own the tooling (Snowflake, NetSuite, ThoughtSpot, Claude and the modelling stack). We measure the function on on-time delivery, errors caught internally rather than by the audience, forecast accuracy, and how many people can produce each recurring deliverable.
WHAT GOOD LOOKS LIKE
First 90 days. You have taken over the monthly pack and the reforecast without the investors noticing a handover. You have met your leadership-team peers and told the CFO what you would change and in what order.
90 to 180 days. The monthly pack, FP&A-approved numbers and lender reporting land on the agreed date, each with a named owner and a written process. No board, lender or investor number has needed restating. The first version of the business line P&Ls is delivered at day 180.
Twelve months. The function delivers month-end and board commitments without you or the CFO stepping in, including when you are away. A team member has delivered a new analytical capability end to end. FP&A and the Data team work from one set of metric definitions. Board members, lenders and the leadership team rely on the numbers without asking the CFO to vouch for them.
THE STANDARD
A finance team has no quota. The thing it sells is trust, and trust is earned with accuracy a bar above the rest of the company and delivery on the date promised.
Three things must not fail in this role.
- Timeliness: deadlines are commitments, not targets.
- Quality: every external-facing number reconciles to a primary source and has been reviewed by someone other than its author before it leaves the team.
- Capacity: within reason, not a constraint. The function absorbs the demands of a 450-person company by organising, prioritising and delegating. If capacity is a hard limit, you make the case for a hire or an automation with numbers, rather than letting the work slip.
That is a high bar, and it is fair because the role comes with the means to meet it: people to delegate to, authority over how the team's week is spent, a budget line, and the standing to say no to the business with the CFO's backing.
What you bring
- A background in investment banking, FP&A or venture capital, building models that senior stakeholders made decisions on.
- You have led a team, directly or through managers, and you want the management part of this role.
- You have presented to boards, investors or lenders as the person answering the question, not the person who built the slide.
- A working understanding of marketplace dynamics: two-sided liquidity, take rates, usage-based revenue without a contract, and what FX does to all of it. Complex cohort modelling is native to you.
- You are comfortable in Snowflake and a modern BI tool, you treat AI tooling as part of the stack, and you would rather fix the pipeline than reformat the output every month.
- You are calm under pressure, low on ego and allergic to spin. You tell people the uncomfortable thing early.
Useful but not required: receivables financing or lender reporting, a multi-jurisdiction group, NetSuite, or a business that trades physical goods across borders.
WHAT THIS ROLE IS NOT
It is not a bigger version of a senior analyst role, and it is not where every difficult model gets built personally. If you are at your best as the smartest modeler in the room and would rather stay that way, this will frustrate you.
It is also not a quiet seat. Month-end, board and lender deadlines are fixed, a 450-person company makes a lot of demands on finance, and you will regularly be the one saying no, with the CFO’s backing. If you want a purely advisory or slower-paced role, this isn’t it.
WHAT WE OFFER
Nivoda is a place where smart, driven people do the best work of their careers. We move fast, give ownership early, and don’t have layers of bureaucracy slowing things down. If you see a problem, you can fix it.
Our current benefits include:

- The chance to join during an expansion phase and shape how Nivoda operates at scale

Your impact begins here
As AI Scientist Specialist, you will turn scientific questions into AI methods that scientists can use and trust. You will build on existing work, start new initiatives and take proofs of concept and minimum viable products towards reliable operational use. Working within Research & Development, you will connect biology with machine learning, so drug discovery and development teams can act on clear, measurable results that support the research behind treatments for people living with serious chronic diseases.

You combine strong technical expertise with the curiosity to understand scientific questions, and you can explain your methods and their limits clearly to colleagues from different disciplines.
• A Bachelor’s degree with 8+ years, a Master’s degree with 6+ years, or a PhD with 3+ years of relevant experience in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Data Science, Bioinformatics or a related quantitative field.
• Experience developing and evaluating AI or machine learning methods through research, experimentation and practical delivery, in academia or industry.
• Strong knowledge of machine learning and relevant AI methods, with the judgement to select and evaluate the right approach for the scientific problem.
• Hands-on Python experience and experience with machine learning frameworks, plus sound software engineering practice: Git, testing, debugging and code reviews.
• The ability to turn research ideas into reproducible proofs of concept or minimum viable products, and to work with engineering and architecture colleagues on further development.
• The ability to translate stakeholders’ needs into actionable technical work.
• Analytical thinking, documentation skills and evidence-based decision-making, with project ownership and a collaborative approach to sharing knowledge.
• Willingness to work from our London office five days a week and to travel to Denmark occasionally.
Useful, but not essential
• An understanding of biology, or experience in bioinformatics or another scientific domain.
• Experience with NLP, Generative AI, Agentic system, frameworks such as PyTorch or Hugging Face, or cloud platforms such as Azure or AWS, depending on the project.
We welcome candidates from pharma, biotech, IT and research institutes.

In your first three to six months, you will get to know existing solutions and ongoing development, contribute to current delivery and take on a new initiative. From there, you will:
• Translate scientists’ needs into clearly defined technical problems, practical AI approaches and measurable outcomes.
• Design, develop and evaluate machine learning and AI methods for scientific use cases, including Generative AI and NLP where relevant.

• Develop proofs of concept and minimum viable products, and contribute to existing solutions, working with engineering and architecture colleagues on requirements for deployment.

Projects typically involve two or three colleagues: one leads, the others contribute, and everyone takes the lead on different projects. That way, knowledge is shared and work continues smoothly.
The team values an open, trusting environment and supports you in building independence and taking on more responsibility.

This role is based in our London office, five days a week, with travel to Denmark about once or twice a year, around five to ten days in total.
You will be trusted to own your work and supported to perform at your best. Leading some projects and contributing to others gives you room to grow your skills, take on greater responsibility and make your voice heard, in a team that shares what it learns.
Start now

The Laboratory Data Processor is responsible for converting raw geotechnical laboratory test outputs into accurate, traceable and report-ready datasets for review and interpretation by the laboratory team and wider Geotechnical Data Intelligence team. The role applies approved processing routines, performs quality-control checks, maintains clear processing records and supports the efficient management of laboratory data throughout the test and reporting lifecycle. The postholder may also contribute towards laboratory quality and accreditation activities, including verification work and external assessments.
What you will do:
The duties and responsibilities for this position include, but are not limited to:
Process geotechnical laboratory test data, including classification, oedometer, triaxial, direct simple shear and resonant column data, using approved in-house routines and tools.
Check processed results for completeness, consistency, calculation errors, anomalous values and compliance with the applicable project specification, test method and laboratory procedure.
Maintain clear and traceable processing records, including source data, calculation files, processing logs, review status, revisions and final outputs.
Manage, name, store and archive laboratory data in accordance with company requirements to protect data integrity, security, confidentiality and retrievability.
Escalate data-quality issues, missing information, out-of-specification results and departures from approved procedures to the Laboratory Manager or responsible engineer.
Keep test programming and tracking systems up to date so that laboratory progress and reporting status can be communicated accurately.
Assist with the preparation and quality review of laboratory reports, schedules, tables and data deliverables.
Develop, test, document and maintain data-processing and data-management tools to improve efficiency, robustness, repeatability and value, subject to appropriate technical review and approval.
Assis, where required, with equipment calibration and verification activities, including the measurement, monitoring and correction of equipment compliance effects where applicable.
Support accreditation and quality assessments, including evidence preparation, verification testing, responses to findings and implementation of agreed corrective actions.
Work collaboratively with laboratory technicians, engineers and project teams to resolve data queries and meet agreed reporting priorities.
General responsibilities:
Work towards the Ocean Infinity and Geowynd mission and objectives by contributing to relevant performance indicators and improvement priorities.
Support Ocean Infinity and Geowynd Health, Safety, Environmental and Social goals and ensure day-to-day decisions are consistent with those goals.
Comply with applicable Ocean Infinity and Geowynd policies, practices, programmes and procedures described in the management system.
Complete required training identified through the applicable training programme.
Contribute to continual improvement by reporting events and problems, participating in meetings and workshops, and recommending practical improvements.
Report unidentified risks, hazards or system deficiencies to the manager or responsible person, using Stop Work Authority, reporting cards, incident reporting or direct escalation as appropriate.
Communicate and apply relevant policies and procedures when working with employees, visitors and contractors.
You ideal candidate should have:
Experience in processing, checking or managing technical, scientific or engineering data.
Competence and confidence working with structured datasets, calculations, charts and technical records.
Experience working within a controlled quality-management or accredited laboratory environment is desirable.
Strong attention to detail and a systematic approach to data checking and document control.
Ability to follow approved procedures while identifying and clearly communicating exceptions, risks and opportunities for improvement.
Analytical problem-solving skills and the ability to investigate discrepancies without compromising source data or traceability.
Clear written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain data issues to laboratory and engineering colleagues.
Ability to manage competing priorities, maintain accurate records and deliver reliable outputs to agreed deadlines.
A collaborative, safety-conscious and quality-focused approach to work.
Salary: up to 30,000 GBP per annum

Job Description
Purpose of the role
The purpose of a Product Owner is to maximize the value of the product by defining a clear product vision (are they setting the vision or would this align to ), managing authoring, refining and prioritizing the Product Backlog balancing trade-offs across desirability, viability and feasibility – making sure the right thing is being ‘built’, and prioritising work based on business goals. They act as the primary liaison between stakeholders and delivery teams, ensuring the product meets user/customer needs and delivers optimal value. Product Owners are responsible for developing a roadmap and driving execution of their product area/sub-journey, applying continuous improvement principles and techniques.
Accountabilities
• Ensure Product Alignment with Business Goals: Ensure that the product & its features are aligned with broader objectives, driving value and contributing to the organization’s overall strategy. About Piran Technology Group
Piran Technology Group is a rapidly growing UK advanced manufacturing business specialising in high-performance composite manufacturing and precision CNC machining.
Operating across the aerospace, defence, automotive, motorsport and advanced engineering sectors, we manufacture technically demanding components and assemblies for some of the world's most innovative engineering programmes.
As our manufacturing operations continue to expand, we are investing in operational excellence, advanced production analytics and continuous improvement.
The Role
We are seeking an experienced and highly analytical Lean Manufacturing & Production Analytics Manager to drive improvements in manufacturing efficiency, productivity and operational performance.
This is a hands-on role combining Lean Manufacturing, continuous improvement, advanced data analytics and production planning.
Working closely with our Operations Director and production management team, you will be responsible for identifying manufacturing inefficiencies, implementing practical improvements and developing sophisticated analytical tools to monitor and optimise factory performance.
We are particularly interested in candidates from automotive OEMs, Tier 1 suppliers, aerospace or similarly advanced manufacturing environments where Lean principles, statistical analysis and data-driven decision-making are embedded in day-to-day operations.
We are looking for someone who can not only analyse manufacturing performance but actively improve it, using advanced data capabilities to identify opportunities, implement solutions and demonstrate measurable results.
Key Responsibilities
Lean Manufacturing & Continuous Improvement
Lead and implement Lean Manufacturing initiatives to improve productivity, efficiency, manufacturing flow and operational performance.
Identify and eliminate manufacturing waste, inefficiencies, bottlenecks and non-value-added activities.
Apply Lean methodologies including 5S, Kaizen, Value Stream Mapping, Standardised Work and structured root-cause analysis.
Analyse production processes, labour utilisation, cycle times, equipment capacity and material flow to identify improvement opportunities.
Establish and refine standard manufacturing times, labour requirements and production performance benchmarks.
Lead continuous improvement projects, working directly with production, engineering and quality teams to implement sustainable changes.
Quantify and demonstrate improvements through measurable reductions in manufacturing costs, labour hours, waste and production lead times.
Production Analytics & Business Intelligence
Independently develop and maintain advanced Power BI dashboards providing detailed visibility of manufacturing performance.
Utilise Power BI, Power Query, SQL, DAX and advanced Excel to develop sophisticated data models, automated reporting systems and analytical tools.
Apply programming and scripting capabilities to automate data extraction, processing and reporting.
Integrate manufacturing information from ERP/MRP systems, production trackers, labour records and quality databases.
Develop comprehensive production KPIs covering output, labour efficiency, material consumption, scrap, rework, throughput and delivery performance.
Apply statistical analysis, trend analysis and Statistical Process Control (SPC) techniques to identify process variation and performance improvement opportunities.
Provide clear, actionable manufacturing intelligence to support operational decisions, capacity planning and continuous improvement.
Strong technical data skills are essential. The successful candidate must be capable of personally developing complex dashboards, data models and automated analytical solutions, rather than simply interpreting existing reports.
Production Planning & Resource Optimisation
Work with Production Managers to develop and maintain effective daily, weekly and medium-term manufacturing plans.
Support the allocation and optimisation of labour, skills, equipment and manufacturing resources across production departments.
Maintain accurate production schedules, resource plans and work-order tracking systems.
Develop capacity models to identify resource constraints and assess the impact of changing production requirements.
Monitor actual production performance against plan, identifying potential delivery risks and recommending corrective actions.
Improve production planning processes through better data visibility, automation and resource utilisation.
Essential Skills & Experience
We are looking for someone who combines strong practical manufacturing experience with exceptional analytical and technical capabilities.
The successful candidate will demonstrate:
Proven experience implementing Lean Manufacturing and delivering measurable continuous improvement projects.
Strong understanding of manufacturing processes, labour productivity, production flow and operational efficiency.
Advanced proficiency in Power BI, Power Query, SQL, DAX and Microsoft Excel, with demonstrable experience developing complex dashboards and analytical solutions.
Strong coding or scripting capabilities, particularly for data manipulation, automation and reporting.
Experience applying statistical analysis and structured problem-solving techniques to manufacturing performance.
Understanding of production planning, capacity modelling and resource allocation.
Ability to translate complex manufacturing data into practical operational improvements.
A proactive, hands-on approach, with the ability to work effectively with shop-floor teams and senior management.
Desirable Experience
Automotive OEM, Tier 1 automotive, aerospace, defence or other advanced manufacturing experience.
Lean Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt certification.
Manufacturing or Industrial Engineering background.
Experience with Python, VBA or similar programming languages.
Experience developing or integrating ERP/MRP and manufacturing information systems.
Familiarity with AS9100, ISO 9001 or equivalent quality management standards.
What We Expect
This is a role where measurable results and practical improvements are essential.
We expect the successful candidate to take ownership of developing our manufacturing analytics capability while actively identifying and implementing opportunities to improve production performance.
You will be expected to spend time on the factory floor understanding manufacturing processes, working with production teams and challenging existing methods where improvements can be achieved.
Success will be demonstrated through:
Measurable improvements in manufacturing productivity and labour efficiency.
Reduced manufacturing waste, scrap, rework and production costs.
Improved production planning, resource utilisation and capacity visibility.
Advanced, reliable and automated manufacturing performance dashboards.
A structured and sustainable approach to Lean Manufacturing and continuous improvement.
The Opportunity
This is an opportunity to play a significant role in the development of manufacturing operations within a fast-growing UK engineering group.
You will have the scope to introduce advanced manufacturing practices, develop sophisticated analytical systems and directly influence operational performance.
We are looking for someone who brings both the practical manufacturing expertise of a Lean specialist and the technical capabilities of an advanced data analytics professional.
This job description is not exhaustive and may be amended to reflect the business’s operational requirements.

Many of the positions within our company are subject to national security clearance and Trade Control restrictions. This means that your eligibility for certain roles may be affected by your place of birth, nationality, current or former citizenship, and any residency you hold or have held. Further details are available at United Kingdom Security Vetting: clearance levels - GOV.UK (www.gov.uk).

ABOUT PLASMA
Plasma is building the primary account for global money.
Money used to belong to a country. Increasingly, it belongs to a person or business moving through many countries. People and businesses now earn, spend, save, hire and invest across borders. Traditional banks cannot serve this new world.
Our first product, Plasma One, is a global money account: a place to receive, hold, send funds in seconds, earn yield and spend with a card in the local economy.
Underneath is the Plasma network, built from first principles for stablecoin payments. Stablecoins make dollars faster, cheaper and more reliable to move.
The opportunity is to become where all global money lands first: where income arrives, balances grow, payments move, businesses operate, and new financial products are built.
THE TEAM & OUR STORY https://x.com/Plasma/status/2067634709727719601?s=20
We are a global team of founders, operators and engineers, obsessed with building the best products. We work at the cutting edge of financial innovation, using stablecoins to create tools for consumers and businesses.
We operate with trust, clarity, and ambition: own your craft, move with urgency, contribute beyond your lane, back your teammates, debate rigorously, and keep raising the bar for what great means.
CUSTOMER EXPERIENCE Plasma is scaling its customer-facing operations across international markets, and we’re growing the Customer Experience Team to match. You’ll join an established team and take ownership of coverage for the CET time zone, making sure our customers get great support when they need it most.
You’ll work across the full customer journey, from first contact through to resolution. Because we’re still building out our playbook, your input will directly shape the processes, standards, and team culture as we grow. You won’t just follow the process; you’ll help refine it.
Some flexibility in working hours & weekend shifts will be needed to support coverage and the occasional busy period. We’re looking for a hard-working self-starter who thrives in a fast-moving startup environment and is committed to the mission alongside the rest of the team.
THE ROLE
- Own the customer experience day-to-day: Be the first person our customers reach when something goes wrong or they need help. You will handle inbound queries across chat, email, and support tooling, and take accountability for the quality and speed of every response.
- Be the right hand of the Ops lead: Work directly alongside the Head of Operations to build out processes, identify gaps, and support decisions as we scale the team internationally. This is not a back-office support role. You will be involved in how we think about operations.
- Build the foundations: We are early. Many of the processes, templates, and escalation paths do not exist yet. You will create them. From response frameworks to internal guides, you will help lay the groundwork the team will rely on as we grow.
- Support international team scaling: As we hire Ops team members in new markets, you will help onboard them, share knowledge, and maintain consistency in how we deliver for customers across regions.
- Spot problems before they become patterns: Track issues across the customer base, flag recurring themes to Product and Engineering, and help prioritise fixes that actually move the needle for customers.
- Work across teams: Collaborate with Compliance, KYC, and Product to make sure the customer experience is joined up, especially during onboarding and verification flows where things can go wrong quickly.
- Represent the customer internally: Your proximity to customer feedback is valuable. Use it. Bring customer insight into internal conversations and push for improvements that matter.
- Be Flexible with Shift Rotation: Most weeks you’ll work the normal Mon-Fri, however team members currently rotate weekend shifts which means that you may be required to work a weekend shift once every 6 weeks. You’ll then be able to take those days worked off the following week.
THE BAR
- 1 to 3 years of experience in customer operations, customer success, or a support role, ideally within fintech, payments, or crypto. We will consider strong candidates from outside these sectors if the fit is right.
- Someone who takes ownership. You do not wait to be told. When something is broken or missing, you fix it or flag it. You hold yourself to a high standard even when no one is watching.
- Clear and direct in how you communicate. You can write a helpful, professional response under pressure and explain a complex situation simply. You know the difference between being thorough and overcomplicating things.
- Competent English Language - our team communicates in english so being competent with the language is a requirement.
- Comfortable with ambiguity. This is an early-stage company. Processes will change, priorities will shift, and some days you will be figuring things out as you go. You see that as interesting rather than frustrating. Preferably, you have worked at a fast-paced tech company.
- Genuinely curious about crypto. You do not need deep technical knowledge, but you need to understand the basics of how stablecoins and digital assets work and be motivated to learn more. Our customers live in this space.
- Organised under pressure. You can manage a queue, prioritise effectively, and keep quality high when things are busy.
- Collaborative by default. You work well with people in different functions, different time zones, and different levels of seniority. Building the team abroad means working with people you may never meet in person, and you are good at that.
NICE TO HAVE
- Experience in a startup or scale-up where you had to build or rebuild processes, not just follow them.
- Exposure to Intercom, Zendesk, Freshdesk, or similar support tooling in a live production environment.
- Any familiarity with KYC or compliance workflows as they relate to customer onboarding.
- Experience supporting or managing a small team, even informally, or helping onboard new colleagues.
- An interest in how stablecoin and DeFi products work and the customer challenges they create.
- Multilingual skills that could support customer communication across our international markets.
WHAT'S IN IT FOR YOU
- Above-market salary for the level of the role, with token compensation.
- A beautiful London HQ with gym access and daily food, for those who thrive in an office environment. Visa sponsorship and relocation support if you're joining from abroad.
- Premium health insurance for you and your family, fully covered by Plasma.
- Monthly wellness budget, whether that's the gym, therapy, sauna, or massage.
- All the tools and tech you need to operate at your best.
- Real ownership and responsibility from day one, with your work shipping to hundreds of thousands of people, moving millions of dollars every day.

We are committed to protecting the privacy and security of your personal data. Any personal information you provide during the recruitment process will be processed in accordance with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and applicable local data protection laws.

Are you a highly skilled Plumber who takes pride in delivering excellent repairs and maintenance and supporting others to succeed?
At Platform Property Care, we're looking for a Lead Engineer – Plumbing to join our team in the Nottingham and Newark areas. This is an exciting opportunity for an experienced multi skilled Plumber to combine hands-on trade expertise supporting colleagues, driving quality standards and helping improve our service delivery.
Acting as the subject matter expert for plumbing, you'll spend around 70-80% of your time delivering repairs and maintenance work, while dedicating the remainder to coaching colleagues, assessing competence, supporting apprentices, and promoting best practice across our Property Care teams.
What could you be doing?
You'll be ensuring our customers' homes are maintained and repaired to a high standard while also helping to drive consistency, quality and best practice across our Property Care teams.
As a Lead Engineer - Plumbing, you will:
• Carry out a wide range of plumbing repairs and maintenance work within customers' homes and communal areas.
• Manage jobs from inspection through to completion, ensuring excellent customer service throughout.
• Support colleagues through coaching, mentoring and skills development
• Assess and sign off colleagues against our multi-skill framework and support apprentices through their End Point Assessments (EPA).
• Promote consistent trade standards and best practice across Platform Property Care.
• Work alongside Learning & Development teams to support trade training and upskilling initiatives.
• Conduct trade audits, reviews and quality assessments to ensure compliance and high standards.
• Act as a technical expert and escalation point for trade-related queries.
• Monitor industry developments, legislation and emerging technologies to support continuous improvement and enhance service delivery.
No two days are the same. It's a challenging and rewarding role that offers the opportunity to combine practical trade expertise with developing others and improving services for our customers.
Who are we looking for?
You'll be a highly motivated and customer-focused professional who takes pride in delivering quality workmanship and supporting others to succeed.
You will be:
• A strong team player with a positive, can-do attitude.
• Comfortable working independently and taking ownership of your workload.
• Passionate about developing others and sharing your knowledge.
• Organised and focused on delivering right-first-time outcomes.
• Able to communicate effectively with customers, colleagues and apprentices.
• Committed to maintaining excellent health and safety standards.
Some things we need from you:
• NVQ Level 2 in Plumbing, completed apprenticeship or equivalent qualification.
• Additional Trade qualifications.
• Unvented Hot Water qualification is essential
• Significant experience working as a Plumber within the building trade.
• Experience working within occupied domestic properties.
• Strong knowledge of health and safety requirements.
• Experience of recording accurate job and repair information using mobile devices.
• Good IT and digital skills
• The ability to coach, support and develop colleagues.
• A commitment to delivering excellent customer service
• Experience working within social housing, a local authority or housing association.
• Previous coaching, mentoring or assessor experience.

• As you will be working within customers' homes this role requires a DBS check.
• This role is for a team covering the Nottingham and Newark areas. Ideally you will only have a maximum of an hour's commute to this area.
Working for Platform Property Care, you will benefit from

This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced multi skilled Plumber looking to take the next step in their career. As a Lead Engineer - Plumbing, you'll play a key role in driving technical excellence, developing colleagues, improving service quality, and delivering outstanding outcomes for customers.
Part of Platform Housing Group, Platform Property Care is a well-established property maintenance business. We value the contribution our colleagues make and are committed to developing a highly skilled and engaged workforce that delivers excellent services for our customers.

job_description:
Why Sony Interactive Entertainment?
Sony Interactive Entertainment isn’t just the Best Place to Play — it’s also the Best Place to Work. Sony Interactive Entertainment (SIE) is the company behind the PlayStation brand. As a subsidiary of Sony Group Corporation, we’re part of a proud legacy of innovation and excellence. SIE is a dynamic technology company, delivering cutting-edge hardware and network services to more than 100 million people and an entertainment leader, home to some of the most beloved and recognizable intellectual properties (IP) in the world. Our role at SIE is to create and nurture the experiences under the PlayStation brand, a name synonymous with entertainment excellence and creativity.
Senior Director, Legal - Global Privacy & Data Counsel
San Mateo, CA or London, England | Hybrid - 2+ days per week in your designated office
Full relocation assistance available for qualified candidates 
Role Summary:
Leading SIE’s Global Legal Privacy program, you will play a pivotal role in shaping and advancing this function, which is central to our mission as a data-driven technology and entertainment company. You will develop, implement, and maintain comprehensive privacy policies, procedures, and practices that reflect industry best practices, comply with applicable data protection laws and regulations, and support SIE’s business objectives. Working collaboratively with teams around the world, you will help embed strong data privacy stewardship across the organization through your leadership, passion, and expertise.
What You’ll Be Doing:
Lead the Privacy Team: Lead a team of professionals spanning legal, operations and compliance, and data governance. Provide strong leadership to build a well-functioning team.
Privacy Program Development: Design, implement, and evolve a robust and forward-thinking privacy program tailored to the specific needs of SIE’s multi-faceted, data-driven business. Provide senior leadership in communicating company's vision, strategy, and objectives for data privacy and data husbandry to stakeholders across SIE. 
Regulatory Compliance: Stay up to date with evolving global privacy laws and regulations, including GDPR, CCPA, and other regional data protection requirements. Ensure the company's policies and practices remain compliant with the changing legal landscape. 
Privacy by Design: Advocate privacy-by-design principles and ensure that privacy considerations are integrated into the development of new products, services, and technologies, working closely with product counselors, product managers, business function leaders and SIE’s ESG team. 
Privacy Policies and Procedures: Create and review privacy policies, notices, consent forms, and related documentation to ensure transparency and compliance with relevant data protection laws. Collaborate with Legal, Compliance, and other teams to disseminate these policies throughout the organization and to customers. 
Employee Training and Awareness: Conduct privacy training programs for employees and management to promote a privacy-aware culture. Foster awareness of privacy responsibilities and best practices throughout the organization. 
Vendor Management: Develop and evolve SIE’s processes to assess the privacy practices of vendors and third-party partners to ensure that data processing agreements and contracts comply with privacy and SIE’s Information Security requirements. 
Privacy Impact Assessments: Oversee the conduct of privacy impact assessments (PIAs) to identify and mitigate privacy risks associated with the company's data processing activities.
Incident Response: Develop and maintain an effective incident response plan for privacy breaches. Coordinate with the Incident Response team to manage and mitigate privacy incidents and associated risks. 
Reporting and Accountability: Provide regular reports on the status of the privacy program to executive leadership and the board of directors. Be a focal point of contact for privacy-related inquiries from regulators and customers. 
What We’re Looking For:
Juris doctor degree; bachelor or advanced degree in computer science, information technology, or a related field. An advanced degree is a plus. 
20+ years of legal experience and 10+ years proven experience in a senior privacy leadership role, preferably as a Chief Privacy Officer or Privacy Officer, within a data-driven technology company or relevant industry. 
In-depth knowledge of global privacy laws and regulations, such as GDPR, CCPA, and other regional frameworks. Broad knowledge of emerging requires in the APAC region a strong plus.
Demonstrated ability to design and implement comprehensive privacy programs that align with industry best practices, laws and regulations and data use requirements typical of a company like SIE. 
Experience in building an incident response process with partnership with the CISO or similar function; experience managing privacy incidents.
Experience conducting privacy impact assessments and building processes for such assessments that will easily scale. 
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to interact effectively with stakeholders at all levels of the organization. 
Strong leadership qualities, with the ability to influence and drive change in a collaborative environment.

job_title: Senior Designer, Brand and AI Systems
job_description:
PolyAI is the Agentic Dialog Platform for building the conversational enterprise, used to build, run, govern, and improve dialog agents at scale. Powered by Raven, a proprietary dialog model trained on more than a billion enterprise conversations, PolyAI agents are built for complexity, open at every layer, and sovereign by design. PolyAI serves hundreds of enterprises across 75 languages and 25 countries, including Metro Bank, Marriott, PG&E, and UniCredit.
 
About the role
We're hiring a senior brand designer to own PolyAI's visual identity and to build the AI-native systems that let that identity scale. You are the day-to-day owner of how the brand looks and feels across campaigns, web assets, sales, events and video. You are also a design engineer at heart. You turn recurring design work into templates, automations and AI-assisted workflows, so the team can produce on-brand work faster without losing craft.
You will work with the Creative Director, the web and content teams, marketing, sales and product. This is a hands-on role with real ownership and a lot of range. One week you may be directing a launch video, the next you may be building a component library or an automated asset pipeline.
What you'll do
Own the brand
• Own and manage the brand identity across all marketing: website, events, advertising, sales materials, video and audio demos.
• Champion consistency across the company, including sales, product and people teams. Say no when it matters, explain why and offer a better option.
• Evolve the identity as the company grows, and document it so others can apply it correctly.
• Design web assets, including landing page visuals, page graphics and animation, and hand them to the web team and partners to build. This role does not build pages.
Build the AI-native design system
• Build and maintain a living brand design system: tokens, Figma libraries with variables and components, templates, and guidelines written for humans and for AI tools.
• Turn repeatable work into AI-assisted workflows, templates and generators that marketing, sales and product can use without a designer in the room.
• Automate production with scripts, AI coding tools and no-code tools, for example resizing and localising ad variants, generating decks and building video templates.
• Define quality guardrails for AI-assisted output: review checkpoints, acceptance criteria and feedback loops that prevent brand drift.
• Evaluate and adopt new AI design, image, video and audio tools. Share what works and what doesn't, and help the wider team build fluency.
Create and direct
• Concept and design campaign assets end to end: key visuals, paid and social creative, ebooks, one-pagers, sales decks, event materials and custom client content.
• Direct and produce video and motion work, from storyboard to final edit, using both traditional tools and AI-assisted workflows.
• Use design thinking to solve marketing problems, and work with the team to test and improve engagement and conversion.
• Repurpose content across channels.
Lead and collaborate
• Partner with design, motion, and development partners or agencies end to end: briefs, direction, review and quality.
• Partner with engineering and product so the brand carries through to product-adjacent surfaces.
• Explain design decisions to non-designers and tie them to business goals.
What we're looking for
• 7+ years of brand design experience, with a track record of owning a brand or identity at an applied AI, SaaS or other fast-growing technology company.
• A portfolio showing a brand system that grew and was applied consistently across channels. Case studies of tools, templates or workflows you built are a strong plus.
• Hands-on experience using AI tools in real creative workflows (generative image, video, audio and layout tools), with a clear view of their strengths, limits and risks.
• Design systems experience: Figma libraries, variables, components and design tokens. You can document a system clearly enough for others to use it.
• Comfort building. You can use AI coding tools (Claude Code) and light scripting or HTML/CSS to automate work and prototype tools, rather than waiting on engineering.
• Expert Figma and Adobe Creative Cloud skills, and strong presentation design.
• Strong typography, layout and art direction instincts, and the conviction to defend your decisions.
• Experience managing freelancers, agencies or junior designers.
• Strong stakeholder skills and clear written and spoken communication. You work well in a fast-moving, ambiguous environment.
Nice to have
• Motion and video skills (After Effects, Premiere Pro or similar), and the ability to direct video production.
• Experience designing with data: testing, analytics and conversion results.
• Web design principles and experience handing designs off to web teams or external web partners.
• Experience building or relaunching a brand at a fast-growing technology company.
• Experience designing for developer audiences or technical products.
Benefits
💰 Participation in the company’s employee share options plan
🏝 Tenure-Based PTO: You will receive 25 holidays when you join and will gain an additional 1 day after 2 years of service, then 1 day each year until capped at 32 holidays
🏡 Flexible working from home policy
🌎 Work from outside of the UK for up to 6 months each year
🫂TELUS Health EAP 24/7 - offers you and your chosen family confidential, judgment-free support for any work, health, or life challenge
🧡 Enhanced parental leave
🚲 Bike2Work scheme
📚 Annual learning and development allowance
🏡 We’re all about making WFH work for you - that’s why we offer a one-off WFH allowance when you join. Offering perks like noise-cancelling headphones or a comfortable desk chair to boost your comfort and focus!
👨‍👩‍👧 Company-funded fertility and family-forming programmes
🌸 Menopause care programme with Maven
🏥 Private healthcare and dental cover, discounts on gym members and relaxation apps, and access to a range of mental health programs
🌎 Sabbatical Program: 5-week paid sabbatical available after 5 years of employment

Start your career in global clinical trials
Are you highly organised, proactive and comfortable working in a fast-paced environment where priorities can change throughout the day?
Perhaps you're a recent graduate looking to take your first step into the pharmaceutical or clinical trials industry. Or you already have experience in customer service, administration, logistics or project coordination and want to build a career within a global organisation.
Thermo Fisher Scientific is looking for a Project Support Coordinator to join our busy Distribution team in Horsham.

You'll join our Clinical Trials Division, working alongside Project Managers to coordinate the global distribution of clinical trial supplies.

• Conduct regular meetings with clients and internal departments to ensure adherence to Clinical Trial specifications.
• Assist in setting up and maintaining study filing systems, while ensuring accurate record-keeping.
• Collaborate with the Project Manager to ensure that all Fisher Clinical Services activities are aligned to meet customer and study requirements.
• Coordinate and communicate all relevant activities, both internally and externally, to ensure timely readiness of services and products as required by customers.
• Provide timely reports and other information to customers, as applicable.
• Provide backup support to the Project Manager and team during absences.
• Monitor Clinical Trial activities and overall business operations.
• Adhere to Good Manufacturing Principles in all areas of responsibility.
What are we looking for?
You don't need previous clinical trials, pharmaceutical or life sciences industry experience to succeed in this role. We're much more interested in the skills and
approach you can bring.

• Experience in a fast-paced, high-pressure environment is required.
• Excellent organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple tasks and meet strict deadlines.
• Strong analytical skills with the ability to analyze problems and propose effective solutions.
• Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to effectively present information and respond to questions from managers and clients.
• Ability to develop strong customer management skills, anticipating and exceeding client expectations.
• Proficiency in learning and using internal systems associated with projects (e.g., GPMS, Trackwise).
• Strong numeracy and computer skills, including proficiency in Outlook and Excel.
• Understanding and competent use of SOPs required by company Quality standards.

• Education: Bachelor's degree or equivalent desirable
• Years of Experience: 2+ years of relevant client facing work experience
• Prefer experience in fast paced and varied administrative role – ie distribution, logistics.
• Prefer understanding of clinical trials.
• Prefer previous experience in a highly regulated industry.

For the right person, this is a fantastic opportunity to get your foot in the door at Thermo Fisher Scientific and build a career within the Clinical Trials Division.You'll gain exposure to global customers, international logistics and clinical trial project management while learning how a major global organisation supports clinical studies around the world.
It's a busy role with plenty of variety and responsibility – and one where you'll be able to see the impact of your work as part of a team.

Patient-Centered Research, In-trial qualitative research Evidera’s Patient-Centered Research (PCR) group combines a unique portfolio of scientific disciplines, including health sciences, psychometrics, epidemiology, psychology, and many other social sciences. Our PCR staff conduct a variety of studies using quantitative and qualitative approaches to develop clinical outcomes assessments, evaluate patient preferences and utilities, execute various implementation science studies, conduct Delphi panels and do secondary data analysis using advanced statistical techniques.
Within the PCR group, the ITR team conduct qualitative (interviews) studies and/or surveys in the context of a clinical trial to obtain feedback from clinical trial participants (patient, caregiver, investigator or study staff) on various topics i.e., understanding patients’ experience with their condition, its impacts on their lives, exploring treatment benefit, describing trial participant experiences and identifying aspects of burden from their participation. ITR can be implemented using an embedded design (e.g., ITR is defined as clinical trial activity in the clinical trial study protocol and ICF) or associated design (ITR is covered under separate protocol, separate ICF, and IRB/EC approval, with separate site recruitment and contracting). ITR can be conducted at any trial phase and at any time in the trial (screening, mid-trial, exit). Over the past few years, there has been a growing interest in ITR studies by regulators to support relevance and interpretation of trial outcomes, meaningful change and/or meaningful treatment benefit.

Hey!

That's exactly what we're building every single day. 
tl;dr
We’re looking for someone who keeps our football data right: results, stats and market values players can trust, especially right after the final whistle.

Agent-native: We build with Claude Code every day. Whichever coding agent you've used so far, you plan with it, review every line it writes, and own what ships.
Small steps, shipped often: Tests first, small merge requests, a teammate reviews - then it's live. That's our rhythm.
Football-curious: You don't need to know everything about grassroots football yet - but you want to understand how it works, inside out.
English first: It's our working language. We're an international team, though, so you'll also hear German, Spanish, Dutch and more around the (virtual) office.
What you'll do - your playing field
This is how you move our mission forward every day.
You keep our football data right. Results, lineups, goals, appearances, stats and market values: you make sure what reaches the app matches what happened on the pitch - and what our users tell us happened there.
You build and run data processing services. Python services and pipelines that turn match data from many sources into the teams, players and stats in our app - tested, monitored and ready for the weekend peak.
You make data quality measurable. Validation, monitoring and alerts - and when something's off, you fix the root cause, not just the symptom.
You become one of our football data experts. Age groups, season changes, renamed and merged teams, duplicate players, players who remember the match differently - you learn how grassroots football data really behaves and turn that knowledge into rules our systems enforce.
You think about the player at the end of the pipeline. A missing goal or a wrong appearance is someone's weekend. You care how data shows up for players and clubs, not only whether the job ran.

Shape how our data models evolve, together with the engineers who own data acquisition and processing
Support our data and business colleagues on the technical side of data requests - the queries, data pulls and checks behind analyses for internal teams and partners
Build small internal tools so our support and product colleagues can check and fix data themselves

Data pipelines: You've built and run production data pipelines that others relied on.
Python: You've shipped Python services with tests and code review.
SQL & data modelling: You're strong in SQL and model data cleanly on PostgreSQL or similar.
Data quality: You've owned the quality of a dataset - with checks, monitoring and gaps made explicit.
Messy data: You've made data you don't control reliable - inconsistent names, duplicates, late corrections and all.
Communication: You explain a data problem clearly to people who don't write SQL.
Tools: Python, PostgreSQL, RabbitMQ, AWS, Kubernetes, GitLab CI, Grafana, Metabase, Claude Code
Good to know
We want you to know what this role really looks like from day one.
This is a software engineering role with a data focus: you write Python services and pipelines, not only SQL models and DAGs. Most of your time goes into getting football data right and keeping it that way.
You join Core Systems, where backend and data work as one team. You'll take over an existing domain with a lot of history, so you'll be working on your own fairly quickly - with the team there to explain the why.
Bonus
Not a must - but this'll definitely earn you extra points.
