You have a football background: you've played, coached or helped run a club
You've built dashboards or reports for non-technical users
You've worked with a mobile or frontend codebase (Flutter is a plus), enough to follow how data reaches the screen when you're tracing a bug

Employee participation (VSOP) - You benefit directly from the company's success.
Modern tech setup - We provide the tools and devices you need to do your best work.

Remote work - Depending on how far you live from the office and your role, you'll work 1-3 days a week in the office and the rest flexibly remote - however works best for you. For Tech & Product, 100% remote is sometimes possible.
Offices in Cologne, Berlin, London + virtual - Whether Berlin, Cologne or London - you get to choose. And our virtual office keeps the whole team closely connected across locations. Fancy a change of scenery? Just work from one of our other offices for a bit.
Work from anywhere - A week of sun abroad or a few days at the family's? No problem - you can work flexibly from outside your home base.
Team events - Whether after-work in Cologne, Berlin or London: we bring our teams together regularly - to connect, hang out and grow even closer as a team.
Offsites with the whole team - Four days away from the everyday with the whole team: travelling together, spinning ideas, working side by side and experiencing real team spirit.

job_description:
Join Reap as Senior Product Manager, Client Activation — build compliant, scalable B2B onboarding that helps businesses get verified and reach value faster across global markets.
About Reap
Reap is a global financial technology company headquartered in Hong Kong with employees across multiple countries. We enable financial connectivity and access for businesses worldwide by combining traditional finance with stablecoins for efficient money movement.
Through our stablecoin-powered corporate cards, payments, and expense management tools, we streamline financial operations and help businesses scale. Our APIs enable businesses to integrate stablecoin-enabled finance into their own products and services—from issuing Visa cards to facilitating cross-border payments.
Backed by leading investors including Index Ventures and HashKey Capital, Reap is building the future of borderless, stablecoin-enabled finance.
Role Overview
We are looking for a Senior Product Manager to own and scale Reap's client activation and onboarding experience as we expand into new markets and unlock new use cases. Client Activation is the company's #1 objective - this role sits at the centre of it.
You will design onboarding that turns regulatory complexity into a competitive advantage: fast, compliant, consistent client activation across geographies, products, and flow types, built on systems that scale and differentiate Reap in the market.
What You'll Do
- End-to-end activation funnels - from application through identity verification, KYC/KYB, AML screening, risk assessment, account setup, and first value. Our core motion is B2B, with consumer use cases alongside it.
- The verification and AML stack in-product - identity and entity verification (KYC/KYB), document and registry checks, sanctions and PEP screening, risk decisioning, and controls that keep us audit-ready across jurisdictions.
- Vendor and orchestration strategy - select, integrate, and get the most out of KYC/KYB providers, identity verification vendors, and workflow engines.
- Scalable onboarding architecture - configurable flows, rules, and decisioning that adapt to jurisdiction-specific requirements without bespoke rebuilds, plus the activation playbook that lets Reap enter new markets and launch new use cases faster each time.
- Regulatory-by-design product thinking - partner deeply with Compliance and Legal to translate licensing and regulatory obligations into product requirements that don't compromise client experience.
- Cross-functional orchestration - partner closely with Engineering day-to-day, and work across Ops, Compliance, and GTM to remove friction, reduce manual review, and improve conversion and time-to-activate.
- Metrics and iteration - own activation funnel metrics (conversion, time-to-activation, verification speed, manual review rates, drop-off by stage and market), run experiments, and drive a roadmap grounded in data.
What We’re Looking For
- Built B2B onboarding/activation systems in regulated fintech - hands-on PM experience shipping client onboarding, KYC/KYB, or activation products. B2B is essential; exposure to consumer onboarding is valuable too.
- Deep fluency in the AML stack - identity verification, KYC/KYB, sanctions and PEP screening, licensing, and data requirements across geographies, product lines, and flow types - plus hands-on experience with onboarding vendors and orchestration tools (KYC/KYB providers, identity verification vendors, workflow engines).
- Thinks holistically - weighs client experience, legal and regulatory requirements, and operationalising together in every product decision; treats compliance as a constraint to design within, not an obstacle to route around.
- Systems thinker - builds scalable, configurable systems (rules engines, modular flows, reusable components), not market-by-market one-offs.
- Client experience obsession - judges every flow by how it feels to a good client: fewer steps, less friction, faster to first value.
- Data-driven - defines metrics, diagnoses drop-off, and prioritises by impact.
- Thinks and acts AI-first - uses AI across how they work and what they build.
- Senior PM craft - operates autonomously, partners closely with Engineering, drives alignment across Ops, Compliance, Legal, and GTM, and communicates clearly with leadership.
Nice to have
- Experience in the crypto / digital assets space (regulated fintech remains the must-have; crypto is a bonus).
- Experience building onboarding across multiple geographies and regulatory regimes.
- Familiarity with payments, cards and cross-border money movement.
- Prior work in a high-growth fintech scaling into new markets.

About the role
Payroll accuracy is non-negotiable. Every calculation, filing, and statutory deadline is a promise Rippling makes to customers and to the regulators who oversee them. Across our premium Global Payroll markets, that promise is kept by a team of Product Compliance experts embedded directly inside R&D. These experts sit alongside the local Product Lead and shape what gets built, how, and why. They write specs, test the product against regulatory requirements, and sit shoulder-to-shoulder with engineers to answer questions and provide feedback before anything reaches a customer.
We're looking for a Director to own our existing Global Payroll Compliance function: Per premium country, 1-2 Product Compliance experts are embedded in the organisation. These experts are an integral part of the local operating model that enables us to provide a premium payroll experience for customers in each market. They collaborate with stakeholders across a wide range of functions - next to R&D also spanning TaxOps, Support, and Implementation for solving real customer problems whenever these require compliance expertise. They also audit each country's software continuously, ensuring it abides by new local regulation.
This is as much a build role as a run role. You'll inherit a team that's already delivering, but you'll be the first person accountable for it as a function - defining what your team can decide independently, what needs escalation, and to whom, in close partnership with our corporate Compliance organisation.
Location: London - the team you'll lead is distributed across our premium Global Payroll markets (Canada, UK, India, Singapore, Australia, Germany, France)
What you'll do
• Lead the team. Coach and manage the Product Compliance leads embedded in each premium GP country, and build the career path for this function as it extends into new markets.
• Own the operating model. Formalise how Product Compliance works inside and outside of R&D - what's decided independently, what requires sign-off, and the escalation path for the rest - in partnership with our second-line Corporate Compliance function.
• Own regulatory monitoring and the global compliance roadmap. Ensure every market has clear visibility into compliance gaps and upcoming regulatory changes, with a defined process to document and spec them, and work closely with country Product Leads to get ahead of issues.
• Ensure global payroll accuracy. Own local quality reviews, audit preparation, and remediation across every market, and drive diagnosis with local compliance experts when payroll incidents occur.
• Partner across the business. Be the executive connective layer between Product Compliance on the one side and R&D, TaxOps, Support, Implementation, Legal, and Sales/GTM on the other.
• Own Help Center articles and communications. Build and maintain accurate, actionable content - help articles, country guides, regulatory notices - in partnership with PMs and Customer Education, so customers always have a reliable compliance experience.
• Define compliance year-end best practices. Year-end is a deadline that cannot slip - coordinate all year-end deliverables for each market (statutory filings, declarations, deadlines, and cross-functional dependencies) end-to-end, so customers close the fiscal year without surprises.
What you'll need
• 12+ years of experience in payroll, tax, or regulatory compliance, including meaningful people-leadership experience managing distributed subject-matter experts across multiple countries or jurisdictions.
• Proven ability to operate inside a product and engineering organization, not just alongside it - comfortable writing specs, reviewing designs, and participating in engineering rituals.
• Working knowledge of payroll compliance across at least some of our premium markets (Canada, UK, Ireland, Netherlands, Singapore, Australia, New Zealand, Germany, France, India). Breadth across several is a strong plus.
• Strong systems thinking: Able to build one consistent operating model across countries with different regulatory regimes and different levels of product maturity.
• Comfort with ambiguity: this is a new leadership layer for an existing team, so you'll be defining the operating model as much as running it.
• Excellent stakeholder management across Product, Engineering, TaxOps, Legal, Compliance, and GTM.
• High ownership mindset: Accountable for compliance outcomes, not just for managing the process around them.
• Strong alignment with our leadership principles, in particular Go and See, and Challenge Each Other Directly.

About the Role
We’re looking for a Senior Payroll Specialist to join Rippling’s Global Payroll Operations team and help lead payroll delivery for our EOR customers across the UK and Ireland.
Our Global Payroll Operations team plays a critical role in ensuring the success of Rippling’s global payroll products, which are natively built and fully integrated with Rippling’s broader suite of products. This role sits at the center of Rippling’s global payroll operations, helping scale country-specific expertise, operational controls, and payroll excellence across our UK and Ireland EOR business.
The Senior Payroll Specialist will own the most complex parts of the end-to-end payroll process, including escalations, corrections, off-cycle support, statutory payroll requirements, customer-facing payroll issues, and post-payroll resolution. Success in this role requires deep UK and Irish payroll knowledge, sharp judgment on tax and payroll treatment, and the ability to guide others through complex issues across pay types, earnings, deductions, reimbursements, allowances, pensions, statutory and leave-related payments, tax codes/RPNs, student loans, terminations, and HMRC or Irish Revenue-dependent cases.
This is a senior, highly cross-functional role for someone who can resolve high-complexity payroll issues, strengthen controls and documentation, coach payroll specialists, and partner with Product and Engineering on durable improvements to the EOR payroll experience.
What You Will Do
• Own complex EOR payroll processing for the UK and Ireland, including inputs, approvals, corrections, off-cycle payments, statutory payroll outputs, post-payroll review, and issue resolution.
• Act as a senior payroll and payroll tax subject-matter expert for escalations, including overpayments, final pay, redundancy pay, tax code/RPN issues, statutory documents, DEA/Attachment of Earnings deductions, Apprenticeship Levy, pension deductions, and HMRC/Revenue disputes.
• Create, review, and validate pay types, payroll inputs, and payroll configurations, ensuring earnings, deductions, reimbursements, benefits, allowances, statutory payments, and leave-related pay receive the correct payroll and tax treatment in each jurisdiction.
• Advise customers and internal teams on UK and Irish payroll requirements, including PAYE, National Insurance, PRSI, USC, auto-enrolment, pensions, taxable benefits, reimbursements, court/attachment deductions, student loans, and leave-related tax treatment.
• Review, reconcile, and validate payroll outputs, including payslips, filings, deductions, pension contributions, correction calculations, and off-cycle calculations across both markets.
• Strengthen payroll controls, audit checks, quality-review processes, SOPs, escalation playbooks, customer guidance, internal knowledge resources, and product/process feedback loops to reduce repeat issues, improve consistency, mentor payroll specialists, and support scalable payroll operations.
What You Will Need
• Expert-level understanding of UK and Irish payroll and tax compliance, including PAYE, National Insurance, PRSI, USC, PAYE Modernisation/RPNs, HMRC/Revenue filings and payments, statutory documents, Employment Detail Summaries, pensions, auto-enrolment, terminations, and year-end requirements.
• 5+ years of experience in UK and/or Irish payroll, payroll operations, payroll tax, or equivalent roles, ideally in a client-facing, EOR, or multi-customer environment.
• Significant experience managing end-to-end payroll processing and complex escalations, including audits, notices, disputes, HMRC/Revenue queries, and customer-facing payroll issue resolution.
• Strong working knowledge of payroll tax treatment across pay types, payroll inputs, earnings, deductions, benefits, reimbursements, allowances, statutory payments, leave-related pay, pensions, and other payroll components, with strong judgment on when PAYE, NI, PRSI, USC, pension, statutory, and reporting treatment applies.
• Experience with EOR or multi-country payroll operations, including how payroll connects to contract terms, worker classification, and the client-employer-EOR relationship.
• Excellent communication, analytical, prioritization, documentation, mentoring, and quality-review skills, with the ability to manage complex case queues and explain payroll issues clearly.
• Continuous-improvement mindset, strong attention to detail, and comfort working across operational systems, documentation tools, and case-management platforms; familiarity with Salesforce, JIRA, and Confluence is a plus.

About the role
After becoming one of the fastest growing startups in the United States, Rippling is ready to up level our growth engine to scale to $1B in ARR over the next couple years, including through international expansion and the addition of new products like Global Payroll, Employer of Record, and Spend Management. Investing in our finance, operational, and entity expansion is a key priority to enable future business growth.
Rippling Payments UK Limited (“RPay UK”) is an authorised Electronic Money Institution supervised by the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) and is a wholly owned subsidiary of Rippling. As Head of Compliance Oversight and CEO of the UK Rpay entity, you will hold a Senior Management Function under the senior managers and certification regime. You will be accountable to the Board of Directors for the leadership, governance and performance of the Rpay UK entity. This role requires a proven leader in global payments and financial infrastructure, someone who can scale complex operations and ensure operational resilience in a dynamic, high-growth environment. This role will require you to be residing in the United Kingdom and come onsite to the London office. What you will do
Strategic & Business Leadership
• Lead the implementation of group strategy within Rippling Payments UK, ensuring effective, compliant, and resilient execution of all payments and operational activities.
• Lead the delivery of sustainable growth across Rpay UK payments and e-money activities, driving operational excellence and customer trust.
• Provide oversight of all functions of RPay UK, including operations, finance, risk and compliance, ensuring effective coordination with Rippling Product, Engineering, and Payment Operations.
• Represent RPay UK within Rippling’s global operational structure, providing insight and strategic guidance on UK payment operations.
Payments Operations Oversight
• Partner with Rippling Product, Engineering, and Payment Operations to ensure payments infrastructure and operations are robust, scalable, and designed for continuous improvement.
• Contribute as a thought-leader to global programs focused on payments automation, monitoring, and control systems.
Governance & Board Engagement
• Maintain strong governance frameworks and ensure clear apportionment of responsibilities across Rpay UK senior management team.
• Report regularly to the Board on operational performance, financial health, key risks, and major incidents.
• Ensure Board visibility and oversight of critical decisions, ensuring transparent communication and timely escalation of material matters.
• Foster a governance culture grounded in integrity, accountability, and prudent risk-taking.
Leadership & Culture
• Foster a culture of excellence, innovation, and accountability, with an emphasis on collaboration between Irish operations and global teams.
• Model ethical leadership and a commitment to customer protection, operational discipline, and long-term sustainability.
• Ensure leadership continuity and succession planning across key roles and functions.
What you will need
The successful candidate will be an accomplished executive with deep experience in global payments operations, incident leadership, and scaling regulated financial infrastructure.
Experience & Capabilities
• 10+ years’ experience in senior leadership roles within global payments, fintech, or financial services.
• Proven leadership in global payments operations, treasury management, or e-money issuance at scale.
• Demonstrated success leading major operational or technology incidents, with direct accountability for business continuity, stakeholder management, and recovery outcomes.
• Experience operating within or leading a regulated financial entity, with comfort engaging directly with Boards and regulators.
• Strong understanding of payments systems and networks.
• Strategic operator with a data-driven approach to performance, risk, and operational design.
Preferred Qualifications
• Prior CEO, COO, CRO or equivalent SMF role in a regulated payments or fintech entity.
• Relevant degree in business, finance, or technology; postgraduate or professional qualifications in leadership, governance, or risk management an advantage.
• Familiarity with enterprise-scale payments infrastructure, cloud systems, and API-based payment models.
Even if you don’t meet all of the requirements listed here, we still encourage you to apply. Skills can be used in lots of different ways and your life and professional experience may be relevant beyond what a list of requirements will capture.
Rippling is an equal opportunity employer.

• Design and build scalable, data-driven systems that transform, normalize, and reconcile payroll data across multiple countries, entities, and currencies.
• Drive platform evolution by re-architecting critical systems for scalability, reliability, and internationalization—enabling global payroll operations at scale.
• Develop AI- and ML-driven solutions to enhance accuracy, detect anomalies, automate workflows, and minimize manual intervention.

Scope automates the data collection that's slowing down the physical world.
Standards are vital for the safety of our infrastructure. Spending hours manually documenting them is not.
Dave is an inspector. Today he’s climbing through one of Europe’s biggest chemical plants, looking for the corrosion that could shut the whole site down, with a notebook and pen in hand. Tomorrow, he’ll spend even longer on the part of the job he hates: turning those scribbles into a report.
We’re building the AI-native data collection layer for the 2 billion field workers like Dave. Scope radically simplifies how inspectors collect data in the field, make decisions, and produce reports. Along the way, we’re building the largest dataset on the condition of the built world and the decisions experts make about it.
It’s a $2T market and we’re just getting started. We're growing rapidly, and already work with 7 of the top 10 companies in the space. Our customers inspect facilities and products for companies including AstraZeneca and SpaceX.
We take pride in our talent density, and have assembled a best-in-class team: acquired and future founders, people from institutions like Imperial, Carnegie Mellon and Oxford, and from firms like Palantir, Goldman Sachs and Flexport .

About the role
Real product ownership. You’ll go on site with inspectors, decide what matters, design it, ship it, and see whether it worked.
The hard, interesting problems in AI. Field data is messy: voice notes, photos, video, half-finished sentences recorded in a chemical plant with no signal. Turning that into a report an expert will sign is a context-engineering problem nobody has solved well yet.
A small team that ships fast. We ship to production every day and put changes in front of inspectors within days, not quarters. Ideas go from a site visit to a live feature in a single sprint. If something doesn’t land, we learn why and iterate quickly. There are no layers of sign-off between you and the user.

Redesign the mobile app for how inspectors actually work: gloves on, no signal, one hand holding on
Build the systems that takes voice notes, photos, videos and proactively finishes reports without being annoying
Engineer how we feed context to AI models: how to store, fetch and select standards, reports, media, user intention
Evolve our workflow builder: something between Retool, Webflow and n8n for inspections
Design the architecture behind the product: how unstructured data flows through the system, how AI is integrated, how offline and online behaviour stay seamless, and how we keep the product simple as it becomes more powerful.
Who you are
You’re deeply technical. You’re a little bit sad that AI tooling creates more distance between you and the code, and you still like knowing how things work underneath.
You’re a manager of one. We believe great teams are made up of highly agentic people who care more about shipping results than collecting badges.

You’ve shipped real applications. Ideally mobile, ideally with Expo or React Native. You care about the details that break in the real world: offline, flaky networks, error states.
You’re curious about AI as an engineering problem. You’re interested in getting messy real-world inputs into a model and getting something reliable back out, not just in calling an API.

Director, Environmental Sustainability Management
Meet the Team
Cisco's Chief Sustainability Office works across the company to advance our environmental sustainability strategy, deliver our goals and help translate complex environmental and technology challenges into informed business decisions.
Our team brings together expertise across net zero, circularity, product sustainability, engineering and supply chain enablement, environmental data and analytics, reporting and disclosure, and stakeholder engagement. Our leaders and teams have deep knowledge of their areas and are responsible for turning Cisco's sustainability priorities into action.
At the same time, the questions we face are becoming more complex and interconnected. The rapid growth of artificial intelligence and digital infrastructure is changing energy demand, technology systems and resource requirements. Energy markets are evolving, new constraints are emerging across supply chains and materials, and the assumptions underpinning long-term environmental strategies continue to change.
We are looking for a Director, Environmental Sustainability Management, to strengthen our ability to understand these developments and determine what they mean for Cisco.
Reporting directly to the Chief Sustainability Officer, you will work across the Chief Sustainability Office and broader Cisco organization, combining deep subject-matter expertise, quantitative analysis and external insight to help teams investigate complex questions, evaluate different approaches and develop credible strategies and recommendations.
Your Impact
As Director, Environmental Sustainability Management, you will serve as a strategic and analytical partner to the Chief Sustainability Officer and leaders across Cisco.
You will bring deep analytical capability and specialist expertise to questions where technology, energy, environmental and business considerations intersect, particularly where the evidence is evolving, assumptions need to be tested, or where teams would benefit from deeper research, modelling and scenario analysis.
Your initial focus will include Cisco’s updated Sustainability Strategy, AI and digital infrastructure and Cisco's Energy Resilience priority. You will help Cisco understand how changes in technology, energy and resource systems could affect its sustainability and business strategy and turn that understanding into actionable choices.
You will:
• Work across the Chief Sustainability Office and Cisco including with supply chain, product engineering, government affairs, workplace resources, sales and other teams to understand emerging developments, bring together different perspectives and evidence, and translate them into strategic implications, options and recommendations
• Strengthen priority sustainability workstreams with additional analytical depth, helping teams test assumptions, develop scenarios, evaluate emerging technologies and understand how changes in the external environment could affect their strategies and plans.
• Develop Cisco's perspective on the environmental implications of AI and digital infrastructure, including energy demand, greenhouse gas emissions, infrastructure requirements, materials, circularity and other lifecycle impacts across hardware, software, networks and supporting infrastructure.
• Analyze developments in energy systems and electricity markets, including demand growth, data center expansion, generation, grid constraints, technology economics and investment dynamics, and assess their implications for Cisco's sustainability, technology and business strategies.
• Support Cisco's net-zero strategy through quantitative analysis and scenario modelling, examining how technology adoption, business growth, energy-system developments and other external factors could affect emissions pathways, assumptions and strategic choices.
• Assess interactions between technology, energy, supply chains and resource demand, including critical materials and circularity, to identify emerging risks, opportunities, dependencies, trade-offs and unintended consequences.
• Develop, commission and apply rigorous models, scenarios and analytical frameworks to evaluate environmental impacts and competing strategic approaches, applying appropriate baselines, lifecycle boundaries, attribution methods and sensitivity analysis and making uncertainty explicit.
• Translate complex scientific, technical, economic and policy evidence into decision-ready recommendations, helping senior leaders understand what matters, what is known, what remains uncertain and what choices Cisco can make.
• Provide constructive analytical challenge to strategies, proposals and sustainability claims, helping teams identify weak assumptions, test whether expected outcomes are supported by the evidence and strengthen the credibility and defensibility of their work.
• Build relationships with leading researchers, institutions, customers and industry experts to bring external insight into Cisco, test emerging hypotheses and identify opportunities for collaboration.
• Represent Cisco selectively in research collaborations, industry initiatives, standards organizations and expert forums, strengthening Cisco's technical credibility and contributing to external discussions where the company has meaningful expertise and evidence to offer.
The portfolio will evolve as Cisco's priorities and the external landscape change. You should be comfortable moving between subjects, developing expertise quickly and working alongside different teams depending on where your analysis and perspective can have the greatest impact.
Minimum Qualifications
• Degree in engineering, physical or environmental sciences, economics, energy systems, computer science, public policy or another relevant quantitative or technical discipline, or equivalent demonstrated expertise.
• Deep expertise across at least two of the following areas, with demonstrated experience connecting them: AI, computing and digital infrastructure; energy systems and markets; climate, net zero and environmental impacts. Additional expertise in one or more of the following is preferred: circular economy; lifecycle assessment; electronics supply chains; or critical raw materials.
• Demonstrated external recognition as a subject-matter expert at the intersection of digital infrastructure, AI, energy and environmental sustainability, evidenced by one or more of the following: authorship or formal peer review of influential research or publications; leadership roles in respected institutions, industry initiatives or consortia; significant contributions to standards or policy; or comparable externally scrutinized work.
• Significant experience conducting quantitative analysis, modelling, scenario development or strategic research related to energy, climate, digital technologies, environmental impacts, resource systems or a closely related field.
• Demonstrated ability to structure ambiguous and complex problems, identify the questions that materially affect a decision and develop rigorous analytical approaches to address them.
• Demonstrated ability to translate complex scientific, technical or economic analysis into strategic options and recommendations for senior decision-makers.
• Experience developing or interpreting quantitative models and scenarios and working with incomplete or uncertain data, including clearly communicating assumptions, sensitivities and limitations.
• Experience working effectively across disciplines and organizational boundaries, collaborating with subject-matter experts and influencing outcomes without relying on formal authority.
• Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to make complex technical analysis accessible and relevant to executive and expert audiences.
Preferred Qualifications
• Master's degree, PhD or equivalent advanced analytical experience in a relevant technical, scientific, energy, economics or policy discipline.
• Deep understanding of the relationship between AI, computing and digital infrastructure and energy systems, emissions, materials and other environmental impacts.
• Experience developing or applying models related to electricity demand, energy systems, data centers, digital technologies, greenhouse gas emissions, net-zero pathways, lifecycle impacts or material demand.
• Knowledge of electricity markets, energy-system investment and the infrastructure implications of growing digital and data-center demand.
• Knowledge of critical materials, technology supply chains, circularity and the resource implications of emerging technologies.
• Experience developing strategies or recommendations that required balancing environmental evidence with technical feasibility, economics, customer requirements, commercial considerations and organizational constraints.
• Experience working with leading research institutions, policymakers, standards organizations, industry associations, customers or other expert communities.
• Experience representing an organization externally on complex or emerging technical issues and communicating with both specialist and non-specialist audiences.
• Ability to learn unfamiliar subject areas quickly, challenge conventional thinking constructively and exercise sound judgement where evidence is incomplete, contested or changing rapidly.

Job Title: HR Data Analyst
Salary: £34,638 - £39,309 per annum
Grade: D
Contract Type: Permanent 
Working Hours: 37 hours per week

About the Department 

The HR Data and Systems Team is responsible for managing and maintaining the
organisation’s workforce data and HR systems, ensuring employee information is
accurate, up to date and compliant with statutory requirements. As the
administrators of Oracle HCM, the team supports the delivery of efficient HR
services through the processing of contractual changes, provision of workforce
data and reporting, coordination of government returns and management of HR
related information requests, including Freedom of Information responses. The
team also serves as the first point of contact for employees and managers with
HR data and systems queries, while working closely with stakeholders to support
system improvements, testing and the implementation of new functionality.
Through its expertise in data management and HR systems, the team provides the
essential foundation for informed decision-making and effective workforce
management across the organisation.

About the Role 

Key Responsibilities

- Oracle HCM Data Management

 * Maintain and update employee records within Oracle HCM, ensuring accuracy,
   completeness and compliance with organisational policies.
 * Process workforce changes including:
   * New starters
   * Leavers
   * Transfers
   * Secondments
   * Contract variations
   * Position changes
   * Organisational restructures
 * Create, amend and manage positions within Oracle HCM in accordance with
   approved establishment controls.
 * Perform data validation and quality assurance checks to ensure data integrity
   across HR and payroll systems.
 * Support system testing and implementation of Oracle HCM enhancements and
   upgrades where required.
 * Ensure all payroll-related employee information is accurately recorded and
   maintained within payroll cut off dates.
 * Process and validate employee changes impacting payroll, ensuring compliance
   with payroll deadlines.
 * Liaise with Payroll teams to resolve data discrepancies and support payroll
   processing activities.
 * Investigate and rectify data issues affecting employee pay, contractual
   information or reporting.
 * Produce scheduled and ad-hoc workforce reports using Oracle HCM and
   associated reporting tools.
 * Analyse workforce data to identify trends, anomalies and key workforce
   metrics.
 * Provide accurate management information relating to:
   * Headcount
   * Establishment
   * Vacancies
   * Turnover
   * Absence
   * Diversity and equality monitoring
   * Recruitment activity
 * Develop and maintain reporting dashboards and datasets to support
   organisational decision-making.

 

- Payroll Data Administration

- Workforce Reporting and Analysis

- HR Support and Customer Service

 * Manage and respond to HR support tickets within agreed service standards.
 * Provide guidance and support to managers and employees on HR systems,
   processes and workforce data queries.
 * Investigate and resolve data-related issues raised through HR support
   channels.
 * Escalate complex cases where appropriate and maintain clear records of
   actions taken.

 

- Information Governance and FOI Requests

 * Support responses to Freedom of Information (FOI), Subject Access Requests
   (SARs), and other information requests.
 * Extract, validate and provide workforce data in line with statutory
   requirements and organisational policies.
 * Ensure compliance with UK GDPR, Data Protection legislation and
   confidentiality requirements when handling employee information.

 

What We’re Looking For 

We’re looking for someone who has: 

 * At least 2 years' experience of working in a similar role within a Human
   Resources department.
 * A keen eye for detail and demonstratable accurate data input skills

Senior Legal Counsel - Product and Regulatory Compliance
Farringdon, London, United Kingdom
Hybrid - Minimum 6 days per month onsite
About the Role
This is a senior legal role with a strong focus on product, technology and regulatory compliance at Toyota Connected Europe (“TCEU”).
TCEU develops and supports connected-vehicle, data, digital and mobility products and services used across Europe. As regulation of data, AI, digital products and connected technologies continues to develop, we are looking for a lawyer who can help the business understand these requirements and translate them into practical, proportionate actions.
You will work closely with Product, Engineering, Data, Information Security, Privacy and other business teams throughout the product and service lifecycle – from early design and development through launch and ongoing operation.
A key part of the role will be supporting TCEU’s response to emerging and evolving regulatory requirements, including the EU Data Act, EU AI Act and other data, digital, technology and product regulation relevant to our activities. You will help identify applicable requirements, assess their impact and work with accountable business owners to embed appropriate requirements, controls and governance into products and services.
This is a practical, hands-on role. You will be expected not only to interpret legislation, but also to help the business determine what needs to change, who needs to own it, and how compliance can be demonstrated.
Alongside this regulatory focus, you will provide broader technology and commercial legal support where required and contribute to the continued development of TCEU’s Legal & Compliance framework.
Key Responsibilities
• Advise Product, Engineering, Design and other teams on legal and regulatory requirements affecting TCEU’s products and services, from initial concept and design through deployment and ongoing operation.
• Lead or support legal analysis and implementation of relevant regulatory requirements, including the EU Data Act, EU AI Act, GDPR and other applicable data, digital, AI, cybersecurity, consumer and product-related regulation.
• Translate complex regulatory requirements into clear and practical guidance, product requirements, controls, governance processes and documentation that can be understood and implemented by technical and business teams.
• Carry out regulatory applicability and impact assessments for new and existing products, services, technologies and use cases, helping the business identify legal obligations, risks and required mitigation.
• Promote a compliance-by-design approach, ensuring that regulatory considerations are identified early in the product development lifecycle rather than addressed only at the point of launch.
• Support TCEU’s governance of AI systems and AI-enabled products and services, including assessment of regulatory requirements, risk classification, transparency, documentation and appropriate controls.
• Monitor relevant UK and EU legal and regulatory developments and assess their potential impact on TCEU, Toyota group companies and the wider connected-mobility environment.
• Work closely with Data Privacy, Information Security, Compliance and other specialists to ensure that overlapping regulatory requirements are addressed consistently and efficiently.
• Advise on technology and commercial agreements where appropriate, particularly where contracts involve significant data, AI, software, intellectual property, cybersecurity or regulatory considerations.
• Develop practical guidance, playbooks, training and awareness materials to help Product, Engineering and other teams understand their regulatory responsibilities.
• Coordinate with external counsel and Toyota group legal and compliance teams where specialist advice or group-wide alignment is required.
• Contribute to the continuous improvement of TCEU’s wider Legal & Compliance framework, including the use of technology and AI to improve regulatory monitoring, legal analysis and compliance processes.
About You:
You are an experienced lawyer who is interested in how regulation applies to real-world technology products and services.
You are comfortable moving beyond traditional legal advice and working directly with Product, Engineering and other technical teams to turn legal requirements into practical solutions.
You can take complex or evolving legislation, identify what is genuinely relevant to the business and explain it clearly without unnecessary legal complexity. You are pragmatic and commercially minded, but equally comfortable challenging the business where regulatory risk requires it.
You enjoy working in areas where the law is still developing and where there may not always be a clear precedent or established process. You are able to work independently, exercise sound judgement and bring structure to ambiguous regulatory issues.
Essential Experience:
• Qualified lawyer with approximately 5+ years’ post-qualification experience, or equivalent relevant experience.
• Significant experience advising on technology, digital products, data or regulatory matters, either in-house or in private practice.
• Working knowledge of key emerging regulatory frameworks such as the EU Data Act and EU AI Act, together with relevant data protection requirements.
• Experience working directly with Product, Engineering, Technology, Data or similar cross-functional teams.
• Ability to analyse new and evolving areas of regulation where established guidance or precedent may be limited.
• Strong written and spoken English, with the ability to explain complex regulatory issues clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.
• Strong judgement, attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple regulatory and legal priorities independently.
Nice to Have:
• Experience working within a technology, software, SaaS, automotive, connected-vehicle or mobility business.
• Experience with regulatory areas such as cybersecurity, connected products, digital services, consumer law, product safety or emerging technology regulation.
• Experience developing compliance-by-design, product governance or regulatory change management frameworks.
• Experience advising on AI governance, including the legal assessment of AI systems, products or business use cases.
• Experience working within an international corporate group or matrix organisation and coordinating legal or regulatory positions across multiple jurisdictions.
• Experience delivering training and practical regulatory guidance to Product, Engineering or other business teams.
Context
TCEU was founded in London in 2019 to process and derive insights from the connected data produced by Toyota and Lexus vehicles in Europe. In 2026, with almost 3 million connected cars on the road and over 2 billion journeys processed each year, TCEU continues to scale its software, data and engineering capabilities across Europe.

Welcome
Thanks for taking the time to consider Tuza.
When joining a company at the early stages of its growth story, there's often more than meets the eye. This is our opportunity to help you understand why your next role should be with us.
We're based in Shoreditch, spend three days a week in the office, and can sponsor visas for the right candidate.
Diversity is a priority for us. We build a better product when the people building it don't all think the same way.
If you're still unsure at the end, drop into our offices in Shoreditch and see it for yourself.
## What we do
We build AI agents for banks, taking on the manual work that stops them from growing.
Every business that comes to a bank for a financial product gets passed from team to team, sales to onboarding to activation, and so on. Right now, every one of those teams is only ever as fast as the number of people in it. Our agents do that work without the ceiling. To be trusted with it in a bank, they have to be accurate, quick, and accountable, with auditability, explainability and security built in rather than an afterthought. That's what makes banks the hardest place to attempt this, and the place where getting it right is worth the most.
## Where we're at
We've raised $7 million from Northzone, Connect Ventures and TriplePoint, and work with acquiring banks including Worldpay, Barclaycard and NatWest.
We're earlier than that list makes us sound. The problem is real, and banks are already paying us to solve it. We're still experimenting with the product that best surfaces our value, and that's a large part of this job, rather than something that will be handed to you finished.
Doing that work is a small but driven team of 12 based in our Shoreditch office who care about their work and its impact.
There's also something you might already know us for. We built the UK's first payments price comparison platform, helping small businesses compare providers. It still runs today on MoneySuperMarket, Uswitch and money.co.uk. You won't be working on it, but it's why we know this market so well.
## How we work
- Extreme ownership: you own the outcome of your work, not just the output. If you see something broken or missing, you have the freedom and the responsibility to fix it.
- Learning velocity: curious, adaptable, and quick to pick things up. Hard problems require grit, and we embrace them.
- Customer-centric: we spend a day a week inside our partner banks, watching problems happen before they're even reported. Product decisions get made in that room, not in a roadmap meeting.
- Open and direct: we communicate openly, directly, and with intent.
## What you'll do
- Develop and optimise AI agents for live banking workflows
- Design review gates, fail-safes, and fallback behaviour
- Build the observability and feedback loops behind agent performance
- Spend time with our partner banks in their offices, and turn what you see there into product changes
## What we look for
We're hiring mid- to senior-level individual contributors with at least 4 years' experience.
- Exceptional Python and experience orchestrating LLMs with tools like Temporal or LangChain
- AI automation shipped and running in production
- A record of making agents reliable and efficient
- Fluency with data pipelines and integrations
We're an early-stage and intentionally lean. That means:
- We judge impact by the outcome of work, not the output
- Priorities shift when we learn something new, and we try to communicate why, but it happens
- You'll be given a direction, and the plan is yours to work out
This suits people who are comfortable with ambiguity, ask early when context is missing, and would rather ship something good enough fast than perfect something late.
It's less suited for those who prefer clear hierarchies, detailed briefs, or predictable roadmaps. That's not a character flaw; we just don't offer that yet.
Probation is a mutual check-in. We give feedback as we go, and we expect the same in return. If the fit isn't there, we'd rather know at month two than month six.
## How you'll be assessed
Our aim is to get candidates through the whole process within two weeks of applying — quick enough to respect your time, thorough enough to keep our standards high.

Click Apply Now to email us your CV, LinkedIn or GitHub
02
20-minute intro call to talk through your background, what you're looking for, and how we work
03
40-minute technical interview digging into products you've built and the decisions behind them
04
3-hour technical assessment, ideally at our Shoreditch office but remote works too
05
30-minute conversation with our CEO, Ed, to close things out and answer anything still on your mind
## What's in it for you
- A competitive salary and generous equity
- Three days a week in our Shoreditch office, Tuesday to Thursday, and the rest wherever you work best
- 25 days holiday, with flexibility when you need it
- £350 a year towards taking a proper break
- £350 a year towards learning or a hobby
- Smart, kind colleagues who care about the work
- Soundbaths, terrarium making, saunas, cooked breakfasts, barbecues on the rooftop and the occasional Mario Kart tournament

The Sector Lead will build and lead an integrated Tyréns UK data centre proposition, bringing together the complementary expertise of Tyréns Hilson Moran and Tyréns AKT. The combined offer spans power and utilities, MEP engineering, structural and civil engineering, sustainability, environmental planning, embodied carbon, infrastructure, technical due diligence, refurbishment and operational optimisation.
The role will position Tyréns UK as a strategic adviser across the full data centre lifecycle, from site selection, capacity enablement and early feasibility through design, delivery, refurbishment and operation. By connecting multidisciplinary expertise, the Sector Lead will help clients address power, planning, environmental, infrastructure and engineering constraints early enough to improve investment and delivery decisions.
This is primarily a commercial and relationship-led role rather than a hands-on design position. The successful candidate will nevertheless bring sufficient delivery experience in a relevant specialist discipline to engage credibly with clients and technical teams. THM’s portfolio includes work for IBM, Global Switch, the Bank of England and BCS across new-build and refurbishment projects, providing a strong platform from which to grow in the colocation and hyperscale markets.
### Key responsibilities
**Sales and commercial leadership**
- Own and deliver agreed annual sales, order-intake, net revenue, margin and pipeline targets for the data centre sector.
- Create and maintain a qualified pipeline with sufficient coverage to support both the annual business plan and longer-term growth ambitions.
- Lead major pursuits, bids, negotiations and client conversion strategies across Tyréns UK.
- Develop strategic account plans for priority developers, investors, operators, hyperscale occupiers, colocation providers and delivery partners.
- Drive cross-selling between Tyréns Hilson Moran and Tyréns AKT, increasing the proportion of opportunities that use the combined multidisciplinary offer.
- Report sales performance, pipeline quality, conversion, forecast revenue and commercial risks against agreed targets.
**Market growth and client relationships**
- Own and strengthen Tyréns UK’s profile, reputation and proposition in the data centre market.
- Bring established industry relationships and convert them into a qualified pipeline of profitable opportunities.
- Develop opportunities across the UK and selected European markets in collaboration with the wider Tyréns Group.
- Represent Tyréns UK at industry events, forums and senior client meetings, building influence and brand recognition.
**Multidisciplinary proposition and delivery**
- Bring together Tyréns Hilson Moran’s expertise in MEP engineering, power, sustainability, environment and technical advisory with Tyréns AKT’s expertise in structural engineering, civil engineering, design innovation and complex project delivery.
- Work closely with the HV Engineering Specialist and discipline leaders across Tyréns Hilson Moran and Tyréns AKT to ensure that proposed solutions and client commitments are technically robust and deliverable.
- Shape integrated propositions that address site capacity, power, planning, infrastructure, building performance, carbon and delivery risk as a connected client challenge.
**Capability and team development**
- Build a collaborative UK data centre community with clear priorities, shared market intelligence and consistent client messaging.
- Support recruitment, succession planning and the development of colleagues from adjacent sectors as the practice grows.
- Use market demand, pipeline evidence and sales forecasts to inform investment and capability-building decisions.

- A current, active network across the data centre ecosystem, including developers, investors, operators, hyperscale occupiers, colocation providers and strategic delivery partners.
- A demonstrable record of achieving sales and growth targets, winning work, growing key accounts and sustaining senior client relationships.

- Senior leadership experience at Director level within engineering, consulting or real estate advisory, or in a credible client-side role.
- Direct project delivery experience in data centres, power and grid connection, or wider mission-critical infrastructure.
- Confidence representing an organisation externally and building a differentiated multidisciplinary proposition.

- Experience engaging with DNOs, IDNOs and NESO, even where detailed grid strategy was led by others.
- Relationships across both colocation and hyperscale markets and a strong understanding of the wider investment, development and infrastructure ecosystem.
- Experience converting single-discipline relationships into broader multidisciplinary commissions.

- the de-risking and delivery of complex utility enabling works including temporary and permanent diversions and disconnections within major building and infrastructure projects often in constrained urban environments.
**Your Responsibilities Will Include, But Are Not Limited To:**
- Together with our Associate Directors and Directors meet with commercial and residential developers and/or landowners, and their supply chain including Architects, Planning Consultants and Project Managers, to understand development needs, both technical and commercial drivers, and develop proposals that meet their needs.
- Once appointed by a client then consult with the wider design team, but particularly utility undertakers and other utilities, energy, and data service providers to understand opportunities, risks and costs associated with our client’s development proposals and advise of these risks, costs and opportunities via meetings, sketches, presentations and reports.

Our mission
We're making Africa the first cashless continent.
In 2017, over half the population in Sub-Saharan Africa had no bank account. That's for good reason—the fees are too high, the closest branch can be miles away, and nobody takes cards. Without access to financial institutions, people are forced to keep their savings under the mattress. Small business owners rely on lenders who charge extortionate rates. Parents spend hours waiting in line to pay school fees in cash.
We're solving this by building financial services that just work: no account fees, instantly available, and accepted everywhere. In places where electricity, water and roads don't always work, you can still send money with Wave. About Us
Craven Street Wealth is an award-winning Chartered financial planning and wealth management firm, helping individuals, families and businesses make confident financial decisions. We combine expert advice with a personal approach, building long-term relationships that help our clients achieve their goals. With offices across London and the South of England, our teams work collaboratively to deliver outstanding service and tailored financial planning solutions. As part of Quanta Group, we're backed by the strength of a wider financial services group that includes Wealthtime and Copia Capital. While each business operates independently, we share a commitment to delivering excellent client outcomes, supporting our people to grow and creating an environment where everyone can thrive. We know that our success comes from our people. That's why we're committed to creating a supportive, collaborative culture where everyone can develop their skills, contribute ideas and build a rewarding career.
About the Role
To work alongside and support the advisory team in promoting and delivering excellent financial planning advice to new and existing clients, in line with the company’s strategy and supported by the Technical and Advice Reporting, Client Services and Client Processing teams. The role will involve significant responsibility for preparing for client meetings, ensuring follow ups are delivered in a timely manner and with a high level of accuracy with the ability to provide and/or sign off the advice independently where required as well as supporting growth by developing an individual client bank.
Key Responsibilities:
Client Service Delivery
• Support the advisory teams in developing and delivering a client service strategy that ensures existing clients are managed to the highest standards.
• Support Senior Financial Planners and Financial Planners to ensure clients receive good value from our service, assisting with quality control so that all client work and supporting documentation meets the highest standards.
• Where appropriate, engage directly with clients to build trusted relationships.
Achieving Good Client Outcomes
• Support the advisory teams in delivering a consistently high-quality service that drives client engagement and keeps attrition low.
• Proactively help ensure every client receives a positive experience and take appropriate action to support good client outcomes.
• Deliver client work to advisory teams in a timely, effective and efficient manner, with a high degree of accuracy.
• Accurately undertake the implementation of client advice.
Working as a Team
• Work collaboratively with the Technical and Advice Reporting, Client Services and Client Processing teams
• Demonstrate and promote CSW’s values and behaviours throughout the
• organisation.
• Work closely with colleagues to ensure all clients receive excellent service and agreed service-level agreements are met.
• Prepare proactively for regular one-to-one meetings and actively seek opportunities to develop experience and competencies.
Service Development
• Participate in and support key projects and practice or technical initiatives across the business as required.
• Provide constructive feedback on new and existing processes to support their
• ongoing development.
Conduct
• Act as a brand ambassador for CSW, promoting our services, values and behaviours to support good client outcomes and meet conduct responsibilities.
• Maintain appropriate continuing professional development (CPD).
• Read and understand all technical research and legislative or regulatory updates provided by internal departments.
• Maintain up-to-date technical knowledge and ensure all work complies with the relevant regulatory and legal requirements.
This isn't an exhaustive list and responsibilities may evolve over time to meet the needs of the business.
About You
Specialist Skills, Qualifications and Experience:
Essential:
• Diploma in Regulated Financial Planning. The Diploma requires 100 CII credits through completion of the six compulsory units R01–R06.
• Commitment to self-study to become a Chartered Financial Planner.
Desirable:
• A relevant degree
Skills and Knowledge:
• A client-centric approach, with a commitment to understanding clients’ needs and delivering consistently positive outcomes.
• Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
• A collaborative team player with a proven track record.
• A positive attitude and a resilient, flexible approach.
• Approachable and available to colleagues and clients.
• Acts with honesty and integrity.
• Willingness to participate in the wider activities of the business.
• Ability to work effectively as part of a team.
We recognise that great candidates come from a variety of backgrounds and experiences. If you're excited by the opportunity but don't meet every requirement, we'd still love to hear from you.

• Hybrid working, with time split between home and office.
• Discretionary annual bonus.
• 34 days holiday per calendar year, including bank holidays, with the option to purchase up to five additional days per year.
• Supported and encouraged professional development.
• Contributory pension scheme
• Medical cashback plan, helping cover the cost of everyday healthcare expenses such as dental treatment, eye care and physiotherapy.
• Occupational sick pay scheme.
• Group income protection scheme.
• Life assurance scheme
• Cycle to Work scheme.
• Up to 10 hours of volunteering leave each year.
• Opportunities for internal progression within Craven Street Wealth and across the wider Quanta Group.
• A collaborative and supportive culture where colleagues are encouraged to grow, contribute and succeed.
Craven Street Wealth is an equal opportunities employer and we're committed to creating an inclusive workplace where everyone feels valued, respected and able to be themselves.
We recognise that people work in different ways and bring different experiences, perspectives and ideas. We believe these differences make us stronger and help us deliver better outcomes for our clients and colleagues.
We welcome applications from everyone, regardless of background, beliefs, culture, gender identity, ethnicity, sexual orientation, disability or long-term health condition.

job_description:
SENIOR AI / COMPUTER VISION ENGINEER
Build the spatial AI behind the future of construction
At XYZ Reality https://www.xyzreality.com, we've created the world's first engineering-grade Augmented Reality solution for construction. Our technology, The Atom, is already being used on major construction projects around the world to help teams build more accurately, efficiently and with fewer mistakes.
Our R&D team applies computer vision, spatial AI and machine learning to one of the most demanding real-world settings there is: the active construction site.
We’re looking for a Senior AI / Computer Vision Engineer with deep expertise in 3D computer vision and spatial AI to join the team and help develop the perception technology behind our products.
As a Series B business entering our next phase of growth, we're investing in our R&D capability and growing our team. This great opportunity will be based out of our Angel, London office on a hybrid basis, 2-3 days per week.
The Role
This is an opportunity to solve computer vision problems that exist at the intersection of the digital and physical world.
You’ll develop the perception and scene-understanding systems that enable our wearable technology to recognise construction objects, understand complex 3D environments, and relate what’s on site to the design model, using real-world sensor data.
For this role, 3D / spatial computer vision expertise is fundamental. We’re looking for someone who understands how AI and computer vision can reason about physical space, not simply someone with broader AI or machine learning experience.
You’ll work across research, algorithm development, optimisation, deployment and productisation, taking sophisticated computer vision techniques and turning them into robust technology capable of performing on active construction sites.
You’ll bring senior technical expertise to the team as we build our capability and presence in Calgary. You’ll also collaborate closely with our Navigation, Embedded Software, Hardware and Product teams across the wider business.
This is a role where you can combine deep technical work with real-world impact, seeing the algorithms and systems you develop ultimately deployed through wearable technology on some of the world's most complex construction projects.
What You’ll Be Doing
- Develop advanced computer vision algorithms for construction scene understanding and spatial intelligence.
- Design and develop semantic segmentation, object detection and instance segmentation models.
- Build algorithms capable of understanding 3D environments, spatial relationships and physical geometry.
- Develop automated BIM correspondence and object-matching capabilities.
- Develop algorithms using multi-modal sensor data.
- Combine AI, 3D vision, SLAM and BIM to develop geometric and spatial reasoning capabilities.
- Explore emerging scene representation techniques including Gaussian Splatting and NeRFs.
- Improve localisation-assisted perception and robustness across varying lighting, weather and real-world site conditions.
- Design, train and evaluate large-scale deep learning models.
- Develop data pipelines supporting supervised, self-supervised and semi-supervised learning.
- Evaluate emerging foundation models, multimodal AI and modern computer vision techniques where they can add meaningful value.
- Optimise models for embedded deployment, improving inference speed, accuracy and robustness.
- Deploy and optimise models for embedded GPU platforms.
- Build and improve production inference pipelines, benchmarking performance, latency and accuracy.
- Contribute to technical architecture, design reviews and our technical direction.
- Share knowledge and mentor other engineers as the team continues to grow.
What We’re Looking For
- 5+ years’ industrial experience in Computer Vision, with strong hands-on experience solving complex technical problems.
- MSc or PhD in Computer Vision, AI, Computer Science or a related discipline.
- Experience with perception for autonomous or embodied systems, such as SLAM, sensor fusion or state estimation, would be valuable.
- Deep expertise in 3D Computer Vision / Spatial AI, this is a core requirement for the role.
- Strong understanding of geometry, spatial relationships and scene understanding.
- Experience developing and deploying computer vision and deep learning systems in production.
- Strong Python development skills and expert knowledge of PyTorch.
- Experience with semantic segmentation, object detection, image understanding and modern computer vision architectures.
- Experience designing and training large-scale deep learning models and working with large image datasets.
- Strong mathematical foundations in machine learning and computer vision.
- Ability to bridge research and production engineering, comfortable exploring emerging techniques while remaining focused on building robust, deployable products.
- Strong debugging and problem-solving skills and the ability to work through complex, ambiguous technical challenges.
- A collaborative approach and the ability to work effectively across multidisciplinary engineering teams.
What matters most for this role is genuine depth in 3D / spatial computer vision and the ability to apply that expertise to complex, real-world engineering problems.
We’re particularly interested in someone who is curious about where computer vision and AI are heading, but who also has the practical engineering mindset to turn emerging research into technology that works reliably outside of the lab.
What You Could Be Working On
From the outset, you’ll have the opportunity to contribute to some of our highest-priority R&D initiatives, including:
- 3D construction scene understanding
- Construction semantic segmentation
- Automated BIM understanding and object correspondence
- Spatial reasoning across wearable sensor data
- Embedded AI deployment
- Foundation models for construction understanding
- Perception for wearable AR
WHY JOIN US
- 🚀 Work at the intersection of Spatial AI, 3D Computer Vision, AR and real-world engineering
- 🧠 Solve genuinely difficult perception and scene-understanding problems
- 🥽 Develop AI that ultimately runs through physical, wearable technology – not just software on a screen
- 🏗️ See your work applied to some of the world’s most ambitious construction projects
- 📈 Join a Series B business at an exciting stage of international growth
- 🔬 Work alongside specialists across Computer Vision, AI, Navigation, Embedded Software and Hardware
- 💡 Have meaningful influence over technical architecture and the future direction of our perception technology
- 🌍 Build technology with tangible, real-world impact
If you’re passionate about 3D computer vision and spatial AI, enjoy solving difficult problems at the intersection of research and engineering, and want to see your work move from algorithms into technology being used in the physical world, we’d love to hear from you.
